# AIV lobby selection audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Installed `CrusaderDE.dll` SHA-256:
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Image base: `0x180000000`; VA is base plus RVA. The entry and data path below
was reviewed against the current semantic decompiler export.

Evidence paths below that start with `Findings/AIVPlacement/AivSeries-20260924/`
are original paths **inside** `Findings/AIVPlacement/EVIDENCE.zip`. The readable
summary is `Findings/AIVPlacement/EXPERIMENTS.md`; use
`Restore-Evidence.ps1` to recover a named trace. The former
`CastlePlanner/AIVPlacement_SOFORTSPAWN_FORSCHUNGSSTAND.md` is archived there
as well; the current scope is in `Findings/AIVPlacement/STATUS.md`.

| Native role | RVA / VA | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skirmish player setup and AIV selector source | `0x94350` / `0x180094350` | High for branching; medium for managed lobby mapping |
| Candidate import and mapper write | `0x55320` / `0x180055320` | High for call order; medium for all field semantics |
| Fixed candidate fit | `0x54DE0` / `0x180054DE0` | High |
| Auto candidate and rotation choice | `0x54F60` / `0x180054F60` | High for control flow and thresholds |
| Mapper rotation | `0x56670` / `0x180056670` | High |
| Projected raster scan | `0x57080` / `0x180057080` | High for scan and score flow |
| Tile placement rules | `0x7B060` / `0x18007B060` | Medium for mapper-specific effects |
| Prepare chosen castle | `0x53D00` / `0x180053D00` | High for call order; medium for effects |
| Execute completed castle | `0x55F50` / `0x180055F50` | High for frame sequence |
| Execute one build step | `0x51790` / `0x180051790` | Medium for all constructors |

For this hash, the projected raster validator `0x57080` calls tile rules
`0x7B060` with player ID 0 and mode 0. Its general height limit is 200;
it does not apply the physical moat-construction threshold of 12. The
later `0x51790` mapper-106 path calls moat constructor `0x59730`
(`VA 0x180059730`), whose height branch requires a tile height below 13
for Vanilla construction. ExtraFeatures gates a bypass of that later branch
for AI players when its audited hook is installed and logically enabled;
it does not alter the candidate fit call. Confidence: high for the checked
call/branch paths and the observed Crater Lake trace; remaining constructor
conditions are not modeled by this statement.

The later mapper-105 drawbridge route in `0x51790` calls building
constructor `0x6D580` and drawbridge creator `0x739C0`. The audited
height-failure writer at RVA `0x7870B` follows a mapper-105 comparison
and a maximum-building-height comparison against 12. ExtraFeatures
suppresses this failure for allowed AI players only when its complete
hook transaction is active. Candidate fit still does not apply this
later height gate. Confidence: high for the guarded native branch and
hook contract; medium for a complete offline build outcome.

On 2026-09-23, the Crater Lake `nizar6.aivjson` prebuild trace on this
native hash recorded mapper 106 in frames 15, 65, and 66. Of 1,025
listed moat positions, 1,022 height-layer changes were observed, all
`130 -> 122`; the ExtraFeatures AI hook was active. The trace has complete
frame/provenance metadata and zero capture errors. The paired no-prebuild
start retained complete native fit scores for Nizar and Wolf. These
observations establish the fit/build distinction for this case, not exact
future construction for every projected moat cell.
The same Nizar capture recorded mapper 105 at frame 28: one prepared
drawbridge position, 25 new building-ID cells, and 15 height changes
`130 -> 122`. This is direct layer evidence for this build, not a
guarantee that every footprint cell receives the same height write.
The later complete 2026-09-24 Crater Lake replay joined tile IDs from the
offline projection and native build trace for Nizar `Default 6`, orientation
270 degrees. Mapper 106 projected 1,025 core-footprint tiles; 1,022 unique
tiles received a height write, all within that projection. Mapper 105
projected 25 footprint tiles; all 25 received a building-ID write, with
no observed write outside the footprint. The active ExtraFeatures AI hook
was recorded. Confidence is high for this exact captured path, not for
other AIVs or disabled-hook construction.

`0x94350` scans player IDs in order, resolves a per-player selector, starts
native AIV state, and routes negative selectors to `0x54F60`. Selector `-1`
passes an enabled alternative-rotation flag; `-2` and lower pass disabled.
The function receives an `AivSystem*`, zero-based village slot, and one-byte
flag. Its candidate count comes from the imported specification. The initial
orientation is stored in the village slot and rotated by `0x56670`; subsequent
orientations advance by two in the native eight-step direction field, wrapping
at eight. The caller later reads the chosen variant index, orientation and
placement state. Complete results prepare the layout and, with completed
enemy castles enabled, execute build steps into the mutable map before the
next player. The offline AIV plan alone cannot reconstruct that later state.

The 2026-09-23 follow-up checked the no-prebuild dependency at this same hash.
`0x53D00` imports the chosen AIV, records prepared frames and owner masks, and
derives the start Keep coordinate from the imported Keep marker. The following
`0x94350` start constructor receives the player ID and that coordinate; the
candidate's subsequent frames execute only through the conditional `0x55F50`
path. The fixed-fit chain `0x54DE0` -> `0x57080` -> `0x7B060` reads the live
tile layers and building records, not the prepared AIV frames or owner masks.
For valid AIVs anchored to the same Keep, distinct candidate choices with the
same selected rotation therefore have the same proven start input to the next
fit when prebuild is off. Confidence is high for this direct call/read chain;
constructor side effects outside the audited start footprint remain outside
the offline prediction. With prebuild on, candidate identity determines later
frame writes and cannot be discarded.

`0x54F60` starts at RNG modulo candidate count and increments before the first
visit. It imports and checks every candidate at the initial rotation. The
first full score `999999` returns immediately with state 2. Partial scores
track the first visited fit above 95%, the best sequential score, and the best
percentage. All ties use strict `>` and retain the earlier visited candidate.
If the flag permits, it checks three more rotations in rotation-major order.
Any full fit returns immediately. A partial alternative is considered only if
there was no positive initial score. With no positive initial score it accepts
an alternative at 86% or higher; otherwise no candidate is selected. With a
positive initial score it selects the first above 95%, else the highest
sequential score when greater than 29, else the highest percentage when at
least 91%, else the highest sequential score. Partial selection has state 1.

The installed Script Extender exposes imported AIV and live build-state views,
but no offline query against an unloaded lobby map. `AivSystem` must remain
pointer-based. The local Fixes mod changes some AIV capacities and KEEP3
handling, so it remains part of runtime compatibility review. The owner-aware
reconstruction of tightly neighboring starts is a model assumption supported
by the archived owner-marked wall discrepancy, not yet by a current-hash
runtime capture. The rechecked archive matches 4/145 cases after the owner
fix; unresolved dense-map states are blocked from later-AI lobby predictions
after any earlier start rebuild if the map has cross-owner start-wall adjacency. Serialized walls with
owner zero still require the previous
adjacency-based removal rule; the archived first-player full-fit case would
otherwise become a false partial fit. A current-hash Oracle trace should
resolve this uncertainty. See `Helpers/MapParser/Docs/AIV_PLACEMENT_RULES.md` for the
existing fit and corpus details.

## Completed-castle execution on this hash

At `0x94350` (`VA 0x180094350`), an accepted AI placement reaches
`0x53D00`, then the coupled start-building constructor. Before the loop
advances to the next player ID, it can set the prebuilt-player bit and call
`0x55F50(AivSystem*, playerId, 100)`. The observed native condition is
`(G_1887EE2F8 && (G_1887EE2F4 || (G_188574B90 != 99 && G_1887EE2F0))) ||
specialStartMode || forcedFixedCandidate`. The special-mode flag comes from
the start-path local mode 4 branch; the fixed-candidate flag is set for a
selector above 999. Exact managed provenance of the three globals remains
open, so `advopt_pre_build` alone must not be claimed to cover those modes.

## 2026-09-25 native start preparation and Vanilla control

The installed `CrusaderDE.dll` still hashes to
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
At `0x94350` (VA `0x180094350`), the first player loop removes serialized
AI start groups through `0xC43A0`. In the later construction loop, both
the AI and human branches write one to global `0x1860AD5AC`, the tile
manager's `+0x204E7FC` flag, before calling `0x6D580`. A failed
`0x77E60` validation returns before construction. After success, type 41
dispatches to `0x74DA0`, which tests this flag and calls `0x5D3A0`
before creating the new compound, then clears the flag. This distinguishes
serialized-start removal from the subsequent compound collision cleanup.

`0x5D3A0` samples the type-41 row of its **unrotated** offset tables:
the 7x7 Keep at `(0,0)`, single cells `(2,7)`, `(3,7)`, `(4,7)`,

building ID goes to `0xC4290`, which marks all live records with the same
nonzero manager `+0x304` cleanup link; `0x5D3A0` then sends marked
records to `0xB8310`. No owner or human-player exemption appears in this
cleanup function. The separately rotated offsets in `0x74DA0` govern
**new construction**, not these contact cells. Confidence: high for
static control/data flow, offsets, and the executed linked deletion.

The user independently reproduced the Wolf Keep loss with the same lobby

native cleanup branch has no such filter, while start anchor, facing, and
player order can change contact. The Vanilla reproduction is a user-reported
runtime control; it was not recorded by the detector. The `0xB8310`
transitive fit-layer write bound and all `0x77E60` abort branches remain

## Lobby construction notices (25 September 2026)

The lobby's new geometric practice score is a mod-side estimate, not an
additional native fit rule. The native `0x54F60` choice remains driven by the
unchanged results of `0x57080`/`0x7B060`; `0x55F50` and `0x51790` may then
produce a different construction outcome before the next AI is checked.
Projecting every available AIV at four rotations can show planned fixed-
building overlap and a bounded score deduction, but it does not establish
which plan the random-start selector actually chooses or which buildings
survive sequential construction. Confidence: high for the native ordering and
selector inputs at installed SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`;
the geometric score is explicitly heuristic.

The `0x57080 -> 0x7B060` fit result does not enforce the later moat and
drawbridge construction height limit. The moat mapper 106 reaches the
height check through `0x51790 -> 0x59730`; mapper 105 reaches the
building-height failure path through `0x51790 -> 0x6D580 -> 0x739C0`
and `0x7870B`. These paths apply the height-12 limit at construction,
after preceding AIV frames. The archived Nizar Default 6 trace records
height changes `130 -> 122` during moat and drawbridge frames. Thus a
projected tile whose **initial** map height exceeds 12 does not alone
prove its height at a later frame. Confidence: high for the split between
fit and construction and for the observed trace; unproven for arbitrary
intermediate frame effects. The lobby must require a separate build-time
height proof before declaring a height-related construction risk.

The linked-record start-contact test above describes a **possible**
earlier Keep loss only when the affected candidate and rotation are among
the native selector's possible outcomes. It does not prove actual deletion
or a later fit state. Pairwise projected AIV footprints can at most prove
a **planned** overlap until the sequential construction and cleanup paths
for both candidates are reconstructed. See `Findings/AIVPlacement/STATUS.md`
for the current publication boundary.

## Coop Trail AI upload and lobby castle encoding (21 October 2026)

Managed audit of the installed `Assembly-CSharp.dll`
(`BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`) together with
this native hash. Reproducible with `ilspycmd` on `FRONT_Multiplayer`, `AIVLoader`,
`HUD_IngameMenu` and `CustomisationFileManager`; no native call was changed.

- `FRONT_Multiplayer.StartSkirmishGame` calls `EngineInterface.initMultiplayerGame`,
  `setMultiplayerStartingData` and `InitAIVLoading` (`DLL_ImportAIV(-1, -1, null, 0, 0)`,
  the bank reset), then per AI member `RegisterSkirmishUser` and the castle upload,
  and only afterwards `loadMultiplayerMap`.
- Coop branch (`coopGame` and Coop Trail 1-4): only `AIVLoader.UploadDefaultAIV(lordType,
  playerId)`. Selected castles and `setCustomLordConfig` are skipped. The skirmish branch
  uses `UploadDefaultAIV` when `builtIn || aivs.Count == 0`, the community or historical
  set otherwise when flagged, else `ImportAIV(playerId - 1, index, data, 1)` per
  candidate, followed by `setCustomLordConfig` for a custom AIC.
- `UploadDefaultAIV` imports eight (historical: one) Vanilla sets with custom flag 0.
  Zero-based Lord types follow `AILords` minus one; the Vanilla castle tables end
  before `SK_X1`.
- `MPAIVInfo.encode` writes `0:` (standard) whenever `builtIn || aivs.Count == 0`, and
  `1:`/`2:` for community/historical only with a non-empty candidate list; the lobby
  carries candidate 0 and the AIC only. A client decodes community/historical with an
  empty list, so Vanilla's own skirmish branch would upload standard castles there.
- `MPAIVInfo.Init(type, name)` clears `builtIn` and `builtInLord` for a non-empty name.
- `RestartSkirmishMapInfo.decode(data, customTrailMission: true)` keeps the saved AI
  slots (AIC, candidates, flags, rotation, name, 144x144 portrait) when the original
  map header cannot be resolved. `importMembers` stores -1 for humans and -9999 for
  empty slots. The original map name follows the member table in the restart block.

APIShared's `CoopAiStartImportService` replaces exactly the Coop branch's upload
for planned slots; see `APIShared/docs/THIRD_PARTY_GUIDE.md#coop-trail-ai-start-import`.

# Assassin attack control test [Scope: Mod work, not Vanilla]

The 2026-10-08 search implementation below is historical and superseded by the captured-gate-only simplification on 2026-10-11.

Native hash: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2 (CURRENT.json and installed DLL checked). Full feature audit combines existing Assassin direct-gatehouse/path/execution/capture contracts with 23 complete bodies retained in _inspect/AssassinAttackControlAudit/native-flow.txt. Canonical Fixes 1.25.1 source and current Script Extender APIs were checked; no changes to either project.

## Native contracts [Vanilla facts]

- Assassin-only dispatcher 16CD70 reads current one-based game unit ID from 9302C4. The selected-entry table used by 182B00 supplies this handler. Two incoming data references point to 16CD70; no recorded incoming edge targets the ten-byte prologue interior. Prologue is two five-byte MOV stores, 48895C240848896C2410; Indirect-only continuation is 16CD7A. No competing owner was found in Script Extender, Fixes or current workspace runtimes.
- State 101 uses 188340 then 193DE0 adjacency/facing checks to enter 107. State 107 calls 7EB00 at 16D54D (wall damage 10, building damage 70 or class-specific 6). These paths do not check captured-gate ownership. Gate capture does not replace original building owner.
- Vanilla's completed-obstacle cleanup at 16D573..16D6DA clears unit +3A4, chooses AI state zero when retargeting fails, and resets animation counter +2AC. The old shared guard used only the three fallback fields and omitted the preceding 122800 retarget call; it was not the complete Vanilla completion path. It ran before exactly one original update; it does not skip common housekeeping, touch unrelated unit types or cancel climb states 126..129.
- EAB80 writes shared native flood stamps/queues. It must not be called as a read-only probe from this guard. 1140C0 sends tribes to building EnterCenterTilePositionX/Y (+260/+262), preserving one-based IDs. 196280 publishes individual paths but does not choose Assassin movement state: replacement orders set state 101 only after observing published destination/plan fields.
- 107160 is a read-only vegetation predicate. Read-only mainmod views reuse the existing transition/surface/gate validator and movement/climb costs, with independent snapshot data and no path publication.
- Fixes SmarterSiegeAssassins retargets the siege-assassin tribe after capture; its target policy is not a global state-107 demolition guard. Testmod retains Fixes and current gate-test policies and issues no group command for mixed tribes.

## Test implementation

Testmods/AssassinAttackControlTest, version 0.1.0, host-only EnableMod/ProtectCapturedGates/PreferCastleAccess default true. Only AI Assassins; own/allied captures protected. Walls, two capturable stone gate types, wooden/postern gates and tower types are obstacle targets. Alternative capture goals are valid, unburning enemy stone gatehouses at Vanilla's center destination; ordinary castle access uses valid routes to the target lord/contact neighborhood. The enemy is resolved from current tribe target, siege target, then verified obstacle owner. Unknown targets do not authorize demolition.

APIShared owns the optional permanent update detour. BugfixesAndQoL only publishes a rooted read-only traversal adapter; no new mainmod setting or active attack logic. No version increment was made for this test feature. APIShared remains 0.4.11; an independent parallel change advanced the mainmod to 1.0.178 and was preserved. The mainmod effective APIShared dependency is now 0.4.11 for the new public contract. New interface/guard registration requires all test participants to install the freshly built packages, even if their version labels already match.

One reusable search worker expands at most 4096 nodes/game tick. Exact topology/policy/goals are validated before each continuation and before orders/fallback. Identical per-player/speed snapshots can be shared; obsolete unit identities and corpse/death records are removed. Incomplete/stale searches never count as no route. Pending units remain idle; stopped searches retry through a guarded state-101 transition. Host switch-off restores only still-owned pending contexts. Completed negative proofs must remain current before damage is allowed.

## Verification and evidence limits

Pre-build: 409 new assertions (100 independent directed weighted graph oracles, exact route costs, stale policies/topology, bounded continuation and actual production NativeX64 Indirect/10 ABI, pointer slot and trampoline). Existing Assassin suite: 16253 assertions. Existing movement compatibility suite: 1478 manual/mixed-group assertions, 35 actual NativeX64 detours and production-generator/death guards. Full source compilation against installed assemblies passed in memory, without emitting runtime DLLs. JSON/lifecycle/permanent hook/XAML/CRLF/native hash checks passed. Existing unchanged EditorDirector.gameLocalPlayerID access is separately recognized by shared preflight; no new private Unity access was added.

No in-game acceptance, multiplayer equivalence or live search/snapshot performance has been demonstrated yet. Test logs report queued/completed decisions, protected gate/capturer, actual replacement publication and aggregate search cost. A valid search or issued command alone is not proof of successful physical gate capture or movement.

Build/install evidence: APIShared, BugfixesAndQoL and AssassinAttackControlTest were built and installed using their elevated build.bat drivers. Logs: _inspect/AssassinAttackControlAudit/api-build.log, main-build-final.log and test-build-final.log. Testmod build has no reported warnings/errors; mainmod build has 842 existing source/reference warnings and zero errors, with no warnings in the new feature sources. SHA256 equality was checked for every package file: APIShared 7, mainmod 48, testmod 4 files. Tests include all eight gate-policy publication identity/null-mask transitions. A first testmod driver attempt stopped before runtime build because child Windows PowerShell lacked Get-FileHash; the driver now uses the standard .NET SHA256 implementation and the final run passed.

## Captured-gate-only simplification (2026-10-11)

Native SHA256 remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2. Audit: 16CD70 complete state machine; arrival/obstacle checks 188340/193DE0/193D90; damage 7EB00; completion 122800 and all role-specific selection branches (111330,111620,111D90,111960,111060,111F20,111AF0,110740); movement publication 1946A0/196280; idle behavior 181890 and tribe scheduling 117520/10AA20/122B40. Database function labels are candidate; the field/branch/argument relationships are statically confirmed against the current native image. Ordinary idle is not a guaranteed immediate retarget. Successful route execution and convergence remain gameplay questions.

Production scope: only live AI Assassins in obstacle states 101/107, protecting main/inner stone gatehouses captured by themselves or an ally. In-transit state 101, humans, corpses, climbing, towers/walls/other gates and hostile captures retain Vanilla. Both host switches EnableMod and ProtectCapturedGates default true. No tick worker, graph search, goal enumeration, topology snapshot or movement command remains. Hook execution after startup cleanup has a session-scoped log marker. Protection details are bounded to 16 reports per map, with total count at map end.

APIShared retains RegisterGuard(string, Func<int,bool>) with IdleOnly semantics and adds an explicit AssassinObstacleCompletionMode overload. NativeRetarget clears +3A4, calls 122800 with module+7CC6720, unchanged one-based unit ID and SIGNED r_AIObjectiveRole2 (+2FE), sets state zero only on unsuccessful selection, and resets +2AC. Successful Vanilla-written state/context are preserved. Managed selection exceptions also reset to safe idle before the original update; zeroed target cannot remain in damage state. Original executes exactly once. Retarget uses an ordinary delegate, no second hook. Native hash and the 24-byte entry prefix are validated before registration. The permanent 16CD70 Indirect/10 contract is unchanged.

The unused IAssassinTraversalView, RegisterTraversal/CaptureTraversal/IsTraversalAvailable API and mainmod read-only provider are removed with explicit maintainer breaking-change approval. Only the testmod consumed them; future target/path selection is Vanilla/Fixes owned. Existing weighted mainmod pathfinding and gate/climb policies remain. Canonical current Fixes source excludes own/allied captures in EAB80 and retargets siege-Assassin tribes on capture; no competing 16CD70 hook was found.

Debug versions remain unchanged. Testmod 0.1.1 now requires the current APIShared 0.7.0 for the explicit mode; no hard mainmod dependency remains. Older PreferCastleAccess values no longer activate any code. Public old guard behavior is retained. The historical search tests are removed from active projects; analysis evidence remains.

Pre-install verification: 171 focused tests including the actual production gate predicate, real corpse/control-WORD fields, all states 0..139, disabled/human/capture/transit cases, completion success/failure/exception/legacy behavior, exact actual NativeX64 Indirect detour and pointer/32-bit ID/signed-role ABI. Independent APIShared completion tests also cover preserved objective/state and public overload compatibility. Existing Assassin suite: 16252 assertions; movement suite: 1481 manual/mixed assertions plus 35 actual NativeX64 detours. Source-only memory compilation against the real game assemblies passed for APIShared, mainmod and testmod. The pre-install isolated test executable excludes only the workspace consumer-package target, since the fresh API package does not exist until the driver builds it; the final testmod driver runs with the full package checks.

In-game and multiplayer acceptance remain pending: protection must prevent actual gate damage, native/Fixes retargeting must resume useful orders, and repeated rejected-target churn must be ruled out. The wider 'demolition only as a last resort' requirement is deliberately outside this simplification.
Final review and installation (2026-10-11): rechecked production predicate, session-rooted callbacks/settings, native state-101 arrival and state-107 damage flow, signed second-objective argument, completion failure handling and original-update-once contract against the audit. Native 122800 publishes state 101 on successful selection; 16CD70 state 101 can enter 107 but breaks out before the damage case. Therefore even a reselected protected gate is caught on the next attack update; convergence still requires gameplay evidence. No additional concrete runtime defect was found. The new independent test initially used an unavailable MSTest ThrowsException assertion; it was corrected to the installed ThrowsExactly API before successful checks.

All three elevated build.bat drivers completed successfully and installed their packages. APIShared suites: 102/102 core, 79/79 API (including four new completion tests), 21/21 presets; focused testmod: 171 assertions. Repeated source/installed-API memory compilation passed for APIShared (131 sources), BugfixesAndQoL (361), and the testmod (9). SHA256 equality: all 8 APIShared, 49 mainmod and 4 testmod package files match installed files. Three existing mainmod LobbyModSettings persistence files remain preserved outside package contents. Logs: _inspect/AssassinAttackControlAudit/captured-only-api-build.log, captured-only-main-build.log, captured-only-test-build.log, captured-only-consumer-review.log. Current mainmod version 1.0.184 (parallel changes), APIShared 0.7.0 and testmod 0.1.1 were retained; this simplification introduced no version bump. No in-game acceptance was performed.

## Mainmod integration (2026-10-11)

The successful single-player custom-game session ran 02:24:45.491..02:34:18.196 with eight AI slots and Fixes 1.26.4. Logs show the permanent guard running after startup cleanup and 85 protected updates. Detailed vetoes include P4/gate727 and P7/gate560. P7 unit1760/global186234 was vetoed twice at 02:28:38.865 and 02:28:39.875, then had a published state-101 movement path at 02:28:40.921 (526/495 ->502/474); unit1529/global366879 had a new path at 02:28:41.879. The user observed no attack on the captured gate, subsequent movement and death on the way. Logs do not establish that the next objective was the gate behind a drawbridge, successful arrival, full damage history or global absence of retarget churn: detailed protection reports stop at 16. No Error-level message or guard failure was present in that run. This is a positive testmod acceptance observation, not an in-game acceptance of the integrated package.

BugfixesAndQoL now owns the existing APIShared guard through its own GUID, NativeRetarget mode. New independent Host setting EnableAssassinCapturedGateProtectionFix defaults true, is under Fixes, uses normal SetSetting/SyncHostOnly/preset/reset/search/localization, and combines only with EnableMod. Setting changes are read in the callback; no code patch, teardown or separate pathfinding activation is involved. The live consumer filters unit eligibility before AI/building/alliance lookup and does constant bounded work with no search, queue, collection or movement command. It logs one post-cleanup debug marker per process; unit details and per-map counters are removed. Existing session publishers root and activate/deactivate it. Native initialization failure is isolated using TryInitializePersistentFeature; an unsupported native image never registers the feature.

APIShared review: sole owner, volatile callback publication, static delegate/hook/transaction roots, Indirect/10 actual-backend validation and original update exactly once remain unchanged. Disabled consumers return false and preserve Vanilla. The successful hot path has no managed allocations from this feature; the second checked unit lookup occurs only after a veto and remains the generic API safety boundary. Native objective selection is invoked only for a protected impending attack and can itself perform Vanilla target/path work; no extra consumer search is added. One-time initialization/backend validation is outside the per-unit hot path. Failure logging is process-bounded. No APIShared source or version change was needed.

Current native hash still matches CURRENT.json and the installed DLL. The earlier full feature audit (23 full bodies plus all objective branches/scheduling) remains applicable; the 122800 evidence package was refreshed as integration-retarget-audit.txt. Installed Script Extender is 2.14.1; canonical Fixes Git describes v1.26.4 with a clean source tree. Capture-event tribe retargeting and single-unit guard continue to have distinct ownership; no competing Assassin-update hook exists in the checked sources.

Pre-build integration checks: 171 moved policy/completion/actual NativeX64 ABI assertions; 16256 main Assassin path/source-extracted setting assertions; 79 APIShared tests; shared preset/network tests including new default, stored false, missing old-preset value, client rejection and authoritative host sync without local persistence. The production initializer/property/SetSetting are source-extracted for setting tests. A historical F4930 wrapper comparison was adjusted only for two separately inspected passive diagnostics (extra report context and raw builder-result observation); original order/result/exception/Leave remains exactly compared. Both source and installed APIShared compile checks passed against actual game assemblies. Build and integrated-gameplay acceptance are recorded separately below.

Integration build/install completed through elevated BugfixesAndQoL/build.bat /nopause; log integration-main-build.log ends with exit code 0. The driver's full runtime/native, host/preset, path/movement and integrated 171-assertion checks passed. Version consistency: plugin constant, project AssemblyVersion/FileVersion, AssemblyInfo, source info.json and installed DLL/info all agree on 1.0.185 (assembly 1.0.185.0); remaining 1.0.184 is historical changelog content. APIShared remains 0.7.0. All 49 mainmod package files and 8 APIShared package files match installation by SHA256. Existing mainmod persistence files were preserved. Exact absolute paths were checked before removing only workspace Testmods/AssassinAttackControlTest and installed BepInEx/plugins/AssassinAttackControlTest_Serp. Active policy/native tests, verification and analysis are retained under the mainmod tests and _inspect/AssassinAttackControlAudit. README documents the independent enabled-by-default host feature. Integrated on/off gameplay acceptance remains pending and must not be inferred from the testmod run.

# Assassin direct gatehouse climb: native audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Audit date: 2026-10-07. Installed CrusaderDE.dll SHA-256:
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
CURRENT.json and DATABASE_INFO.json identify this same binary. Complete function
pseudocode, caller/callee lists and disassembly from the installed binary are
preserved in `_inspect/AssassinGateClimb/0x<RVA>.txt`.

## Confirmed static result

Vanilla's physical Assassin climb implementation supports gatehouse roof tiles.
Its special path search and path reconstruction nevertheless reject a climb
edge when either endpoint has a nonzero building ID. Gatehouse roofs have both
the wall flag and a building ID. Thus a freestanding gatehouse has no direct
Assassin climb edge in the vanilla special path graph. An ordinary movement
connection through an adjoining wall can bypass this restriction. This explains
why wall-connected access can work without proving any particular rare observed
climb was direct. No controlled game run has yet established that observation.

Function names classified as candidate in the semantic database remain candidate
names. The conditions below are confirmed static instructions for this hash;
runtime behavior of the proposed change remains untested.

## Gatehouse tile construction and topology

- Building dispatcher 0x6D580 selects 0x74240 for type 45 and 0x74080 for type 46.
  Both constructors enumerate the footprint through 0x69850, raise the tile
  height by 90, set tile property IsWall (0x100), assign the owner, and write the
  allocated 1-based building ID into the building grid. They initialize building
  path topology through 0xD8510 and update tiles through 0x725E0.
- Grid building IDs reside at RVA 0x4B6AA50, wall/property grid at 0x48F71B0,
  height grid at 0x4DDD350 and movement direction grid at 0x51890D0. These are
  separate grids. Removing an IsBuilding flag does not remove a building ID.
- Load/topology flow 0x71670 -> 0xC8380 -> 0xB9510 preserves IsWall on the complete
  type 45/46 footprint and clears IsBuilding (0x400). It does not clear roof
  building IDs. Type 47 follows a separate high-wall branch and is outside scope.
- 0xC5040 and 0x725E0 call 0xD8CE0 to update gate passage direction bits according
  to gate orientation/state, adjacent surface legality and height difference.
  These ordinary movement connections must remain authoritative.

## Human target recognition and synchronized movement

- Input flow DLL_TroopSelection / DLL_RunTick -> 0x8C5F0, with target resolution
  0x79B90 -> 0x90830, distinguishes buildings from ground and walls.
- In 0x8C5F0, selected-Assassin predicate 0x196870 and the building-type switch
  already permit gate types 45/46 to enter the movement branch when the
  Assassin reachability query 0xE2CA0 succeeds. An unsuccessful query leaves
  building attack handling available. This is a reachability restriction, not
  absence of all gatehouse command handling.
- 0xB70C0 probes perimeter attack reachability; 0xB72C0 is a separate wall attack
  probe. They must not be replaced with unconditional climb acceptance.
- Ground move staging 0x195E30 emits Chore 17. Its consumer 0x10AE0 -> 0x196100
  -> 0x11B520 issues group movement. 0x199C30 handles separate command/sound
  bookkeeping and is not the movement consumer. Input release must not be
  replaced by an unsynchronized second command.
- 0xE2CA0 may return immediately for a shared path component or consult its pair
  cache; its forced query path uses 0xD9C40. Cursor and group queries therefore
  need the same climb-edge eligibility as actual route creation.

## AI and route generation

- AI tribe processing 0x117520 -> 0x10AA20, case 0x41A, already calls 0x1140C0.
  This gate-target action queries 0xEAB80 at increasing search budgets, resets
  tribe members through command 3 in 0x11E960 and moves the tribe to gatehouse
  coordinates through 0x11B520. Target search already recognizes live, nonburning
  enemy gatehouses of types 45/46; it is not proof of a realizable climb route.
- 0x117820 identifies an Assassin-only tribe. 0x11B520 then builds a reverse
  Assassin distance field through 0xD9C40 before distributing per-unit movement
  through 0x196280. Mixed groups use ordinary path constraints.
- 0x196280 -> 0xF4930 creates/reconstructs a per-unit route. 0xD9C40 callers also
  include 0xE2CA0 and 0x123090. Negative target coordinates request a flood field;
  the flood's zero return does not necessarily mean no useful field was built.
- 0xD9C40 accepts an ordinary direction-bit edge first. Its extra climb branch
  requires a cardinal direction, permitted target surface (mask 0x4A5014B1 or
  the vanilla vegetation exception 0x107160), zero source AND target building
  IDs, and IsWall at one or both endpoints. This is the direct gatehouse blocker.
- 0xE1640 reconstruction mode 3 repeats cardinal/zero-ID/wall constraints when
  ordinary direction bits do not connect the pair. Relaxing the search alone
  cannot produce a consistent usable path. Other reconstruction modes, ladder
  logic, search limits, stamp ownership and packed path semantics remain intact.

## Physical step, animation and completion

- Simulation 0x182B00 -> 0x1855A0 consumes low-first packed direction nibbles.
  Existing Assassin states 126..129 suspend ordinary movement stepping.
- For a new step, 0x1855A0 calls 0xDCE60 then 0xDCD60. The Assassin branch of
  0xDCE60 accepts ordinary direction connections first, otherwise validates the
  target surface and IsWall. Unlike the path search, it has no zero-building-ID
  requirement. Unit type 73 enters ascending state 126 or descending state 128;
  height difference, facing and animation/progress fields are initialized there.
  Other movement profiles and ladder branch are separate and outside scope.
- Assassin state dispatcher 0x16CD70 progresses 126 -> 127 and 128 -> 129,
  updates climb animation/progress, then resumes ordinary state 101.
  0x180A80 finalizes next-tile coordinates and actual height with ordinary
  occupancy remove/add helpers. 0x188340 is the normal movement-arrival test.
- Ordinary gate interaction/capture and combat remain vanilla. Merely setting
  movement or attack context is not evidence that states 126/127 occurred.
  A runtime test must observe command, route, physical climb state and arrival.

## Workspace and Fixes compatibility [mod integration]

- BugfixesAndQoL AssassinPathfindingRuntime owns the 0xD9C40 function replacement.
  AssassinPathReconstructionPatch owns the 0xE19D8 / 0xE19F9 reconstruction guards.
  Its current reservation policy permits nonzero IDs only when the endpoint's
  ordinary movement mask is nonzero. It is not a gatehouse-specific contract.
- AssassinSelectionAdapters own selection call adapters at 0x8D724, 0x8E2B8,
  0x8E550, 0x8F325, 0xB7161 and 0xB7321. The Script Extender owns predicate
  0x196870. Positive original results remain authoritative; competing hooks at
  any of these owned addresses are unacceptable.
- AssassinClimbRuntime and AssassinClimbCancellationRuntime govern existing
  player climb settings and stop/cancel semantics. A gatehouse experiment must
  respect those settings and cannot reset active climb states independently.
- Canonical external Fixes source was checked first. SmarterSiegeAssassins hooks
  gate target filtering at 0xEAD8C and departure at 0xEACC3; the optional non-siege
  target filter and capture handler affect later AI targeting. Fixes preserves
  live/type/fire eligibility and does not remove the D9C40 zero-ID climb rule.
  A testmod must preserve Fixes' captured-gate/ally decisions, not replace its
  complete gate selection action.

## Shared implementation decision (2026-10-07) [mod integration]

The user authorized central ownership in APIShared. AssassinPathAPI owns the
D9C40 detour and all four building-ID guard adapters. BugfixesAndQoL registers
its weighted builder and consumes the same gate endpoint rule. The experiment
does not replace human command dispatch or Fixes AI target selection. Physical
climbing remains Vanilla. Runtime gameplay acceptance remains pending.

Audited spans: D9C40 NativeX64 Indirect-only / 10 bytes; X64InlineHook D9F0C /16,
D9F1C /15, E19D8 /18, E19F9 /23. Complete containing functions and cross-function
direct edges were checked for interior incoming branches. Source-linked native
tests execute the productive assembler, decode it completely, validate actual
installed RedBird displacement and detour pointer-slot contracts, and exercise
active/inactive gate eligibility. See `_inspect/AssassinGateClimb`.

## First human acceptance (2026-10-07) [mod integration]

18:32:20-18:36:50 editor run with both testmods, weighted improvement and Fixes 1.25.1: seven completed ascents and two descent sequences; user confirms commands worked. Cursor, formation and physical climb code remain unchanged in the subsequent gate-safety step. This confirms the human experiment, not yet all AI, switches or mainmod regressions. See ENEMY_GATE_ASSASSINS.md for the shared classifier and conservative distance-field guard.
## Coordinated review and installation completed (2026-10-07) [mod integration]

After the parallel APIShared work finished, the installed APIShared was verified current (package/install SHA256 equality and new public contract present); no redundant APIShared build was needed. The final review also required a weighted diagnostic climb endpoint to match the exact gate responsible for the blocked edge, rather than a neighboring gate. Actual diagnostic runtime tests now pass 46 assertions. The main movement test fixture was adapted to the parallel UnitAccess.IsReallyAlive addition (enum alias and low-word death-marker field); production UnitAccess was preserved.

All pre-build Native/Interop, compatibility, JSON, Lifecycle, permanent-hook, XAML and CRLF checks passed. Independent Assassin tests: 15,862 assertions; Gate tests: 9,900; installed RedBird Assassin execution tests: 1,396. The full BugfixesAndQoL build driver and all its regression suites completed successfully, with zero errors and the existing MSB3277 assembly-binding warning. EnemyGatePathfindingTest build.bat completed with zero warnings/errors. Both drivers installed successfully. Installed/local package hashes match for APIShared, BugfixesAndQoL and EnemyGatePathfindingTest; evidence: _inspect/EnemyGateBuildingContextAudit/transition-installed-hashes.json. Successful build logs: transition-main-build-complete.log and transition-gate-build-complete.log in the same directory. Earlier failed-attempt logs remain historical evidence.

AssassinGatehouseClimbTest is unchanged and needs no rebuild. Versions and README files remain unchanged. No new native hooks or changes to cursor, formation or physical climb execution were introduced. In-game acceptance remains pending: Assassin commands to the roof and behind open/closed enemy gates, ordinary soldiers denied the ground passage, improvement enabled/disabled, and AI behavior at the same setup. Bridges remain outside this acceptance. Native-only historical mask overlaps are not retroactively marked resolved.

## Exact weighted single-unit route publication (2026-10-07) [mod integration]

Native reference hash: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
E1640 reconstructs from step distances, with a mutable best distance inside its direction loop.
For target-first nodes T(1,1,d4),R(2,1,d3),P(2,2,d2),S(1,2,d1), it can accept R at direction 2,
then S at direction 4 against the already reduced distance 3. This replaces the cheap
S->P->R->T entrance route with a costly S->T climb. Weighted parents and tick costs
are not represented by the published unit-step distances. This is a confirmed static
counterexample, not yet causal proof of the user's particular gameplay run.

APIShared's existing F4930 owner now opens a synchronous, thread-local single-unit
handoff. Bugfixes stages a copied exact low-nibble-first forward direction sequence;
F4930 still executes once, then its checked output buffer receives the prepared bytes
before the 196280 consumer latches length/cursor/state. Successful staging retains the
original D9C40 field/result until the outer builder publishes. Failure inside a unit
frame preserves native data. Flood/continuation calls never stage; standalone queries
retain the checked stamp/distance publication path. Nested builders shadow all outer
frames, including unqualified/manual-probe frames. Delegates live only in the synchronous
frame, whose Leave restores its predecessor in finally; native hook roots remain permanent.

Existing hash-bound data contracts (no additional hook, fixed RVA, AOB or executable write):
- Path manager at module+60AD660: source int32 +8/+C, destination int32 +10/+14;
  Assassin flag int32 +88, moat flag +84, later alternate-builder flag +94.
  Exact publication requires Assassin enabled and the other two flags zero.
- F4930/E1640/E4E90/196280 prove output pointer +155F60, direction-count int32 +155F68.
- Unit manager module+67E8400: buffer +B4FE78 + one-based unitId*1000, capacity
  1000 bytes/2000 directions. Buffer arithmetic derives the ID and checks it against
  UnitAccess, type, true life, Global-ID, control player and native movement start.
- Existing grid bases: connections 51890D0, direction masks 312620, row table 402FF2C,
  heights 4DDD350, surfaces 48F71B0, building IDs 4B6AA50. Physical DCE60 accepts
  source-forward OR destination-reverse before climbing. E1640 tests its own
  target-to-predecessor connection, so reconstruction capability is checked separately.

All addresses derive from the canonical installed-hash disassembly and the existing
shared command layout validator. Fixed layouts have no independent semantic fallback;
search scope is the supported installed module only. Unknown hashes retain the existing
fail-closed feature initialization. F4930 hook resolution/backend remain unchanged;
its existing section-bounded function signature fallback and displacement checks apply.
On native updates re-audit field layout, buffer ownership, nibble reversal, movement-start
selection, alternate builders and the terminal 196280 consumer before permitting publication.
No new Assembly-CSharp access. Fixes gate targeting and Script Extender selection ownership
remain unchanged; the existing soft dependency loads the mainmod after Fixes.

Regression sources compile the productive handoff, encoder, and actual shared builder/
publication methods. Tests cover the expensive reconstruction shortcut, exact buffer bytes,
length, ID reuse, changed policy/pointer, nested frames and native exceptions. Physical
walking/climbing and open owned/captured gate roof acceptance still require an in-game run.
README files and versions remain unchanged during that acceptance.

Validation completed 2026-10-07:
- 15,890 Assassin A*/Dijkstra, physical-transition and exact-publication assertions passed.
- 1,396 source-linked Assassin checks passed on the installed NativeX64 backend.
- Actual F4930 wrapper/publication methods compiled in an isolated memory fixture:
  exact entrance bytes/count, changed identity/policy/buffer and native exceptions passed.
- Shared source/API visibility, JSON, lifecycle, permanent-hook, XAML, CRLF, UnitAccess
  and Fixes compatibility preflights passed; existing native command/moat suites passed.
- APIShared public API regression now permits only the audited context parameter of
  TryStageWeightedRoute in addition to the existing native builder bridge exceptions.
- Elevated direct build.bat drivers completed for APIShared and BugfixesAndQoL.
  The first APIShared driver stopped in its public API test before runtime build;
  the corrected test passed before the successful driver retry.
- Installed standalone APIShared SHA-256:
  A1B08496BEE16EDCACB66B657BD342168F6B74B7F0508BF7F0ABC02F964A2DB1.
- Installed standalone BugfixesAndQoL SHA-256:
  1041E2AFFD6B90C2E3A33774B02E58F9F5EE64F7F4B1162CB2AB7C0FFF1799DE.
  Both match their local package DLLs. Build logs: _inspect/AssassinGateClimb/
  exact-route-APIShared-build-retry.log and exact-route-BugfixesAndQoL-build.log.
- No in-game acceptance claimed. Test roof orders on both gate sizes, owned/captured
  open gates and different approach sides, with Improved Pathfinding on/off.

## Assassin request-index life filter, 2026-10-08

The weighted request index now uses APIShared.UnitAccess.IsReallyAlive rather than AliveState alone. The confirmed low-word death marker at GameUnit+0x29C excludes death-animation/corpse records that remain IsAlive; the unrelated upper word is ignored. Such records previously could create false player/control-player ambiguity or inflate the slowest movement delay when sharing a coordinate with a live Assassin. No native hook, path-edge eligibility or route-publication contract changes.

Regression tests compile and execute the actual BuildRequestIndex, its request record and the actual reference-view life predicate. Cases cover live units mixed with foreign/same-player corpses, corpse-only coordinates, deleted/empty slots, nonzero upper word with zero death marker, preserved slowest live speed and preserved ambiguity between living players. The Assassin suite passes 15,892 assertions. This is automated evidence; no new gameplay acceptance is claimed.

## Weighted-route validation and request cost, 2026-10-08

The complete feature audit above still applies to the unchanged installed native hash.
Search/physical walking accepts the source forward connection OR the destination
reverse connection; E1640's reconstruction connectivity is checked separately.
F4930 capture and terminal 196280 consumption remain under their existing ownership.
Script Extender v2.13.1 retains its selection override, Fixes v1.25.1 its targeting
decisions; no hook sites/backends, movement costs, neighbor order, heap ordering or
search budgets changed. Published hooks remain permanently rooted and installed.

E1640 mutates its comparison distance within the eight-direction loop. For the
target-first route T=11(d4), R=12(d3), P=22(d2), S=21(d1), width 10, it first
accepts R and reduces the comparison from 4 to 3. S can then pass `distance >=
comparison-2 && distance < comparison`, even though S lies three route steps behind
T. Testing only one/two earlier steps misses this candidate. The conservative field
validator now examines every adjacent node with smaller stamped distance: at most
eight neighbor probes per route node, no pairwise route scan. The regression rejects
forbidden S->T before any replacement field is written. This proves the native
reconstruction counterexample, not a new observed gameplay failure.

The synchronous F4930 frame optionally provides the already bound unit's full control
word and current speed. The profile proof uses manager/buffer assignment, one-based
unit ID, live/type/Global-ID, actual native movement start, start/target, current full
control word and speed, path flags/counters and capacity. Moving units use the native
next-tile start when appropriate. Unknown/invalid/nested-shadow contexts provide no
profile. Ownership is restricted to the registered weighted builder. Gate-mask
queries still require the complete control word in 1..8; without a mask the existing
low-byte behavior is retained. Unbound queries retain the existing command index.
Both added unit fields are public in the installed genuine SHCDESE metadata:
`r_CurrentSpeed : UInt16`, `N00000569 : Byte`. No new Assembly-CSharp member is used.

Each A* resolves its suffix dictionary once. Exact staging rejects unqualified
contexts before route/encoding/delegate allocations; C# delegate captures are in a
separate qualified method to avoid method-entry closure allocation. A command's
immutable cached route retains its packed bytes and bound validator delegate.
The delegate rechecks current map epoch, settings, climbing, gate policy, physical
transitions, costs and direct-gate state every time; no validation result is cached.
APIShared still clones bytes at its public boundary and performs all final unit,
buffer, context and route checks before writing. Direction encoding and cached-route
validation share a static lookup with explicit invalid/row-wrap rejection.

Final validation and packed publication are now included in command publication and
total-request phase timing. The per-frame completion callback preserves nested
isolation, reports publication failures and cannot change the result if measurement
code throws. No per-unit log or cross-command route cache was added.

Production-method correctness, load measurements, methodology and limitations are
documented in `_inspect/AssassinPerf/RESULTS.md`, with raw CSVs and retained preflight
logs in that directory. The repaired EnemyGatePathfindingTest source references point
at APIShared's UnitCommandPathRuntime; its complete suite passes 9,900 assertions.
Automated evidence covers Dijkstra agreement, cache bounds, cheap entrance/faster
climb/disabled climb, moving units, profile changes/ID reuse/invalid full player,
nested frames, fallback and current installed NativeX64 contracts. Offline timings
exclude real native Vanilla work and do not establish game performance. User reports
that the earlier roof fix worked; this optimization still needs game acceptance on
owned/captured open gates, both gate sizes and approach sides. README/version unchanged.

Final comparison against Git f57dfdb02 and 8fe105a11 checks unchanged native fallback,
physical/cost/cache validation, heap, native field publication and F4930 wrapper
contracts as normalized C# syntax. The A* body differs only in the once-per-search
suffix lookup. Accumulated command node/heap counters are now 64-bit: 10,000 searches
over sufficiently large reachable regions could overflow the previous diagnostic
Int32 sums. Per-search counters, budgets and route selection stay unchanged; the
overflow regression exercises the actual accumulator methods.

### Performance diagnostics default off (2026-10-08 follow-up) [mod integration]

BugfixesAndQoL now uses the compile-time `PerformanceDiagnosticsEnabled=false`
switch independently of gameplay and testmod policy observers. Disabled active
path methods contain no clock/statistics calls in the compiled IL. Exact-route
staging does not create a measurement callback; APIShared clocks publication only
when such a callback was supplied. Native contracts, original builder invocation,
search budget, route edge counts used by cache validation and live final checks
remain unchanged. Both switch states pass the source-linked Dijkstra, publication
and prior Git contract regressions (16,229 assertions). Detailed measurements and
limitations are recorded in `_inspect/AssassinPerf/RESULTS.md` and the diagnostic
switch CSV. No new game acceptance or measured native Vanilla timing is claimed.
## Main-mod integration, 2026-10-08 [mod integration]

BugfixesAndQoL 1.0.177 now owns the existing APIShared gatehouse activation rule through its PluginGuid. EnableAssassinGatehouseClimbFix is a SyncHostOnly setting in Fixes, initialized and reset to true. Its effective flag is EnableMod && EnableAssassinGatehouseClimbFix. Native initialization and existing settings publishers call the same isolated activation method. APIShared retains all hook ownership; disabling changes data only and does not abort active physical climb states. No new native/managed hook, unit scan, coroutine or teardown is introduced. Existing weighted-route cache keys and publication validators include the gatehouse flag.

The standalone testmod's tick/unit observation is intentionally not carried into production. The preflight now checks the integrated host contract, locales, UI section, installed public setting API and permanent shared hook ownership without requiring the removed testmod. Native audit artifacts and shared execution tests remain in _inspect/AssassinGateClimb.

Automated evidence: 1,396 actual RedBird native execution checks; 16,231 Assassin path assertions including the production activation method extracted and executed for native readiness, both switches, owner and reactivation. Host/preset regressions cover default true, preserved stored false, missing-key migration, client lock and host synchronization; production reset/default/SyncHostOnly contracts are checked statically. README updated. Historical 1.0.176 test results remain unchanged; all active main-mod version declarations and the raid preflight version check are 1.0.177.

Previous successful standalone gameplay observations are retained above; no new integrated gameplay or real multiplayer acceptance is inferred. Remaining gameplay checks: human roof commands and AI on standalone small/large gatehouses, adjoining walls, occupied roofs, ordinary building attacks, improved pathfinding on/off, per-player climbing bans, host toggle/main switch, active climb during toggle, save/load and Fixes enabled. An active climb must finish through Vanilla after disabling; subsequent queries use the disabled endpoint rule.

Integration installation completed: elevated direct build.bat /nopause passed all driver regressions with zero errors. Installed assembly 1.0.177.0 and all 48 package files match local hashes. The verified workspace AssassinGatehouseClimbTest directory was removed; its installed plugin directory was already absent. Installed/local APIShared and its hooks were not rebuilt or changed by this integration. Build evidence: _inspect/AssassinGateClimb/integration-build-final.log.

## 2026-10-14: Assassin descent ownership and height review

The functional closed-gate descent guard now belongs to EnableAssassinGatehouseClimbFix, independently of EnableEnemyGatePathfindingFix. APIShared remains the sole owner of 0x185D55 (20 bytes). Sources: BugfixesAndQoL/src/Assassins/AssassinGatehouseDescentFeature.cs, AssassinGateDescentRuntime.cs and AssassinGateDescentRule.cs. Gate diagnosis only attaches optional observers; detaching them cannot disable descent. No new hooks or API contracts.

The live guard validates unit/global ID, full control WORD, exact native pointer and current gate/global/owner/capturer identity before and after transition classification. No gate-policy snapshot permission is substituted. All four settings combinations, session changes and observer detach are covered by the production feature harness (64 assertions together with reader fixtures).

Native height review: DCE60 initializes grid-height difference; 16CD70 consumes descent progress and commits the destination through 180A80. 184FD0 independently adds the roof/render offset and climb progress. Executing the installed 184FD0 in an isolated memory fixture demonstrates that a wall/building offset of 40 is separate from the grid-height difference. This is NOT yet proof of the actual reported visual defect: the earlier logs lack those raw heights. No speculative coordinate/height correction was applied. Existing movement observations now include world coordinates, base height, render offset, climb height and progress. Logical destination changes must not be undone merely to alter animation.

Validation: full 60 search/climb and 21 planning/output native audit retained; gate suite 157368 assertions, native adapter register/flags tests, copied native height reader, runtime preflight and shared-boundary checks passed. Installed public field layout validated for B6/B8/410/414 and full control WORD at 92h. Interop fields 410/414 are DWORD storage; native audited instructions consume their signed low WORDs. # Assassin route reconstruction failure and full-map repair [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native hash `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2` (installed DLL, 2026-10-20).
Evidence: disassembly of the listed functions plus a runtime replay of the descent on the live field
(BugfixesAndQoL DEVDIAG, 8-lord save) and an executed copy of E1640 in an isolated fixture.

## Flow (confirmed)

- `0xF4930` (per-unit route builder): when path manager `+0x88 != 0` (Assassin profile) the field comes
  from `0xD9C40` (or `0xDA590`/`0xDAAC0` on the `+0x80` branch); `0xF4B5A` then calls
  `0xE1640(manager, startX, startY, targetX, targetY, mode)` with mode 3. Otherwise mode is
  `(+0x84 != 0) + 1`. `0xE32B0` uses mode 0; F4930's second call (when `+0x94 != 0`) mode 1.
- `0xE1640` descends from the target tile to the start tile. A neighbor qualifies when its stamp
  equals the target's stamp and its distance is in `[best - 2, best)`. Mode 3 (`0xE19BB`..`0xE1A12`):
  ordinary edge = `conn[current] & mask[dir]` (`0xE19C0`); otherwise only a cardinal climb with
  building-ID rules (`0xE19D8`, `0xE19F9`) and a wall bit (`0x100`) on either tile.
- No qualifying neighbor: `++manager+0x78`, then `0xDAA50` (D86F0 over all 320800 tiles, ~9–10 ms),
  `0xE49D0(manager, 1)`, `0xC3E50`, `0xDE6A0`; about 19 ms per failure. The output stays empty.
- `0xD9C40` expands u -> v by `conn[u] & mask[dir]` (`0xD9EA6`): the start-side tile's bit. The
  physical step `0xDCE60` accepts either endpoint's bit (see ASSASSIN_DIRECT_GATEHOUSE_CLIMB.md).

## Inconsistency (confirmed by runtime replay)

Across a one-way ordinary connection the field contains the edge, but mode 3 rejects it because it
tests the target-side tile's bit back toward the start. Observed case: Assassins standing in their own
gatehouse (building with tile flag `0x10000000`) and leaving over its drawbridge; the drawbridge tile
lacks the bit back toward the gatehouse. All 63 in-game failures of one run had exactly this shape
(drawbridge buildings 382/675/831), every member of an AI Assassin group failing in the same tick.

Counts per 60 s on `test_8lordsmiddle` (PerfFixTest native counter `manager+0x78`):
Script Extender only 10; BugfixesAndQoL with direct gatehouse climbing 112 (the AI then sends
Assassin groups out of their gatehouse far more often); same with the APIShared rule below 3.

## Correction (APIShared `AssassinPathAPI`, site 0xE19C0/14) [mod integration]

While policy flag 1 (weighted reconstruction) or 2 (direct gatehouse climbing) is set, mode 3 also
accepts `conn[neighbor] & mask[(dir + 4) & 7]`, i.e. exactly the edge D9C40 used. Stamp/distance checks,
climb rules, other modes and the repair path are unchanged. Executed fixture: Vanilla fails with the
four repair calls; with the rule the route is reconstructed (packed directions verified); a step
without either bit still fails; mode 1 is unaffected.

# Weighted Assassin search cost after loading (2026-10-23) [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native hash `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2` (installed DLL, verified 2026-10-23).
Evidence: decompiled `0xD9C40` (baseline database), BugfixesAndQoL DEVDIAG request counters and
per-search lines on `test_stresstest4.sav` (8 AI lords, largest map), runs L2BFQD–L5BFQD.

## Native builder `0xD9C40` (confirmed by pseudocode)

- Breadth-first search over the native queue (`manager+0x155F3C/+0x155F44`, ring of 0x4E520 entries).
- Returns 1 when the target tile is dequeued; 0 when the queue index reaches `param_6` (node limit),
  when the dequeued tile id exceeds 0x4E51F, or when the dequeued distance exceeds **800**
  (`*(short*)(0x5225B10 + 2*tile) > 800`). Vanilla therefore never accepts a route deeper than 800 steps.
- Edge u -> v: `conn[u] & mask[dir]` (`0x51890D0`, `0x312620`); otherwise only the even-direction
  climb fallback with `(flags[v] & 0x4A5014B1) == 0` (or special flag 0x1000 accepted by `0x107160`),
  building layer `0x4B6AA50` zero on **both** tiles, and the wall bit 0x100 on either tile.
- Callers: `0xE2CA0` (PCL-pair reachability, 400000 nodes), `0xF4930` (per-unit route), `0x11B520`
  (Assassin group order), `0x123090`.

## Observed load pattern (runtime evidence)

- In the first ~1.5 s after "mission ready", one AI Assassin group (player 5, tribe 4327, all units on
  tile 499,207) received ~100 `AttackBuilding` target commands. Vanilla's builder returned 0 for almost
  all of them (`native=0`): the start tile is a building/reserved climb endpoint that the native climb
  fallback rejects. BugfixesAndQoL's weighted search (reserved/direct-gatehouse endpoints allowed)
  found ~40 routes (13,000–43,000 expanded nodes, ~10 ms each).
- 15 targets were unreachable for the weighted search as well. Each search expanded exactly 243,362
  nodes (the whole start component) for ~70 ms: about 70 % of the ~1.5 s simulation stall.
- A reversed-edge search from those targets (same edge predicate) visited only 1–11 tiles; for every
  reachable target it visited ~244,000 tiles and met the start. No contradiction to the A* result.

## Consequences in BugfixesAndQoL (managed only, no native change) [mod integration]

- `ProvesTargetUnreachable`: bounded (512 tiles) reversed-edge proof before the A* and existence
  searches; skipped when Vanilla's builder already reached the target. Exactly the forward predicates,
  so a proof only replaces a search that would return "no route" anyway.
- Four-ary heap with packed (estimate, cost) key; identical pop order (unique insertion orders).
- Host settings split: `EnableImprovedAssassinPathfinding` (human players, climb button) and
  `EnableImprovedAssassinPathfindingAI` (AI lords), both on by default.

# Pause and zoom automation boundaries [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Static audit 2026-10-20. Installed native SHA-256 FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2 and managed SHA-256 BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789 match CURRENT.json / DATABASE_INFO.json. Source-based multiplayer/zoom integration observations refer to the current workspace, not an assertion that its mods are installed.

## Native pause flow

- Confirmed export `DLL_GameAction`, RVA 0x81870: action 0x418 (the real managed `GameActionCommand.Game_Paused`) writes signed Int32 `value` to VA 0x18366A0F8 and returns 0. The `structureID` and `value2` parameters are not used by this branch. Managed `EngineInterface.GameAction` owns the engine lock; its return is not a pause success signal.
- Native initialization at RVA 0x87D10 resets this global to 0. RVA 0x71670 writes -1 for an initialization-related pass. Internal function names remain candidate confidence; these writes are directly present in the hash-matched decompiler export. Read normal 0/1 pause states only in a ready gameplay session.
- The complete enclosing updater at RVA 0xCDE60 was inspected, including network wait/error branches, frame-skip and pause gates. Native time/update work requires pause == 0; the main simulation body requires the supplied skip byte == 0 and pause < 1, and its transient negative pause path normalizes to 0. A positive pause skips that body without stopping all preparation/presentation work. Network loading/acknowledgement states can independently prevent progress.
- Confirmed export `DLL_RunTick`, RVA 0x86680, encloses the update/presentation chain. Candidate-named output builder RVA 0x19D960 copies the native pause into PlayState, later consumed as `lastGameState.game_paused`. Therefore the published managed snapshot may lag a direct native read.
- All 15 named-global references in the current semantic decompiler export were checked: RVA 0x2230, 0x25E0, 0x87D0, 0x71670, 0x81870, 0x87D10, 0x89D10, 0x89F40, 0x8BD60, 0x90830, 0x90CD0, three references in 0xCDE60 and the output builder at 0x19D960. The other readers gate local input/counters or save/load-related handling; they do not create a second public pause command. This is a named-global audit, not a claim to exhaust aliased memory accesses.
- Script Extender `IsLocalPaused` reads the Int32 at its resolved `GamePausedVA` and compares against 1. `SetLocalPaused` is a raw write and explicitly does not synchronize multiplayer. `Director.Paused` is a separate managed flag: `SetPausedState(true)` refuses multiplayer; setting it false does not clear the native pause.

## Managed requests and camera

Vanilla's non-MP pause key sends Game_Paused with `(1,1)` or `(0,0)`. BugfixesAndQoL queues pause as a synchronized Chore, but sends unpause through the direct transport so a stopped simulation can resume. Existing authorization, active-human sender validation, main-thread dispatch and sender-local application remain required. Requests are currently private implementation methods, not a public automation API. CastlePlanner's existing GameAction Pre observer can veto unpause during preview.

Public `PerfectPixelWithZoom.adjustZoom(float,bool)` changes the step position, clamps/wraps it and starts Unity-time interpolation. Positive values zoom in. It contains no pause check; input-side pause gates live in KeyManager/CameraControls2D. Public getters expose actual scale and interpolation completion. `SetZoomImmediate(float)` clamps/applies scale but neither synchronizes `zoomPos` nor cancels in-flight interpolation. BugfixesAndQoL's existing zoom hooks normalize scale to resolution and alter step boundaries; consumers should call the public methods and observe the result.

Full public-call examples, scheduling requirements and acceptance scenarios: [AutomatisierungTest.md](../../../../../AutomatisierungTest.md). Pause/zoom live acceptance is not claimed; only the earlier 2026-10-19 AutoLoadSave run has live evidence.

# Bedouin healer target selection [Scope: Vanilla]

Native build: `CrusaderDE.dll` SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`, image base `0x180000000`. Static findings below use the semantic decompiler and entry disassembly. Function names remain `candidate` until live confirmation.

- `FUN_1800d1ad0` (RVA `0xD1AD0`) periodically calls `FUN_180181340` with the unit-manager pointer in RCX and player ID 0–8 in EDX. Both direct call sites target the function entry at RVA `0x181340`.
- `FUN_180181340` (RVA `0x181340`) rebuilds each player's unit-ID (`short[10000]`) and global-ID (`int[10000]`) candidate arrays. It scans game IDs 1 through `r_NextUnitId - 1`, requires `AliveState == 2`, native field `GameUnit + 0x29C == 0`, same alliance and nonzero native field `GameUnit + 0x2A0`. Eight type IDs are explicitly skipped: 39/40/41 (Catapult/Trebuchet/Mangonel), 58/59/60/61 (Siege Tower/Ram/Portable Shield/Ballista), and 77 (Arab Ballista). The active list also depends on the native player-owner field at `GameUnit + 0x92` and an alternate game flag. The exact civilian exclusion among these gates is not yet individually proven.
- `FUN_18018de10` (RVA `0x18DE10`) is called only by the Bedouin healer updater `FUN_180174100` (RVA `0x174100`). It reads the above candidate arrays, checks self, injury, `+0x29C`, `+0x458`, matching global ID, range, height and line of sight. It returns an in-range unit ID; for a more distant selected target it orders movement with `FUN_180196280` and changes the healer to state `0x65`, returning zero.
- The healer updater reads and writes its AI state at `GameUnit + 0x2BC` and its current target's one-based unit ID at `GameUnit + 0x450`. The selector uses world positions at `GameUnit + 0xB2/+0xB4`; its ordinary search threshold begins at `0x20` world units. These fields support read-only per-catapult diagnostics, but list inclusion alone does not establish that the selector accepted a target.
- The healer updater's state 7 verifies target ID/global ID, injury and `+0x29C`; it searches again when invalid. On a healing pulse it adds 10 HP, clamps to maximum and updates percentage and health-bar blocks. It also retargets after a unit reaches maximum HP. `FUN_180188340` checks movement completion and `FUN_180197a10` turns the healer toward the target.
- The Script Extender 2.12.0 `OnUnitHealByBedouinHealer` hook changes the later heal amount; it does not change target selection. Fixes has separate Bedouin-healer creation patches, not a detour at the list-builder entry.

Machine entry contract: RVA `0x181340` begins `48 89 5C 24 10 48 89 6C 24 20`; the installed RedBird NativeX64 backend 1.5.0 copied-entry probe selected `Indirect`, displaced exactly 10 bytes, installed `FF 25` with a valid pointer slot and hook entry, then restored all copied bytes.

# Building repair contract (CrusaderDE.dll FBCB9319…F2831E2) [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

The installed `CrusaderDE.dll` has SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.

- `FUN_1800B6F70` (RVA `0xB6F70`) calculates repair wood and stone only. For each positive construction cost it uses `max(1, floor((maxHP-currentHP)*baseCost/maxHP))`; full health yields zero. The manager's output fields are at offsets `0x31B824` (wood) and `0x31B828` (stone).
- `FUN_1800D51A0` (RVA `0xD51A0`) supplies the HUD's repair costs and permission, including the native proximity check. The audited entry begins `48 89 5C 24 08 57 48 83 EC 30 48 63 1D E3 31 71 06`. `FUN_18019D960` calls it for Vanilla tower and gatehouse HUD modes.
- `FUN_1800D4EE0` (RVA `0xD4EE0`) handles the RepairBuilding action and checks only wood and stone before queuing chore `0x44` (68).
- `FUN_1800D5030` (RVA `0xD5030`) executes the chore. It validates the building global ID, checks and subtracts the queued wood and stone, then restores health to the maximum. Gold, iron and pitch are absent from this path.
- The installed Script Extender exposes `BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingRepair` around the `0xD5030` repair execution: Pre runs before the original and Post only after the original was called. It exposes player ID, one-based building ID, global ID, wood and stone costs, and `SkipOriginalFunction`.

APIShared's optional repair capability checks the full installed hash and the entry bytes before calling `0xD51A0` under `EngineInterface.threadLock`. Its event handler checks extra resources in Pre and charges them in Post only after a verified damaged-to-full-health transition for the same building global ID. This supplement is tied to the above native and Script Extender contracts and requires re-audit on either update.

# Multiplayer building sleep and local selection

Native build SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`. The installed DLL hash was checked before using these RVAs. The functions below are identified by direct data flow; `DLL_GameAction` is a confirmed export, while the other symbolic roles are static reconstructions from candidate-labeled decompiler functions and references.

`MainViewModel.ButtonToggleZZZMode` calls `GameAction(ToggleSleep=1003, lastGameState.in_structure, 0)`. Native `DLL_GameAction` (`0x81870`, case `0x3EB`) stores the 1-based building ID in global `0x67E8394` and calls `0xD6F00`. That producer reads the selected record's building type, subject to a game-mode-specific early branch, then queues Chore 43. The Chore callback is table entry `0x2C7B88` (`0x2C7A30 + 43*8`) pointing to `0x13C10`. Its mode-1 path serializes **two bytes of building type** via `0x1F5F0`; its mode-0 path reads those two bytes and calls `0xD5980` with the Chore sender's player ID and the decoded type. It does not transmit a building ID.

`0xD5980` toggles the sender's per-type sleep flag and calls `0xC7E90`. For every alive building whose owner and type match the two arguments, `0xC7E90` updates the sleep state, clears local goods at record offsets `0x120` onward, and clears dependent references. The alternative branches are no matching record and an out-of-range type (`>=91`), which do not perform the reset. The periodic synchronizer at `0xC7D50` compares the building's sleep state with the per-type flag and resets on disagreement; the direct `0xC7E90` path already writes the new state. Native checksum builder `0x22020` hashes each building's `0xD0..0x32B` record interval, including iron at `0x138`, stone at `0x130`, and wood logs at `0x124`.

Fixes 1.19.1's installed `fixes.dll` patches the reset block at `0xC7F3E`. It reads Script Extender's `CurrentlySelectedBuildingIdVA`, which resolves to the same native global at `0x67E8394`, indexes the building array by ID minus one, and selects a preservation branch from that building's type. Chore 43 itself supplies only the sender's building **type**; its callback and reset path do not update the selected-building global. Therefore the preservation branch depends on the local value of that global when the Chore executes.

Runtime confirmation, 27 September 2026 at 00:32:12 (host `BepInEx/LogOutput.log`, client `\\LENOVO_SERP\Stronghold Crusader Definitive Edition\BepInEx\LogOutput.log`): the passive `FIXES_BUILDING_SLEEP_PROBE` logged the same iron mine (`building=58`, `global=4124`, owner 1) with `iron=1` before the type-wide sleep toggle on both peers. The host's selected building was iron mine 58, and its iron stayed 1 at the next tick and 20 ticks later. The client's selected building was woodcutter's hut 24, and its iron became 0 at both follow-ups. The tester reported a desync during this test. Neither inspected log has an explicit desync or checksum message, so the direct runtime proof is the different resource value, not a checksum-to-cause trace.

The prior curated Chore-43 entry described a four-byte building ID payload from historical discussion; the current native producer and callback establish a two-byte building type instead.
