# CastlePlanner building visual observation (2026-10-24) [Scope: Mod work, not Vanilla]

Installed native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The diagnostic does not install a native hook or change any graphics value.

## Relevant audited boundaries [Vanilla facts]

- The construction dispatch at 0x6D580 reaches the generic construction path
  0x75780, which calls allocator 0xB47E0. Native building records use stride
  0x32C; their managed interop view is `GameBuilding`. The allocator's spawn
  Post event can precede the caller's footprint and graphics registration.
  `NeedsInit` at that boundary is not by itself a failure.
- 0x75780 records occupied tile IDs, current height, building occupancy,
  structure ID/type and changed state. Its 0x6CDD0 helper updates the
  miscellaneous display grid; 0x725E0 updates the affected tile/path region.
  0x69850 supplies the scale/rotation-dependent footprint offsets.
- The confirmed Extender-bound `c_game_update_visual_resourcetile` at
  0x6E620 writes GFX/alpha grid entries. Sprite variation 15 has an explicit
  selection branch; it must not be classified as invalid or normalized to zero.
  Other role names above are descriptive, not newly confirmed symbols.
- The actual managed `GameMap` render-packet consumer maps native coordinates
  with `mapGameTileToTilemapCoord`, reads 21-short entries, resolves graphics
  through `SpriteMapping`, and stores sprite, construction, height and hover
  state in `GameMapTile`. `TilemapManager` subsequently refreshes the tilemaps.
  Native and managed observations can legitimately belong to different phases.

Verified against hash-selected semantic function records and the native field
flow, the local Extender APIs and actual installed Assembly-CSharp metadata.
`getMapTile`, `mapGameTileToTilemapCoord`, `CurrentRotation` and the observed
GameMapTile fields are public in the installed assembly. Unknown grid values
and raw building bytes remain observations, not validity rules.

## Reproduction and interpretation limits

Reported reproduction: The Bulls eye.map, Vanilla wolf6.aivjson, green start
location in the lower right, castle rotation South (0 degrees). The user reports
several affected buildings, hover flicker and persistence across camera rotation.
The two later screenshots show blueprint overlays and the clear ground, not the
glitched placement state. No causal terrain or placement conclusion follows.

CastlePlanner's /devdiag-only observer captures the native construction stages,
then UI/hover/rotation/blueprint states, with immutable bounded file output.
It does not call refresh/repair routines, change sprites or alter gameplay.
The normal DLL is checked for absence of the diagnostic implementation and calls.
Real reproduction and diagnostic output are still needed to locate the fault;
static checks and a successful diagnostic installation are not gameplay evidence.

## Pipeline observation extension (2026-10-24)

The installed hash remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The reproduction produced 41 captures with no dropped captures or observation
exceptions. Granary building 10/global 13170 and the adjacent granary and brewers
had complete, distinct 4x4 occupancy and current/default native height 8 throughout
their footprints. This rules out a height discontinuity in those captured cells,
not a graphics or other terrain-dependent bug. No root cause is established.

Further managed audit against the installed real Assembly-CSharp.dll confirms:

- Director consumes MemoryBuffers in order through GameMap.processTestMap,
  then TilemapManager.endTileRefresh. A buffer can update a cell repeatedly;
  a method-post observation is the final state of that entire buffer, not the
  intermediate result of each record. Records are 21 signed shorts; a negative
  requested count uses a negative record-kind sentinel. Observers additionally
  bound reading to the actual managed array, without changing Vanilla arguments.
- Type-zero records resolve construction, base sprite, heights, light/colour and
  chevron graphics and enqueue a tile refresh. SpriteMapping can legitimately
  remap images and lighting; raw material/image numbers are not Unity sprite IDs.
- endTileRefresh consumes dirty cells only for visible rows and columns; refresh
  and GetTileData completion need not coincide with the incoming native packet.
  gameTile.GetTileData also applies colour and transform to the actual Tilemap,
  updates refresh bits and mirrors the returned sprite. A raw TileData transform
  or colour alone does not describe those separate Tilemap writes.
- setMouseTile performs an explicit mouseOver/refresh operation. There are no
  ordinary managed callers in this assembly; normal building hover is also
  carried by PlayState.in_structure. Do not interpret zero setMouseTile callback
  counts as a failed normal-hover observer.
- Building animation rows are a separate rendering path with composite object
  IDs, pixel offsets, transparency and row/layer sorting. A render object ID is
  not assumed to equal a native building ID. GameMap.buildingAnims is private;
  the exact Dictionary<int,BuildingAnim> reflection contract is validated before
  hooking. BuildingAnim/GameSprite scalar and renderer fields are public.

The /devdiag extension observes these four public managed methods through permanent
MonoMod hooks, preserving the existing APIShared.Audio processTestMap IL hook.
There are no new native hooks or graphics setters. Native snapshots are copied
only in the existing loader/spawn/tick contexts; render observations reference
their copied identities and monotone timestamps, with explicit age/generation.
Loaded-save observation waits for the matching successful central lifecycle start
and does not execute castle creation. The new save is test_castlespawngraphicglitch.sav.

Evidence and pending runtime boundaries are recorded under .work/a/castle-visual/002.
Read-only state comparisons and transition traces are observations; delayed
refresh, transparency changes, missing callbacks and shader property absence are
not automatically classified as errors. Hook callbacks, real save replay and
the first divergent rendering stage still require the next in-game test.

## Loaded-save observer selection correction (2026-10-25)

The next real run loaded test_castlespawngraphicglitch.sav in a new process and
the user reports that the visual defect persisted. Native hash is unchanged.
However, the diagnostic selected zero granary watches: the mode snapshot has
gameMembers=-1, and ActivePlayerHelper intentionally returns an empty list when
the synchronized multiplayer roster is absent. Reusing that helper for local
save observation was a diagnostic bug, not evidence of absent granaries.
There were 1,559 process-map and 5,826 refresh callbacks but no focused building
captures; the single 6,782-byte file contains only presentation-state transitions.
It cannot locate the rendering defect. Zero focused GetTileData callbacks in
this run do not imply that Vanilla did not call GetTileData.

The diagnostic now uses the central MissionContext.LocalPlayerId for local saves;
the roster remains supplemental evidence only in real multiplayer. A corrected
identity or initially missing targets schedules one discovery retry on the existing
native tick. Empty target sets are explicitly unavailable, never logged as ready;
a failed final retry retires observation instead of accumulating unrelated data.
The existing frame/native-thread boundary and all rendering hooks are unchanged.
Runtime proof and regression evidence: .work/a/castle-visual/003. This is a fix
to observation selection; the building graphics cause remains unresolved.

## Confirmed supplemental granary graphics variant mismatch (2026-10-25)

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The corrected observer recorded two actual player-1 granaries in session
20261025-001928-365-p43444-s1. Original AIV granary 10/global 13170 has variant 15;
supplemental granary 245/global 13700 has variant 0, both with size 4 and base
production image 237. The earlier synchronous spawn observation already shows
245 with variant 0 in NeedsInit: this value was not introduced by save loading.

The complete relevant parameter chain is confirmed against the selected native
records and installed Extender enums (MAPPER_GRANARY=80, STRUCT_GRANARY=19):

- CastlePlanner CreateSupplementalPrefab passes constant zero as CreatePrefab a7.
  The Extender forwards it as parameter 7 to 6D580. The dispatcher preserves it
  for mapper 80 (the mapper-54 exception is unrelated), converts mapper to struct
  via C77C0 and uses the generic 75780 path for struct 19. That forwards it as
  allocator B47E0 parameter 9. The allocator stores it at manager/slot+15E, the
  same variation read by the renderer. Granary does not enter the allocator's
  type-specific variation rewriting branches.
- 6E620 (confirmed c_game_update_visual_resourcetile) has distinct variation-15
  automatic and non-15 camera-relative branches. Non-15 adds a direction-dependent
  multiple of footprint size squared to the image; granary size squared is 16.
  The ordinary AIV placement path 51790 starts with variant 15 and granary mapper
  80 does not enter its directional/special-building exceptions. Constructor role
  names remain descriptive; the parameter flow and renderer branch are confirmed.
- Actual UI sprite sets match the unintended offsets exactly: managed camera 7
  gives original 237..252 versus supplemental 269..284 (+32); camera 5 gives
  237..252 versus 301..316 (+64); camera 3 gives 278..293 versus 374..389 (+96).
  The last pair uses the alternate image set in both buildings. These shifts are
  already in type-zero input packets and are preserved by SpriteMapping,
  GetTileData and the actual Tilemap. There is no recorded returned-sprite versus
  Tilemap-sprite discrepancy for this interval.

This establishes a wrong spawn graphics variant for the supplemental granary.
It explains incorrect image fragments and view dependence without a terrain or
missing-refresh hypothesis. Other supplemental buildings share this caller, but
their appropriate variants must be audited per mapper; globally replacing every
zero with 15 is not established by this granary finding.

The packets also alternate rapidly between image sets separated by 41 during
hover/rotation. That fluctuation exists before Unity; whether correcting the
variant removes every flicker symptom requires a targeted gameplay comparison.
The 32 MiB limit was reached after roughly ten seconds, so later activity is not
covered. The captured interval includes the relevant hover and three camera views.

Evidence: .work/a/castle-visual/004/cause.json. No runtime implementation, installed
DLL or game state was changed by this analysis. Existing saves retain variant 0;
a corrected future spawn alone cannot repair those persisted records.

## Supplemental prefab automatic sprites (2026-10-25)

Native SHA256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The complete current supplemental set is audited in
`.work/a/castle-spawn-fix/001/supplemental-audit.json` (21 mapper entries,
checked against installed Extender enums and the catalog-driven spawn routes).
Native AIV builder 51790 initializes argument 7 to 15; none of these mappers
enters its hovel/directional/workshop/drawbridge exceptions. In 6D580, argument
15 and the old 0 both select unrotated placement geometry; the difference is
sprite selection in 6E620, where 15 avoids camera-relative sheet offsets.

Constructors are covered by dispatch, not by assuming granary behavior:
- Granary, armoury and the ordinary fear buildings: 75780 forwards variation to
  B47E0 argument 9. That allocator persists the variation consumed by 6E620.
- Stores (struct 10): 76E80 creates four stockpile records and forwards the
  variation to B47E0 for each record.
- Gardens, statues and shrines: 73EA0 passes the mapper-derived family subtype
  to B47E0 (confirmed from canonical machine code, since decompilation omits
  arguments). The caller's orientation argument is not the family subtype.
- Cess pits and ponds: 76060 similarly retains the mapper-derived family data;
  allocator normalization preserves their specialized sprite behavior.

SupplementalPrefabVisualPolicy accepts exactly the current supported mappers
and supplies the automatic-sprite sentinel 0x0f (no Extender enum defines it).
Unknown supplemental mappers are rejected before creation, pending their audit.
All supplemental calls pass through SupplementalPrefabSpawner and the one
CreatePrefab call in CastlePlannerRuntime; native AIV placement, hovel styles,
keeps, gates and workshops retain their separate conventions. No new native
hook, offset, public member, serializer or lifecycle callback is introduced.

Tests enumerate all Extender mapper values against actual FearFactor and
compound/storage routes, then execute each supported mapper through the real
capture helper and verify a single delegate invocation with variation 15.
Existing identity, nesting, raw-return, terrain and rotation checks remain.
Existing saves keep their persisted wrong variation; this is a future-spawn fix.
Gameplay confirmation, especially the rapid alternate-image hover symptom,
requires a newly spawned castle rather than reloading the old defective save.

# CrusaderDE Chore system knowledge

## Scope and confidence

This document is the self-contained human-readable companion to the structured Chore knowledge records in this directory. It describes native facts, runtime observations, and still-open interpretations. Addresses are RVAs relative to image base `0x180000000` and are valid only for the explicitly named binary hash.

Confidence is deliberately split by fact. `confirmed-runtime` means that a focused runtime trace observed the behavior. `confirmed-static` means that complete native data flow, an export, or an exact binary contract establishes it. `probable` is a strong semantic reconstruction. `candidate` is a lead that still needs validation. Historical HD names never establish DE semantics by themselves.

The historical analysis and accepted two-peer runtime trace used:

- Native SHA-256 `17F8DD4A92FF6125BD6A3A70ABC80C727682E489696C218D146A7EA6D2F88BF4`
- File size `3,446,784` bytes
- PDB reference `D:\Jenkins\.jenkins\workspace\CrusaderDE\CDE-DLL-STABLE\CrusaderDEDLL\Source\ff_gfx_manager\Release\Crusader.pdb`
- PDB GUID `{C1E26511-89D7-4315-843A-C3DF84430ECC}`, age `7`

The current canonical baseline and installed game use:

- Steam build ID `24816905`
- Native SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`
- File size `3,451,392` bytes

## Managed and network path

Managed UI actions normally call `EngineInterface.GameAction(...)` while holding `EngineInterface.threadLock`. Native `DLL_GameAction` stores opcode-specific parameters and queues a native Chore. `DLL_RunTick` emits outer Chore records through the managed multiplayer layer. Native Chores use multiplayer packet type 1 on Steam channel 2. Received data is passed through `EngineInterface.ReceiveChore` to `DLL_ReceiveChore`, appended to the native incoming FIFO, parsed, and converted into a remote pending slot.

The sender does not receive its own network record. Its pending slot is created during local enqueue. Receivers create their pending slots from the incoming record. At the scheduled tick, both paths call the same opcode handler in execute mode.

Historical Script Extender custom Steam packets were reliable transport but did not create a native pending slot, command ID, scheduled tick, or SyncEvent barrier membership. The later Script Extender Chore transport reserves opcode 106 and routes its payload through the native queue.

## Wire formats

### Outer managed/native record

Each outgoing or incoming record is:

| Offset | Size | Meaning |
|---:|---:|---|
| `0x00` | 4 | Signed payload length |
| `0x04` | 1 | Outgoing target player ID or incoming sender player ID |
| `0x05` | variable | Payload |

Outgoing target `0` means normal broadcast. The outgoing buffer is terminated by a negative payload length. A record consumes `payloadLength + 5` bytes. `DLL_ReceiveChore` reconstructs the same shape with the separately supplied sender ID. The observed incoming FIFO capacity is approximately one million bytes; overflow drops a record in the inspected path.

### Normal inner Chore

| Offset | Size | Meaning |
|---:|---:|---|
| `0x00` | 1 | Opcode |
| `0x01` | 3 | Scheduled tick, little-endian unsigned 24-bit |
| `0x04` | 4 | Command ID, little-endian signed 32-bit |
| `0x08` | variable | Opcode-specific payload |

The 24-bit tick is zero-extended on receive. Its theoretical wrap is `16,777,216` ticks, approximately 116.5 hours at 40 ticks per second; such a match was not tested.

Opcodes `0`, `1`, `125`, `126`, and `127` use special timing, synchronization, compression, or ping paths. The normal handler table is valid through opcode `120`. Bytes corresponding to `121` through `124` are not reliable normal handler pointers.

## Pending slots and handler ABI

A normal pending slot is `0x500` bytes. The inspected queue has 500 slot candidates.

| Slot offset | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0x00` | Scheduled tick |
| `0x04` | Sender/player ID |
| `0x08` | Opcode |
| `0x09` | State; `1` denotes a new pending command |
| `0x0C` | Command ID |
| `0x10` | Already included in a host barrier |
| `0x11` | Opcode-specific parameters |

Relevant ChoreManager offsets are current-slot index `+0x84CC8`, handler mode `+0x84CCC`, payload size `+0x84CD4`, field cursor `+0x370BF8`, and pending slots `+0xB0BF8`.

Handlers take no explicit parameters and read the active context through ChoreManager state:

- Mode `0`: deserialize/use slot fields and execute the simulation effect.
- Mode `1`: serialize the locally staged values into the slot/outgoing record.
- Mode `2`: publish the expected receive payload size.

The field-copy helper moves one field in the direction selected by the mode and advances the cursor. Mode 2 makes fixed payload sizes the safe baseline contract. A bounded envelope can carry a logical length, but truly variable native payload sizing needs additional receive-dispatch handling.

## Scheduling, identity, and barrier

Observed command IDs follow `commandId = playerId * 100000000 + perPlayerCounter`.

Initial scheduling is dynamic, approximately `max(currentTick, trackedReferenceTick) + currentDynamicCommandDelay`. A special path uses `currentTick + syncPeriod * 50`; a period of four produces 200 ticks. Runtime tracing established that the first scheduled tick is provisional. Before execute mode, the host SyncEvent can move the pending slot to its final target tick. Source player, request ID, and command ID remain stable correlation identities; changing scheduled ticks are not identity conflicts.

The host normally emits opcode-120 SyncEvents approximately every four ticks. It scans pending slots, marks commands not already assigned to a barrier, and includes their command IDs. The payload begins with target tick, command-ID count, and sequence number followed by the IDs. Static analysis indicates a maximum of 25 IDs; runtime testing confirmed batches of five.

At the target tick, a client checks whether every listed command ID exists locally. A missing command stalls simulation advancement. After approximately three seconds, the native path logs `SyncEvent - Forced run` and permits progress. This fallback was found statically but was not triggered in the accepted runtime test.

## Native function map

| Historical RVA | Current RVA | Working meaning |
|---:|---:|---|
| `0x23960` | `0x23990` | Queue local Chore |
| `0x237D0` | `0x23800` | Build normal inner Chore |
| `0x23E40` | `0x23E70` | Append received outer record |
| `0x23C00` | `0x23C30` | Pop incoming record |
| `0x235F0` | `0x23620` | Parse and dispatch incoming payload |
| `0x23EE0` | `0x23F10` | Schedule received normal command |
| `0x19C370` | `0x19D3C0` | Write outgoing outer record |
| `0x1F5C0` | `0x1F5F0` | Copy/serialize one Chore field |
| `0x1F7B0` | `0x1F7E0` | Execute due pending Chores |
| `0x1BCC0` | `0x1BCF0` | Sync barrier / can advance frame |
| `0x1ADE0` | `0x1AE10` | Opcode-120 SyncEvent handler |
| `0x27DB0` | `0x27DE0` | Adjust dynamic command delay |
| `0x24E50` | `0x24E80` | Frame lag/skip calculation |
| `0x1CCF0` | `0x1CD20` | Additional ping/lag management |
| `0x1F6B0` | `0x1F6E0` | Queue synchronized autosave |
| `0x127A0` | `0x127A0` | Opcode-31 MakeTroop handler |
| `0x80AE0` | `0x81870` | Export `DLL_GameAction` |
| `0x856F0` | `0x86480` | Export `DLL_ReceiveChore` |
| `0x858F0` | `0x86680` | Export `DLL_RunTick` |

All listed internal function pairs except separately marked gaps have confirmed one-to-one version identity through unique raw or normalized instruction hashes and CFG. This establishes identity across builds, not automatically unchanged semantics.

For the current build, the handler table is at `0x2C7A30`; opcode 111's entry is `0x2C7DA8`. The entry still points to RVA `0xFC30`, whose expected bytes begin `C2 00 00` followed by padding. The queue entry is derived from the unique interior pattern at `0x239AE` minus `0x1E`, because a prior startup hook may replace its prologue. The field-copy entry remains `0x1F5F0`.

## Known opcode interpretations

The structured opcode catalog is authoritative for machine queries. Important interpretation cautions are:

- `31` MakeTroop has a statically observed five-byte native payload even though an early enum comment described two `INT32` values. The disagreement is retained as counter-evidence.
- `35` covers both ration changes and food restriction and therefore has mode-dependent payload meaning.
- `36` is a combined unit-order operation; stop, disband, attack-here, and cow-related submodes are not fully separated.
- `109` is AutoTrade settings in DE, despite historical HD use as a skirmish-screen command.
- `113` has a confirmed ally-command family but four mode-dependent values remain incompletely named.
- `119` is reached from managed `GameActionCommand.ExtremePower`; its eight payload bytes are not field-mapped.
- `120` is synchronization/barrier metadata and carries no gameplay mutation itself.
- `111` had no direct static producer in the historical build and targeted a trivial handler. Indirect generation was not disproved, so it is only a hash-bound unused candidate.
- Historical opcode groups `46`, `49`, `54-67`, `80-84`, `87-101`, and `114-116` remain candidates until their DE producers and handlers are validated.

## Accepted runtime evidence

The accepted no-op probe used opcode 111 and a fixed 16-byte payload containing magic `SCH1`, protocol version 1, source player ID, zero flags, per-source request ID, and sentinel `0xC011AB1E`. It held `EngineInterface.threadLock`, staged one payload, called the original queue, and made no simulation mutation in mode 0.

Before the comprehensive delay test, a one-human smoke test executed two host requests exactly once. A normal two-peer test executed 11 requests (six host-originated and five client-originated) with identical command IDs and final ticks on both peers.

The comprehensive test used a 500 ms incoming delay on the non-host peer and five commands per click:

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---:|
| Logical requests | 30 |
| Host-originated / client-originated | 15 / 15 |
| Mode-0 executions per peer | 30 |
| Relevant host SyncEvents | 6 |
| IDs in each relevant SyncEvent | 5 |
| Held / barrier-observed / released / reinjected | 15 / 15 / 15 / 15 |
| Minimum / maximum / average hold | 502 / 524 / 509.2 ms |
| Minimum repeated barrier-wait run calls | 15 |
| Maximum tick beyond barrier before reinjection | 0 |
| Commands crossing the barrier early | 0 |
| Errors | 0 |

Every request had one origin enqueue, one mode-1 serialization, one remote mode-2 sizing call, one mode-0 execution per peer, identical command ID/final scheduled tick/actual tick, and `mutation=none`. Every delayed remote command followed incoming observation, hold, matching SyncEvent, repeated barrier wait, release, reinjection, and execution at the original final target tick. No forced run, resync, access violation, callback failure, malformed payload, correlation collision, duplicate execution, tick mismatch, legacy custom-packet path, or state mutation occurred.

## Safety and remaining gaps

- A native integration must fail closed on unknown hashes, unexpected handler pointers/bytes, non-unique patterns, or invalid memory bounds.
- Managed exceptions must never cross native callbacks. Delegates, hooks, and handler pointers must remain rooted for process lifetime and must not be removed from SHCDE's startup-time plugin `OnDestroy()`.
- Only handler mode 0 may apply synchronized gameplay mutation. UI and capability packets may enqueue or negotiate but must not apply the effect themselves.
- All peers require compatible registrations and payload semantics; an unmodified peer would execute a custom opcode as a no-op and desynchronize.
- Still unproven: save/load with pending custom Chores, native resync, repeated sessions and map changes, disconnect/host migration, sustained slot recycling, exact 25-ID limit, 24-bit tick wrap, indirect opcode-111 producers, and deliberate forced-run behavior.
- Opcode 42's historical handler did not receive a safe current-build version match and remains historical/candidate until located and revalidated.

# Packaged Coop maps and Ready admission [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Observed 2026-10-26 against native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`
and installed Assembly-CSharp SHA-256
`BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
This is a confirmed-static managed control-flow contract; the reproduced run did
not record the private map-valid flag. No native RVA or patch is required.

## Closed relevant path

- Coop page XAML sends `Ready` through `MainViewModel.MultiplayerMenuCommandFunction`
  to `FRONT_Multiplayer.ButtonClicked`. `ReadyLock` is a distinct command.
- `CoopMissionChanged` obtains the selected mission's `header` from the Coop table
  and assigns `selectedMPHeader`. Host `UpdateHostInfo` publishes that header's
  `fileName` and its CRC cast to `int` via `Platform_Multiplayer.UpdateHostLobbyInfo`.
- `MapFileManager.GetFileInfoFromFileName` reads its second argument as the actual
  local file path. It returns a header; it does not register that header in an MP
  catalog. Its returned `fileName` is the basename without extension.
- The client's `FRONT_Multiplayer.Update` checks `MPMapChecked` and `MPLastMapName`.
  When necessary, it calls `GetHeaderFromFileNameMP(name, parsedLobbyCrc)` after
  waiting for an active map retrieval. That overload searches only BuiltInMP,
  WorkshopMP and UserMP, using case-insensitive names and the existing CRC comparison.
- Missing or nonmatching headers leave `MPMapValid=false`, clear local readiness
  unless locked, and expose Vanilla's map-retrieval UI. A matching header updates
  `selectedMPHeader` and the briefing/radar and sets `MPMapValid=true`.
- `ButtonClicked("Ready")` changes readiness only when `MPMapValid || isHost`;
  otherwise it publishes false without an explanatory error. Returning from the
  command is therefore not evidence of acceptance. Unready and unlock are separate
  transitions and must remain possible.
- Header CRC is a public `uint`; the lobby query uses `int`. Preserve the game's
  comparison and transport semantics. A matching CRC alone does not establish
  package integrity: the content provider must independently validate its package.

## Package consequence and correction boundary [mod integration]

The inspected Suffer of the antler package contains 40 bundled map references,
each under `Assets/<mission>/map.map`. Direct package loading can succeed while
the subsequent catalog lookup cannot find that local map. Different missions
also share the Vanilla basename `map`; name-only map-check caching is insufficient
after a package mission changes.

APIShared's exact-name/CRC lookup broker allows a consumer to supply its current
verified package header without changing global catalogs. ExtendedData scopes that
offer to the active Steam lobby, package fingerprint and selected mission, and
invalidates the cached check when this identity changes. Vanilla remains the writer
of successful map validity. Other callers and inactive providers retain Vanilla.

## Chat observation boundary

Steam lobby sends and the Extender receive event do not prove visible chat text.
`FRONT_Multiplayer.receivedLobbyChat` skips ordinary messages when `MPChatMuted`,
truncates individual text to 300 characters, and appends accepted messages to the
shared lobby history. Its `systemMessage` argument bypasses that mute check.
APIShared's system-message classification retains this original renderer exactly
once; ExtendedData splits its own warnings into numbered messages of at most 280
characters and never treats chat text as network authority.

Source verification: the managed files selected through CURRENT.json and the
installed assembly metadata. Runtime acceptance still requires a real host/client
run, including a bundled mission change and ordinary installed-map comparison.

# Coop Trail Customize presentation [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Static audit: 2026-10-21. Native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`;
installed `Assembly-CSharp.dll` SHA-256
`BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
Both were compared with CURRENT.json / DATABASE_INFO.json before use.

## Managed state and consumers

- `FRONT_Multiplayer.CoopMissionChanged(int,int,bool)` receives zero-based Trail
  and one-based mission selection. It creates the roster and setup, updates the
  Coop page radar and host data, but does not initialize `MPLobbyMember.teamShield`.
- `ReSortTeamInfo()` sorts one-based player IDs and can normalize team IDs.
  `CreateTeamShields()` returns immediately while `coopGame` is true.
- `PopulateTeamsPanel()` calls `ReSortTeamInfo()`, resets each member's
  `teamShield` to -1, then assigns team IDs to grouped members. It populates the
  hidden panel's faces/names/slices without changing `Show_SkirmishTeamsPanel`.
- `Update()` uses `teamShield` for lobby-row background colors. The radar reads
  the same field through `getKeepTeamShield(int zeroBasedKeepIndex)`; regenerate
  radar shields after generating team presentation. Opening the team panel runs
  `PopulateTeamsPanel()`; closing it updates the radar. A presentation refresh
  must not replay mission selection, which would replace customized settings.
- `ShowSetupScreen()` changes visibility/readiness presentation, but does not
  project the full setup into skirmish captions, advanced-option indicator or map
  metadata. `SetupSkirmishModeSettings()` and `PopulateMapDetailsPanel(FileHeader)`
  provide those projections; the latter overwrites `StandaloneMissionText`.

## Input callback boundary

`SetupSkirmishModeSettings()` sets all four Coop game-speed sliders.
Each page subscribes `ValueChanged` to
`FRONT_Multiplayer.MP_Settings_GameSpeed_Slider_ValueChanged`. That handler returns
when `!panelLoaded || !panelActive`. Otherwise it modifies `MPTEMPsetupData`, or
the active Coop `MPsetupData` based on the currently visible Trail page; when none
is visible its initial speed is zero. Vanilla `doOpen()` leaves `panelActive`
false while setting up controls. A late presentation refresh must likewise
suppress these callbacks and restore the previous gate in `finally`.

The team and UI state is managed. Native `DLL_GetTrailMissionInfo` (RVA 0x84600,
confirmed export; built-in non-Coop customization comparison) and
`DLL_ApplyMultiplayerSetupData` (RVA 0x81050, confirmed export; setup submission)
do not initialize these managed presentation fields. Their unnamed helpers at
0x286C0 and 0x26370 retain candidate names in the semantic database.

Evidence: hash-matched managed decompilation of FRONT_Multiplayer, all four
FRONT_CoopTrail pages, MainViewModel, Platform_Multiplayer and EngineInterface;
semantic function queries for the exports and their callees. The executable
member check in `ExtendedData/Test-RuntimePreflight.ps1` verifies the selected
installed assembly's reflection/direct-access signatures. Adapter tests execute
production source against boundary doubles; they do not prove Noesis rendering
or live host/client synchronization. In-game visual acceptance remains pending.

## Custom partner keep assignment, 2026-10-25 [mod integration]

Reverified the installed native and managed SHA-256 values above. This is a
managed lobby-state defect; no new native hook or structure offset is needed.

`CoopMissionChanged` creates the local AI partner in player slot 2, then writes
the complete mission keep order, accounting for `coopOrderSwapped`. ExtendedData
supplies the same mission table contract through `MissionProjection.KeepOrder`.
First selection and Coop continuation reach this initialization from
`FRONT_Multiplayer.Update_Coop`; mission selection and SwapCoop also call it.

`updateSteamIDMappings` removes absent identities through
`remove_player_from_keep_locations`, then adds new identities through
`add_player_to_keep_locations`. The latter uses `System.Random.Next` among free
keeps when the player lacks an assignment. BugfixesAndQoL's former partner
replacement removed Vanilla's slot-2 identity and inserted a temporary Custom
Lord identity before finalizing it. The mapping update therefore discarded the
correct mission keep and could choose another free keep. Preserving the member's
list index, colour and team did not preserve its map position.

The corrected path configures Vanilla's existing member and publishes a freshly
prepared MPAIVInfo, retaining the member identity, all eight mappings and keep
assignments. Final launch validation checks the selected name against both the
member and AIV selection. Saved/customized setup positions are not reconstructed
from mission defaults at launch. Normal creation of new random opponents keeps
its existing placement semantics.

Native data-flow cross-check: confirmed export `DLL_ApplyMultiplayerSetupData`
at RVA `0x81050` calls generic candidate-named helper `0x26370`, copying transfer
ints 10..17 into eight signed-byte keep assignments. Candidate-named lookup
`0x89870` returns the one-based keep whose assignment equals playerId-1, or zero.
The start path at `0x94350` uses that lookup to obtain keep coordinates for both
fixed and automatic AIV selection and the no-fit fallback. These are static
call/data-flow findings for the recorded hash, not runtime placement evidence.
`UpdateHostInfo(bool)` submits setup data immediately even with delayed=true;
only lobby transport is delayed. Retaining the identity avoids transient wrong
submissions as well as the final wrong assignment.

The actual managed assembly exposes the required lobby/member/AIV data publicly;
the existing private `UpdateHostInfo(System.Boolean)` method is accessed through
a signature-checked reflection adapter. Automated tests execute the production
configuration and launch-validation helpers against actual game data types.
Fresh-game visual and spawn acceptance remains a separate in-game check.

# Crenelated wall construction and sticky high pieces [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256 FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2; managed BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789. Installed SE 2.14.1 hash E5D78FDF2EA9701336C398F7D29410F206D141FC01AA8099F30C824E6AB8A0B3, fork commit 5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3, tree c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295. Fixes source v1.26.4. Audit date 2026-10-14. Findings are confirmed static data/control flow for these identities, not observed game execution; internal FUN names are not exported APIs.

## Complete feature path

Managed `EngineInterface.PlaceMapperItem` serializes access with `threadLock` and calls exported `DLL_MapAction` at 0x85BD0. This sets/restores temporary native view/player state and enters 0x8AAF0. Wall line handling 0x94120 uses 0x7A3B0 validation and 0x61210 preview, then enqueues Chore 25 on mouse release. Both requested coordinates must be active; validation retains terrain, structures, ownership/unit eligibility, distance and native path/build-range branches. Crenel eligibility calls 0x5C580 for adjacent suitable wall masks. Native line walking advances every nonzero coordinate difference by one per iteration and revisits the endpoint.

The current Chore table at 0x2C7A30 points opcode 25 to 0x11B50. Mode 1 writes fields; mode 0 restores them and calls 0x6F230 with the Chore sender from native global 0x88E3D6C, not the local view. 0x6F230 reruns validation and reads current availability at 0xCF640. Its command maximum limits raster visits, while availability limits actual new placements with a strict-less-than comparison. Native validation failure or zero maximum cannot place tiles. Intact existing walls are skipped for mapper 26; damaged cells may be reconstructed.

0xCF640 returns 100 for the native cheat/editor branch, uses its separate native mode-6 resource branch, otherwise computes twice the stone/plank balance minus one when a corresponding remainder exists, with maximum 250. 0x6F230 stops when availability is less than the already placed count, not less-than-or-equal. A delayed command can consequently place a shorter prefix than its queued maximum. 0xC8CC0 charges the actual placement count and retains a partial-stone accumulator; SE supports wall cost multipliers and Fixes has an additional low-wall-only quota adjustment. Do not infer current quota from a local preview or implement a replacement price formula merely to validate shape.

On successful crenel placement, 0x6F230 sets bit 0x200, raises native byte height by 68 or 98 according to 0x5C0E0, and sets bit 0x400000 when X/Y parity differs. It establishes wall/owner state, handles units/vegetation, refreshes tile/neighbour pathfinding, queues area refresh via 0xE3B90, charges actual wall count and marks component state dirty. Owner storage preserves upper bits and stores player-1 in the lower three bits. The public SE owner getter returns the raw byte; consumers must decode it.

AI placement 0x6CB20 (caller 0x51790) independently handles mappers 26/35, flags, native height, parity, ownership, refresh and costs. This is a countercheck, not the human entry point. The proposed consumer does not replace or subscribe to the AI placement path.

## Renderer and downstream semantics

0x65830 consumes changed tile/region state from the normal loop 0xCDE60 and reset path 0x5BC70. For intact wall/crenel cells without structures, 0x5C2D0 recognizes the two-opposite-neighbour straight case; 0x5C1C0 recognizes corner cases. Straight pieces select low/high sprite families 0xC0070..0xC007F according to orientation, tile variation and the high bit. Other endpoints, corners and junctions use special sprites 0xC0080..0xC0084 and OR high into the logic layer. That write is permanent: transitioning an already high endpoint into a straight middle never clears its old high bit. Parallel rows also fail the isolated-straight predicate and are forced high. This explains the single-placement and double-row behavior without assuming a different user-input mapper.

The three explicit 0x400000 logic-layer OR writers are human placement 0x6F230, AI placement 0x6CB20 and visual recomputation 0x65830. Generic clear/removal paths and construction conversion must still be respected. Damage uses its own graphics branch, and destruction/removal invalidates the old topology. Readbacks use current ownership, flags, damage and structure state; a consumer must not retain old tile identity blindly through unload/reload.

High is not cosmetic only. 0x6B530 adds 10 for a low crenel and 20 for a high piece and complements an inaccessible result according to owner/context. 0x9C730 also distinguishes height +10/+20. Path and edge readers at 0xD86F0, 0xDC900, 0xE9D90, 0xE9FF0, 0xF0710 and 0x10DF60 branch on the high bit. Render path 0x41D60 has additional height/presentation reads. Therefore a logical correction requires the public path/visual refresh, not only a sprite write.

## Corrected Chore-25 evidence

The older consolidated opcode-25 row's proposed six Int32 fields/24-byte size is not the contract of this build. 0x11B50 declares nominal payload size 12 and copies fields of sizes 2,2,2,2,1,2 through 0x1F5F0. Their consumed offsets are beginX 0, beginY 2, endX 4, endY 6, mapper 8 and signed build maximum 9. The four coordinates are zero-initialized before their low words are read. The sender comes from the decoded Chore slot, not a payload field. 0x1F5F0 advances its cursor by the literal copy size, hence these fields consume 11 bytes; the meaning/content of the remaining nominal byte is not interpreted by this handler. This current static audit supersedes that historical proposed row. The raw/consolidated artifacts and SQLite publication are preserved rather than silently relabeled during unrelated ongoing baseline work.

## Consumer contract and validation [mod integration]

SE's existing `OnBuildWall` publisher is process-lived. Its Pre inputs are mutable; the wrapper ignores `SkipOriginalFunction` and always calls Vanilla with the effective inputs. Post is reconstructed from original inputs and has no usable success result. Setting maximum zero is a supported native no-placement input, but a runtime before/after check remains necessary. The debug mirror tool calls native originals before Pre and is outside this interception boundary.

`Testmods/CrenelatedWallTest` uses these existing events and public APIShared mission/preset services. It installs no hooks, preserves Vanilla special pieces, corrects straight own middles, rejects new 2x2 blocks or unavoidable equal triples, and persists only touched cells. Its sole direct native access calls the unmodified 0xCF640 getter read-only, with full-body live validation, executable-pattern fallback, hash binding and permanent delegate rooting. Save classification uses APIShared because the installed SE can mark multiplayer saves as non-save archive loads; repeated archive callbacks stage data rather than applying it early.

Executable regression: `Testmods/CrenelatedWallTest/tests/audit-native.py` verifies the current identity, 27 feature functions, Chore table/dispatch, the complete 179-byte availability getter and all three explicit high-bit writers. Policy tests exercise actual production algorithms, preservation of modeled Vanilla special-piece redraws, ownership/bounds, rejected-command neutrality, resources/prefixes, deterministic two-peer maps and actual MessagePack encoding. Runtime sources and XAML bindings are type-checked against the installed true assemblies without emitting the mod DLL. Game graphics, unit height, native callback execution, real peer synchrony and save acceptance must be checked in game; do not promote fixture passes to those claims.

## Follow-up audit: low straight endpoints, 2026-10-15

This section supersedes the initial consumer's fixed-high endpoint/no-hook restriction above; the native identity and original observations remain unchanged. The user explicitly approved a permanent graphics hook owned exclusively by the testmod. APIShared itself remains unchanged by this follow-up. Its independent development source is now 0.10.0, the local DLL has assembly version 0.9.1 and lacks build evidence, while the game has installed 0.9.2. The user explicitly authorized consuming that installed 0.9.2 DLL without building/copying APIShared; both development and installed files are hash-checked unchanged.

The complete straight predicate at 0x5C2D0 is 237 bytes, Win64 ABI `int(tileManager*, int tileId, int rowY, int direction)`. EAX is 0 or 1. A full executable-section branch scan finds only two direct entries, 0x65DD6 and 0x65E4F, both in renderer 0x65830; pseudocode cross-check finds no non-renderer consumer. The callers use R9D=0 and R9D=2 respectively. The predicate reads exactly four cardinal crenel bits via row*8 neighbor deltas, with directions 0/4 sharing one axis and 2/6 the other. The admitted NativeX64 Absolute scheme requires 14 patch bytes, rounded to 15 by three full five-byte home-slot stores: RBX at RSP+8, RSI at RSP+10h, RDI at RSP+18h. No relative operands, branches or flags are displaced. Trampoline continuation is 0x5C2DF, the original XOR. No direct executable-section branch targets the interior of these 15 bytes. The full function and live entry are matched before publication; existing modifications/chaining are refused. Installed RedBird.Backends.NativeX64 hash is 0843DD4C381A3E77DD6D8B51D5CCF95465B3FB49BFDF2980F39A212D774AADB0. Its actual NativeDetour, PrologueAnalyzer, JumpFactory and options were decompiled for this audit, rather than inferring behavior from another hook family.

The approved override calls the original first and preserves every positive result. A negative result can become positive solely for an immutable published low-endpoint assignment, matching manager, packed tile, row, owner and live intact/non-building state. Exactly one unchanged cardinal neighbor must remain, on the requested axis. This selects native low straight graphics without allowing the special fallback's sticky-high write. The callback writes no simulation data and makes no policy decisions. Session changes empty the snapshot; installed code remains published for process lifetime.

The actual production validator and disabled callback were executed through the installed NativeX64 backend on a copied full 237-byte function, with independently allocated tile data, for all 16 cardinal masks and four axis directions: 146 checks passed. This validates Absolute/15, inline target/NOP patch, the unchanged three displaced instructions, real trampoline continuation, argument/return semantics, and disabled Vanilla behavior. It does not confirm in-game endpoint appearance or peer synchrony.

## Follow-up audit: native red construction preview, 2026-10-23

Native identity remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2, verified against the installed canonical DLL. These are confirmed-static field/control-flow findings; visual game acceptance remains open. Earlier consumer-state observations above remain historical.

The complete 1627-byte 0x7A3B0 validator has Win64 ABI void(tileManager*, int playerId, uint beginX, uint beginY, uint endX, uint endY, short mapper). Executable-section direct-branch scan confirms only calls 0x6F299 and 0x941F1. It initializes the 64-bit pair at tileManager+0x204E6E4 to 1 (invalid int=1, next int=0), and clears only the invalid int after full successful raster validation. Early failure, bounds/support-wall/terrain/unit/build-range branches retain invalid. Crenel supporting-wall eligibility is 0x5C580, unchanged. Automated AI construction calls its separate validator 0x77CF0 and is not a caller of this hook.

The same field is independently proven by UI global 0x60AD494 = tileManager base 0x405EDB0 + 0x204E6E4. UI 0x94120 runs validation before either preview or release. 0x61210 selects invalid crenel ghost sprite 0x60014 versus valid 0x60004 from this int, zeroes the invalid preview count and calls the native preview-price path with preview flag 1. On release, 0x94120 enqueues Chore 25 only if this same status is zero. It obtains current CF640 quota and queues that value as maximum raster visits; execution's additional actual-placement quota remains a distinct comparison. Native execution revalidates at 0x6F230. No error-reason number needs fabrication for a mod shape veto.

The tested NativeX64 backend hash remains 0843DD4C381A3E77DD6D8B51D5CCF95465B3FB49BFDF2980F39A212D774AADB0. Absolute/14 minimum rounds to 18 bytes at the validator entry: mov [rsp+10h],edx (4), push rbx/rbp/rdi (1 each), push r12/r13 (2 each), sub rsp,80h (7). Continuation 0x7A3C2; no direct executable-section entry into the displaced interior. There are no displaced relative operands or branches. Consumer fixtures run the production callback and actual backend/trampoline with this exact prologue plus an isolated seven-argument native ABI/status probe; the real validator body depends on module globals and is checked statically, not executed outside the game. Disabled paths, original veto, additional veto, next-call reset and managed policy failure preserve original-once semantics.

The consumer optionally registers the entry as Exclusive and remaining body as Observe using existing public NativeSiteRegistry; APIShared itself is unchanged. Complete snapshot/live bytes are checked, no chaining is admitted, and a failed preview install retains existing execution protection. No published code is unpatched. Rendering only consumes the native invalid state; actual construction continues to use fresh synchronized admission, bypassing the preview policy through current-thread OnBuildWall scopes. Preview cache reuse validates every raw read, failed/empty boundary read, saved preference and request input; it never authorizes execution. The only preview write is the int invalid-status zero-to-one transition.

# Lord defeat loot audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2` (installed DLL verified). The owning unit-state function is `FUN_18015a950`, RVA `0x15A950`, VA `0x18015A950`; its autogenerated function name is a candidate, while the reward instructions and branch bytes below were independently checked against the installed binary.

The state-machine path reaches the one-shot lord-death branch after an already marked death (`unit manager + unitId*0x490 + 0xA69 == 99`) has been excluded. The defeated player's one-based ID comes from the unit owner word loaded at RVA `0x15C44F` into R8. The credited winner's one-based ID comes from the unit kill-attribution word loaded at `0x15C458` into EBP. The player-record stride is `0x583C`, matching the installed Script Extender's `GamePlayerResources` view. `0x15C475` tests the winner ID. Its `JE` at `0x15C477` skips to `0x15CDC3` if no winner exists; the following `CMP` at `0x15C47D` and `JNE` at `0x15C487` skip the reward for the special unit flag. The surrounding death-state branches, including the separate `0x6E` path and non-lord processing, do not enter the reward block.

At `0x15C48D` the reward block starts. Gold is signed `r_TotalGoodsGold` (`GamePlayerResources + 0x50C`); Vanilla awards truncated 25% of the defeated player's gold, clamped to 500..100000, directly to the credited winner. Twenty goods totals are read from the defeated player's `r_TotalGoods*` table and truncated 25% is added to the winner's `r_incoming*` table (`+0x46C` base). The goods-notification flag is set only if a positive goods amount was credited. The reward branch then records award statistics, clears the defeated player's goods and rejoins death-state, animation and notification handling. The no-winner and special-flag paths rejoin the same downstream state handler at `0x15CDC3` without those awards. There is no separate managed reward dispatch in this path; the native simulation writes the gold and pending goods directly.

The first testmod hook at `0x15C477..0x15C487` jumped human winners to `0x15CDC3`. The in-game test confirmed that this suppresses gold but also skips loser-goods cleanup, the type-8 kill notification, the type-1 gold notification and the `FUN_18003F640` follow-up. That target is therefore unsuitable when the kill notification must remain.

The first in-game test on 2026-09-26 exposed a RedBird context-stub flag hazard: both human Rat defeats incremented the callback's suppression count, but the game still credited and announced 500 gold. The installed `RedBird.X64.dll` (assembly version `1.5.0.0`) runs `sub rsp,144` before `pushfq` captures `Rflags`, then runs `add rsp,144` after `popfq` restores them. Thus the context does not expose the earlier Vanilla flags, and a changed `Rflags` does not survive to a relocated conditional branch. A post-callback `TEST` is required. The second in-game test verified suppression of gold but no kill notification, exposing the overly broad skip described above.

The narrower entry at `0x15C4EA` follows the winner guards and the `INC BYTE [R10+RBP+0x27AD01]` victory counter at `0x15C4DB`. `RBX` and `R14` already contain the defeated one-based player ID, `R11=R14*0x160F`, and `R12D` contains the clamped gold award (minimum 500). Its exact RedBird span is two seven-byte instructions, `IMUL R10,RBP,0x160F` and `IMUL R13,RBP,0x583C`, ending at `0x15C4F8`; the first gold write is at `0x15C4FC`. No direct incoming edge into the span interior was found in the Ghidra reference export. For a human winner, set `RCX=moduleBase+0x366C210`, `R12D=0`, `RDX=0` and branch to `0x15C980`. For AI/error, set `RDX=1` and execute both displaced instructions. RDX is dead on the AI path until overwritten by `IMUL ECX` at `0x15C512`, and the human path overwrites it with `XOR EDX,EDX` at `0x15C980`. The cleanup uses RCX, R11, RBX and zero R12D, then sets R13 itself at `0x15C988`; later R12 is overwritten at `0x15CA7B` or `0x15CAB1`.

The installed RedBird 1.5.0.0 `X64InlineHook` generated an RIP-relative indirect `JMP [RIP]` for each stub continuation. The two copied-buffer probes and generated-stub checks passed before the 2026-09-26 build/install. This is an assembler contract observation, not an in-game behavior confirmation.

30 entries are complete instruction spans at least14 bytes, with no known DB xref into their displaced interiors. # Gatehouse damage and premature drawbridge destruction [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2. Static audit: 2026-10-13. Semantic function names remain candidate-level; the following byte/data flows were checked directly against this installed binary. This is not an in-game fix confirmation.

## Creation, target eligibility and damage

0x739C0 creates drawbridges through allocator 0xB47E0. Native building Game-IDs are one-based, sentinel-relative slots have stride 0x32C, and the public GameBuilding view starts at slot+0x5C. Allocator writes current/max Int16 health at slot+0x168/+0x16A from the four-byte default table at 0x2E7510. STRUCT_DRAWBRIDGE (49) defaults to zero HP; gate main/inner default to 2000/1000.

Damage eligibility table 0x2E6710 has entry zero for STRUCT_DRAWBRIDGE, one for both stone gatehouses. Both shared direct damage 0x7EB00 and area damage 0x7DF60 reject zero-health/ineligible buildings before subtraction. Target helpers 0xC2190/0xC2280 also reject ordinary drawbridge building targets; managed click handling 0x8C5F0 permits specialized unit attack paths separately. A siege projectile can therefore hit a bridge without damaging/removing the bridge. This describes unchanged Vanilla tables; foreign overrides can differ.

## Premature removal decision

0x7EB00 receives tile manager, tile ID, X, Y, damage, argument 6, source player, argument 8 and unit argument 9. Projectile handler 0x9C730, building fire 0xC60F0 and other non-direct paths pass argument 8=0. Recorded direct unit attack callers pass 1 (including the stack-form call in 0x160420). A source-player negative value can request alliance protection; damage is subtracted as signed-16 native health before the early bridge branch.

At 0x7EE62 the new HP is stored. At 0x7EE6B..0x7EE7E argument 8==1 and type STRUCT_GATE_MAIN/INNER select an early removal branch. This branch does NOT test the remaining HP. It uses adjacency helper 0xB9330 to find up to two live STRUCT_DRAWBRIDGE contacts and calls 0xC4290 on each. Only afterwards does 0x7F018/0x7F024 check positive HP and bypass normal destruction. Consequently a surviving gate can lose bridges on its first effective direct hit.

The later lethal gate branch already repeats coupled-bridge removal before gate removal. Area damage 0x7DF60 removes coupled bridges only in its lethal branch. Manual bulldoze 0x12400 separately removes up to two coupled bridges, validating the gate Global-ID. No extra bridge protection or restoration is required to correct the early branch.

## Coupling and terminal state

0xB9330 iterates footprint-perimeter contacts via 0xC0270, occupancy tile map and type/alive checks; owner parameter is not an ownership filter. It returns a positive one-based Building-ID, excludes the previous result for a second bridge, or returns zero. 0xC4290 sets slot+0x12C to removal state 3, updates removal presentation flags and can propagate shared compound-group removal. This is a state assignment, not immediate slot clearing.

0xC60F0 processes removal state 3 through 0xB8310. Removal releases workers/auxiliary state, calls tile restoration 0x61FC0, clears the record and invalidates pathfinding. Drawbridge-specific 0x622D0 clears bridge tile occupancy and restores moat/support representation; 0x61EF0 clears footprint properties/effects. Regular refresh/terrain semantics remain authoritative.

## Minimal correction boundary [mod integration]

The test correction inserts an additional positive-health guard before early removal, restricted to direct attacks on the two stone gate types. It keeps normal damage, notifications, lethal removal, area damage and demolition unchanged. Hook starts 0x7EE6B and displaces 4+6+5=15 bytes, continues at 0x7EE7A or skips to 0x7EF87. Full-function direct branches and exported incoming xrefs contain no target inside this span. Installed RedBird X64InlineHook uses max(minimum,14) and rounds to whole instructions; production generator is assembled/decoded and tested on private native fixtures.

Last observed save run: test_gates_v2.sav, 2026-10-13 15:27, recorded gate 163/global2560900 losing 6 HP (1000 to 994). Existing log alone does not prove which bridge removal was caused by this hit. At that point dedicated acceptance was pending; see the subsequent acceptance sections and historical documents retained under _inspect/DrawbridgeDestructionIntegration.

## First editor smoke test, 2026-10-13 [mod integration]

Process start section begins at LogOutput.log line 6667 (version-independent BepInEx start marker). Installed testmod 0.1.0 reports matching native hash, reference-rva resolution and 15-byte span at 16:30:35.979. Other mission consumers identify a new EditorCreated/MapEditor session at 16:30:49.251..397. At editor unload 16:31:32.352, the testmod reports entered=167, suppressed=166, diagnosticErrors=0. The user reports the fix behaved correctly in the editor. Native counters establish actual guard execution after startup; they count branch decisions, not individual bridges saved. The one unprotected entry is consistent with a lethal hit but cannot be classified from these counters alone.

Diagnostic coverage is incomplete: this editor session has no MAP, HOOK_CONFIRMED, DAMAGE_PRE/POST, NEXT_TICK or REMOVAL_FOLLOWUP marker. The observer's mapActive remains false because its OnStartMap/OnLoadSave registration misses creation of a new editor map. Therefore diagnosticErrors=0 does not validate the inactive capture path, and individual bridge identity preservation/terminal removal are unobserved. # Drawbridges: curated native contracts [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Date: 2026-09-17. Static contracts were checked against the canonical DLL; the resulting ExtraFeatures behavior was also verified in game. Editor placement and editor lifecycle are outside this document.

Detailed implementation history, failed approaches and live-process methodology: [Findings/Drawbridges.md](../../../../../Findings/Drawbridges.md).

## Height topology

- `DefaultHeightGrid` is image-relative at RVA `0x4E2B870` and manager-relative at `tileManager + 0xDCCAC0`. The mutable `HeightGrid` is manager-relative at `tileManager + 0xD7E5A0`.
- Vanilla moat depth is eight raw height values. Elevated moat and drawbridge tiles therefore use `max(defaultHeight - 8, 0)`. Drawbridges at default height `<=12` retain Vanilla height zero.
- Completed drawbridge creation uses the 17-byte block at RVA `0x73B35`; lowering uses the 15-byte block at RVA `0x64546`. Vanilla state update, image-base restoration, graphic refresh and pathfinding refresh remain authoritative.
- Removal and cancellation paths restore the tile's own `DefaultHeightGrid`; no building-wide constant replaces tile-local terrain restoration.

## Common building-height reference

- Building records use manager RVA `0x64CCBB0`, stride `0x32C`, and height field `+0x148`.
- The building creator at RVA `0x6D580` calculates the footprint midpoint from minimum and maximum height, forwards it through the drawbridge creator at RVA `0x739C0`, and the allocator at RVA `0xB47E0` writes it at RVA `0xB49DC`.
- This building height is the common rigid reference for all visual drawbridge parts and units. Tile-local `HeightGrid` remains the terrain/topology value and must not be substituted as the rigid visual reference on sloped footprints.

## Rendering paths

- Three distinct Vanilla paths contribute drawbridge graphics and all are required:
  - special renderer entry RVA `0x45820`, 19-byte hook span;
  - animated arguments RVA `0x43BA2`, 17-byte hook span;
  - static arguments RVA `0x44EDD`, 16-byte hook span.
- The special renderer receives the Building-ID in `EDX`; immediately after its prolog Vanilla sign-extends `EDX` and multiplies it by record stride `0x32C`. Its two direct calls are at RVAs `0x44E3C` and `0x44EC3`.
- For an elevated building height `H>12`, the special and animated paths apply the relative shift `-(H-8)`. The static path uses `shadow-H`. For `H<=12` or an inactive feature, the displaced Vanilla instructions execute unchanged.
- The apparently doubled chains observed during development were differently positioned Vanilla subparts, not duplicate custom render objects. No custom queue entries, sorting or replacement renderer are needed.

## Unit height

- The common unit-height writer starts at RVA `0x184FD0`; the drawbridge block at RVA `0x18511C` has a 19-byte hook span and continues at `0x18512F`.
- Vanilla stores current elevation at unit-slot anchor `+0x712` and vertical correction at `+0x714`. For elevated drawbridges the correction is `buildingHeight - currentElevation`; the resulting surface is therefore the same building height used by all rigid drawbridge parts. Low drawbridges retain Vanilla `8-currentElevation`.
- Type-2 sprite producers at RVAs `0x43EF3` and `0x44346` consume this correction. Type-52 interpolation forwards the already computed height at RVA `0x1A22C4`; separate movement, interpolation or sorting hooks are not required.

## Hook backend contract [mod integration]

- Installed RedBird.X64 is `1.1.0`; installed Iced is `1.21.0`.
- RedBird's requested hook size is a minimum. The verified displaced byte counts for the six drawbridge hooks are `17`, `15`, `19`, `17`, `16`, and `19` bytes in the order creation, lowering, special renderer, animated renderer, static renderer, and unit correction.
- Productive generators are assembled and fully decoded in the internal test project. Hook publication is atomic and fail-closed; missing, mutated or ambiguous native signatures prevent the complete Elevated-Moat transaction from being published.

## Scope boundary

These contracts establish runtime drawbridge height, rendering, unit placement, refresh and restoration behavior for the stated binary hash. They do not establish editor-mode placement permissions or editor lifecycle behavior.

## Blueprint view contract (2026-10-07) [mod integration]

Installed native and managed hashes were rechecked: native `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`, managed `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`. The following is a static rendering audit and asset inspection. On 2026-10-07 the user confirmed that the installed correction works in game; this confirmation does not establish which camera/terrain combinations were individually exercised.

- Creation `0x6D580` dispatches drawbridges to `0x739C0`; allocator `0xB47E0` stores tile X/Y at building-relative `+0x14A/+0x14C`, footprint size at `+0x154`, and the orientation argument at `+0x15E`. Native records are sentinel-relative, one-based Building-IDs, stride `0x32C`. Invalid map coordinates and exhausted allocation return zero. The creation path writes the ordered footprint occupancy and refreshes graphics/pathfinding through `0x6CDD0/0x725E0`.
- `0x6CDD0` selects drawbridge render-anchor cells for all four camera quarters. `0xA5E20` clears the previous subpart frames and calculates `(buildingOrientation - cameraRotation + 8) % 8` for negative differences; valid cardinal views are `0/2/4/6`. Open, raising, raised and lowering states use that same view index; state transitions do not derive orientation from height. Gate-adjacency lookup `0xB9330` chooses alternate static supports in two views and returns zero when no eligible live gate is found.
- Tile renderer `0x41D60` routes the drawbridge to the special/animated path `0x45820` and static path `0x4C1D0`, with flattened-view and tile-render flags controlling visibility. `0x19D110` publishes the selected frames, offsets and transform fields into the sprite queue. Height shifts affect placement, not the view choice. Function names in the semantic index remain candidate names; these specific branches and field flows were inspected directly in the current export.
- Managed `GameMap.mapGameTileToTilemapCoord` applies the current North/East/South/West camera transform before isometric cell projection. Blueprint direction must use these planar cell centers; adding terrain or flattened-view heights before comparing bridge and gate can reverse the vertical sign on slopes. The visual ground-height path remains separate.
- CastlePlanner's bundled `DrawbridgeFront` PNG is canonical BottomRight; `DrawbridgeRear` is canonical TopLeft. Mirror the front for BottomLeft and the rear for TopRight. Composite and depth captures resolve through `BlueprintBuildingCaptureCatalog`; the fallback catalog shares the same mirror mapping. Unknown adjacency retains the existing unresolved-image behavior.
- Retained regression coverage: `Helpers/AIVParser/AIVParser.Tests/Program.cs` tests both gate sizes, A/B axes, both bridge sides and all 16 castle/camera combinations per fixture against frozen expected screen directions and the audited managed projection. `_inspect/Test-CastlePlannerDrawbridgePreflight.ps1` checks that runtime direction cannot consume terrain/flattened height, and that the two library readers share the capture request. No native hook, executable patch, Script Extender source change or new game API is needed.

Validation on 2026-10-07: all 39 AIVParser test groups passed, including 128 gate/castle/camera fixtures; all 98 CastlePlanner test groups passed. JSON/lifecycle, persistent publishers, XAML, enum source/assembly parity, planar-direction and workspace executable-mutation checks passed. The runtime build reported zero warnings/errors. Installation used CastlePlanner/build.bat; local and installed CastlePlanner.dll match SHA-256 BF8BCA1EEEA3000F844F3837F24785E0985C9A19B588C028BF698E80276EDA6C. This initial validation build used version 0.8.36; automated fixture success does not claim a live four-view visual check.

Release acceptance on 2026-10-07: the user confirmed the fix works and requested the version increase to 0.8.37. Plugin and package versions are advanced together; the historical 0.8.36 changelog remains intact.

# Editor map lifecycle audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Managed SHA-256: BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Script Extender: 2.6.0, commit 2cee24e33b5a5d81d1c275efabc714ac59917b7b,
tree 9cfb59b7b531553b23709b90b3cc3f10b0615cc1. Installed assembly independently inspected.

## Native and managed contract

- `DLL_PreInitMap_Editor`, RVA 0x85E90, confirmed export/PInvoke: `(int mapSize, int mapType, byte siegeThat, byte multiplayerMap, byte* retData)`. Initializes a blank native editor map and sets the output errorCode to 1. `EngineInterface.newMapEditor` passes siegeThat=false, gets colour mapping and increments the returned mapRotation. `EditorDirector.createNewMap` then initializes GameData, GameMap, scenario UI, simulation and one-based player ID 1 before returning. Its managed success branch is `!siege_that || initData.errorCode == 1`; the current native export always initializes errorCode=1.
- `EngineInterface.LoadMapFile` first calls that SAME preinitializer with `(160,0,false,false)`, then `DLL_LoadSaveGame` at RVA 0x853F0 (confirmed export/PInvoke). Its arguments are UTF-16 bytes, signed int BYTE length, output struct pointer, and editor byte flag. Native failure returns 0; success returns 1 and sets output errorCode=1. `EditorDirector.loadMapIntoEditor` only performs subsequent managed editor initialization when that errorCode equals 1, returning true afterwards. `SaveCustomTrailMap` can call the lower EngineInterface loader without starting an interactive editor session.
- Reset functions RVA 0x87D10 and 0x5BC70 and archive reader RVA 0x87D0 have baseline confidence candidate. Their pseudocode was followed for reset/load/abort flow. 0x5BC70 is independently confirmed as the installed Extender unload pattern target. Both exported editor paths call it repeatedly (also through 0x87D10); these are internal teardown notifications, not completed editor sessions.
- The installed Extender's OnStartMap patterns uniquely resolve to RVA 0x94350 (skirmish), 0x8AE80 (non-skirmish), 0x87C40 (campaign). None is reachable in the baseline direct-call graph from the two editor exports. OnLoadMap wraps DLL_LoadMapToPlay. OnLoadSave wraps DLL_LoadSaveGame; Post occurs BEFORE the outer managed editor initialization.
- MapEditorR3EventHooks contains editing/placement events only, not a session-ready event. Current managed Extender hooks have no equivalent editor lifecycle completion signal.
- MainViewModel.InitNewScene(MapEditor) sets IsMapEditorMode and calls GoToScreen(ActualMainGame). Options return before changing screens. Other scene transitions can leave IsMapEditorMode stale: actual screen and flag must be considered together. Native editor preinit alone, a mode-flag edge, and simulation start alone do not establish a complete interactive editor session.
- The first GameData.lastGameState arrives later through setGameState; it is explicitly cleared inside editor initialization. Complete managed initialization does not imply first PlayState/render/building readiness.

## Workspace integration [mod integration]

The editor-only public contract below is historical. It has been superseded by the [unified mission lifecycle](MISSION_LIFECYCLE.md); the native/editor findings above remain applicable.

APIShared owns managed hooks around createNewMap/loadMapIntoEditor and captures newMapEditor's output for creation success. It observes actual GoToScreen transitions and external unloads, suppressing nested unloads within its operation scope. It publishes one Ready per successful operation and one Ended per retired ready session. A failed replacement leaves no active session; late observers replay only a currently ready session.

Shared.GameplaySessionLifecycle translates those notifications into EditorCreated/EditorLoaded, with no fabricated MapStartEventArgs or save restoration. It updates the per-assembly activation gate before feature callbacks. Feature-specific readiness and editor-player changes remain local. Runtime evidence from an actual game session is still required; this document records static analysis, not a live test.

# Editor terrain changes and stale path regions [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Observation: 2026-10-26. Native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Managed SHA-256 `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
The native function names remain candidate database labels unless otherwise noted;
the described writes/gates are confirmed static machine facts, not GUI acceptance.

## Mutation and consumption

The confirmed export `DLL_MapAction` (0x85BD0) maps editor moat actions 106/107
to internal actions 45/44. Input handler 0x90CD0 chooses width 3, or 5 with Shift;
this is independent of the selectable landscape brush. It queues Chore 21 with
property 0x40000000 and operation 2 (direct completed placement) or 3 (removal).
Handler 0x111D0 calls 0x6FE90 with player, packed tile, Y, footprint, property and
operation. The ordinary landscape dispatcher 0x92FF0 reaches the same handler
for terrain type changes, including water.

0x6FE90 checks accepted cells, writes flags/height and (where applicable) moat
records, then calls the confirmed 3x3 edge updater 0xD90D0 at 0x7094D. Neither
the generic terrain writer nor the 3x3 edge updater marks context+0x6C dirty.
The latter's terminal global write is the separate building/render notification
at 0x67E6424, not the component dirty flag. Terrain clearing 0x7AE50 also updates
edges without directly setting component dirty. Texture-only branches may omit
the 3x3 update. They must not be inferred to be topology-free: clearing previous
terrain can also change passability.

Height preset 0x6FA10, numeric/shape height 0x70DF0, raise/lower 0x6C0F0 and
equalize 0x64700 have separate accepted-cell guards and deferred terrain work.
No blanket assertion that all of these fail is made. Vegetation placement
0x6E2C0 and the vegetation-removal branch of editor deletion 0x62AB0 mark the
component grid dirty. Completed digging 0x639C0, filling 0x69470 and ordinary
building placement 0x6D580 likewise set dirty. This explains why placing a wall
can cause old water/moat topology to become visible to path-region consumers;
the original hover-only explanation was withdrawn by the reproducer.

The real rebuild 0xE49D0 takes `(pathContext*, int force)` and returns int 0/1.
Nonzero force writes dirty=1 and resets the countdown. With force=0 a countdown
and dirty=0 can independently skip work; waiting does not repair an unmarked
edit. A completed flood increments context+0x74, clears dirty and republishes
the UInt16 PCL grid, component counts and gate-related processing. Equal stale
nonzero PCLs immediately succeed in the confirmed query 0xE2610. Do not replace
that valid fast path; repair the publication of the input regions instead.

## Safe consumer boundary and limits [mod integration]

The real public `EditorDirector.preDLLCallActions(ref int, ref int)` is called
exactly once inside `EngineInterface.run(bool)`'s existing private threadLock,
before `DLL_RunTick` and its cursor dispatcher 0x8C5F0. A managed postfix can
consume prior completed edits there, including while the native game clock is
paused. Editor lifecycle must come from APIShared's managed completion service.

The consumer uses existing SE Post events for terrain, height, deletion and
vegetation. Post means the native call returned, not that any cell was accepted;
conservative no-op requests are allowed and coalesced. The event's BrushSize
label is not a reliable semantic guide for the generic terrain delegate: its
second native argument is the player, and the actual footprint is argument five.
The correction deliberately does not interpret that payload.

Live calls through 0xE49D0 preserve the existing command-runtime repair guard.
No second native detour is installed. A changed generation since the latest edit
plus clean dirty marker proves Vanilla completed the pending batch; a clean marker
alone or a rebuild preceding a later unmarked edit does not.

## Release batching (2026-10-26) [mod integration]

The user confirmed the initial editor correction works. The follow-up efficiency
change defers its own dirty request as well as its forced rebuild until Mouse0 is
released. Native E49D0 checks dirty independently from its countdown, so merely
delaying the forced call while still setting dirty would retain avoidable Vanilla
rebuild requests during continuous drawing. Native or foreign dirty writers and
forced calls remain untouched.

Confirmed-static managed input chain: EditorDirector.Update reads physical primary
button down/held/up and produces its separate engine mouse state. Its preparation
method consumes that state, performs held painting and a final release placement;
the native Chore can complete later during DLL_RunTick. Consequently a late real
edit must remain pending even after a release-triggered rebuild.

KeyManager.Update independently advances its own key states and filters them for
Noesis keyboard capture; the SE raises down/held/up events after that method. These
events are not a reliable sole physical release boundary for terrain brushes.
The correction instead samples physical input in a permanent EditorDirector.Update
prefix only while edits are pending, atomically tagged with their batch. New work
starts unknown, held work returns before engine-side map reads, focus loss ends
deferral and focus regain requires resampling. The existing locked pre-cursor
boundary remains the only place where the correction invalidates/rebuilds regions.
No new native hooks or public APIs are required. Runtime cost savings from this
batching still require actual continuous-drawing measurements in a DEVDIAG build.

Tests execute the unchanged canonical 0xE49D0 and 0xE2610 in private image memory
with explicit flag/edge graph inputs and a fixture replacement for memory fill.
This proves flood/gate/query behavior, not execution of every editor tool or GUI
input. Actual water/moat cursor acceptance, continuous drawing and gameplay
latency remain separate in-game checks. See `BugfixesAndQoL/Test-EditorRegions.ps1`.

## Confirmed weighted-route bypass and compatibility correction

LogOutput.log, map session 1 at 20:58:48--20:59:26: 15 target-bearing Assassin builder calls returned native 0 and weighted 1. Sessions 3--5 reported weighted-disabled; user observed alternative paths with the improvement disabled. Session 2 had no materialized gate-policy violation; its physical conditions are not inferred from the unchanged topology fingerprint. Negative-destination flood-field returns of zero are not treated as target-route failures.
