Its complete body/write contract remains in UNIT_COMMAND_PROBE_SCRATCH.md:
manager+98/C0/C4 (three int32) restore in finally for query-only use. Equal positive
regions avoid a query; other answers are reused only for a single command and key.
A positive macro answer is not a proof of a tile route or movement permission.

The new batch is prepared before queue and formation mutation. Ordinary groups
with unsupported moat, Assassin, structure/exit or active-provider contexts keep
existing routing. Shift insertion is identified by a read-only queue predicate;
admission runs when its waypoint executes. All-excluded commands skip 11B520 and
never open queue/formation completion scopes. Player-wrapper +56C is restored for
that rejected invocation, with nested frame ownership preventing parent rollback.
Mixed groups enter 118E00 once and the native stamped exclusion table skips writes
to excluded identities. Topology invalidation disables the current mask; stale
parents cannot reactivate it on nested return. No tribe membership is rewritten.

Formation protocol 7 retains full ordered selection identity with a separate hash.
Canonical execution filters members before slot generation, preserving direction,
density and intended width. Its execution plan hash includes the selected identity
and admitted subset. A filtered plan is generated in synchronized simulation;
the sender's full-selection preview plan cannot authorize it. Missing preview
slots do not block native dispatch. Observed rejection/partial execution consumes
the input once instead of replaying the entire group. Multiplayer acceptance
requires matching builds on both peers; mixed protocol builds are not validated.

Production-source fixtures exercise actual admission, formation and dispatch code.
The real generated X64InlineHook is executed against destructive order/path writes,
checking unchanged old state for exclusions, thread/tribe/generation/global-ID
guards, ABI/flags, and 100/200/550/1000 members. Harness timings exclude the engine
and real E2610 and must not be reported as in-game command latency.

# Dry mixed-group movement recovery [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Historical implementation: superseded on 2026-10-26 by
[pre-mutation group admission](MANUAL_GROUP_ADMISSION.md). The dated findings and
original proof limitations below are retained as historical evidence.

Observed 2026-10-25 against installed native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Names other than E2610 retain candidate confidence; the following control/data-flow
findings are confirmed-static, not game acceptance.

## Native flow

The input/Chore chain is in MOVE_COMMAND_RELEASE.md. Group dispatcher 11B520 reads
the one-based leader ID (tribe record +5A, stride 688), its current PCL and the
target PCL. Ordinary cross-region movement obtains group mode from 117C70 and
calls E2610(player, source, destination, mode). Zero leads to E9D90/E9FF0
structure-exit checks; failure returns zero before per-member moves. A dry leader
enclosed by moat can block members already in the target ground component. The
cursor's 18E1E0 witness is independent and cannot seed simulation ownership.

Native fallback 118E00 writes group waypoint/patrol fields and enumerates members
through 119F90. It retains its own native life/kill/state/capability predicates
before calling 196280. It is not equivalent to issuing terminal moves directly
to captured units. 196280 normalizes its start, checks member regions/portals and
only then constructs the actual path. Positive macro reachability is not movement
permission; FORMATION_MOVEMENT_PERMISSION.md still applies.

## Macro query write closure

Full E2610 body: RVA E2610, 1589 bytes, SHA-256
`7F875ED003B5E0A047F394632F0F2F952D4364DCC9DD8C9A62D179441B39A0ED`.
All 347 instructions were decoded directly from the installed PE. The only call
is the security-cookie checker. Apparent r11 writes at E271D/E2725 address the
local stack array established by `lea r11,[rbp+230]` at E26B9.

The entire non-stack write set is three int32 values in manager RVA 60AD660:
+C4 counter (E2660), +C0 search state (E2747/E297E/E2996), +98 fallback state
(RIP writes E298A/E29A5/E2C29 all target 60AD6F8). All other stores are stack
locals. The query does not touch tile distance/stamp grids, packed paths or
terrain. It traverses connection records using exact player/diplomacy/building
and connection-mode inputs. Equal positive regions need no query. Mode is the
native signed value, not an unconditional default ladder mode.

The constructor's full hash gate binds this closure. Recovery also validates
representative writer bytes and the existing GameUnit mode offset. No semantic
fallback is claimed on unknown DLLs. Query-only calls restore +98/+C0/+C4 in
finally, including exceptions; real simulation queries keep their side effects.

## Consumer ordering and limits [mod integration]

Extender BulkTribeDetours raises Post after 11B520 and returns its ReturnValue.
Post has original inputs; a retained Pre object has final effective inputs.
Recovery rejects changed/vetoed inputs and requires matching effective early
rejection, zero group result and no previous member movement event. It is limited
to human dry-ground commands, unchanged leader identity/location, map/tick/revision
and command sequence. A later nested order invalidates the older recovery. Attack,
work, moat-start, special and planner scopes cannot provide this proof.

Recovery precedes frame clearing, queue Post and formation Post. A local scan
first seeks a same-target-region member; otherwise each distinct (player, source,
destination, signed mode) is queried once, stopping at the first witness. There is
no cursor cache, full probe, synthetic Chore, membership mutation, new hook,
new moat-placement batch or terminal-move loop. ObserveCommonGroupMove preserves
the existing native/formation integration. Native refusals remain authoritative;
a failed/throwing replacement is never retried.

Evidence: `.work/a/manual-region/001`. FriendlyMoatMovement.Tests executes actual
production recovery/observation with native boundaries doubled, checks the full
installed function fingerprint and guards Post integration timing. 100/200/550
members require zero full probes, zero extra graph queries on successful originals
or same-region witnesses, and at most one per distinct queried key. Actual game
latency, editor behavior and real host/client acceptance remain separate.

# Native market price query contract

Audited 2026-10-10 against CURRENT native SHA-256
FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Installed RedBird.Backends.NativeX64 SHA-256:
0843DD4C381A3E77DD6D8B51D5CCF95465B3FB49BFDF2980F39A212D774AADB0.

- Buy: RVA CEB10, 31 bytes, full function SHA-256
  5B45784D8B227D4BEB1AA822E6B12523BD9A0825EFA17764909A037E613C6C6A.
- Sell: RVA CEB90, 31 bytes, full function SHA-256
  D428FAE5C2A3BED0B48195B2661F56550E5B53F6E8EE9A603FADA56DAEE8F670.
- ABI: int(void* manager, int playerId, int good, int amount), RCX/EDX/R8D/R9D,
  signed EAX result. The helper does not read playerId. Good is sign-extended into
  RAX, indexing an eight-byte price pair at manager+1817B8 (buy) or +1817BC (sell).
  It computes signed (basePrice / 5) * amount, truncating division before unchecked
  Int32 multiplication. No native side effects occur inside either helper.

Complete audited callers:

| RVA | Meaning and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| 29650 | Buy execution: goods addition succeeds before gold/stat deduction and bookkeeping. |
| 3EC90 | AI planned-goods affordability: the same buy price must agree with 29650 execution. |
| 29700 | Sale execution: gold/stat update, goods removal and bookkeeping. |
| D78C0 | Ally goods transfer/request path: sell price feeds sender/receiver statistics. |
| D7AD0 | Ally delivery path: gold handled directly; other goods use sell valuation and update both statistics. |

These are native price queries, not general player-trade events or transaction
acknowledgements. Replacing a price does not cancel the surrounding caller. In
particular, replacing/vetoing with zero changes valuation/cost rather than aborting
a purchase. Consumer policies must remain deterministic and consistent across
planning, execution and ally valuation on every multiplayer peer.

Current semantic xrefs contain zero incoming targets into either complete helper
interior. The two functions have one straight-line block with a final return and no
internal branches. Exact full bytes are checked against the installed file and live
entry. APIShared 0.6 owns both helpers, and consumer AI classification stays private.

Only the installed NativeX64 NativeDetour Indirect schema is accepted. It requires
six patch bytes, extends to ten bytes (MOVSXD 3 + table MOV 7), and resumes at +10,
the five-byte MOV EAX,66666667. FollowJumps=false; no alternate schema is attempted.
After commit and before publication, validate Scheme, DisplacedByteCount,
TargetAddress, ChainDepth, FF25 patch, NOP padding, pointer slot, hook entry,
relocated bytes, trampoline jump to +10 and untouched remaining helper bytes.
Private executable fixtures use the productive backend and validator, invoke the
actual native ABI over signed/overflow cases and exercise changed-continuation
rejection. They are not X64InlineHook probes. Published runtime hooks and static
roots remain for the process; only an unpublished failed transaction can roll back.

The Script Extender 2.14.1 and canonical Fixes v1.26.3 source searches found no owner
of these two helper entries. Occupied entries or unknown native hashes fail closed.
Evidence and caller exports are retained in .inspect/APISharedHookAudit. This is a
static/backend contract audit; no interactive host/client gameplay run is asserted.

# Unified mission lifecycle audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Managed SHA-256: BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Installed Script Extender 2.6.0; canonical fork commit 2cee24e33b5a5d81d1c275efabc714ac59917b7b,
tree 9cfb59b7b531553b23709b90b3cc3f10b0615cc1. No fork changes or additional native detours.

## Audited boundaries

- `DLL_LoadMapToPlay` RVA 0x84AC0 (confirmed export) dispatches campaign initialization (0x87C40), ordinary mission initialization (0x8AE80), skirmish initialization (0x94350), trail routing (0x28960), and tutorial initialization (0x100530). The three initializer addresses match the installed Extender's OnStartMap targets; internal implementation names remain candidate-level where the database has not confirmed semantics.
- Successful native initializers return low 32 bits 0xFFFFFFFF. Campaign errors -11/-21, ordinary reader failure 1, and skirmish reader failure 0 are not success. The enclosing loader can normalize negative results to errorCode=1; a failed inner initializer therefore vetoes an otherwise successful outer result. Tutorial uses its separate route and is not required to emit OnStartMap.
- Save loader 0x853F0 succeeds with native return 1 and output errorCode=1. It restores native state without normal new-game startup. Multiplayer restoration also enters the skirmish initializer with the save byte set; consumers must not infer a new game from the existence of an OnStartMap callback.
- Reset 0x87D10 and unload 0x5BC70 are repeatedly nested in preinitializers/loaders. The unload target is independently confirmed by the installed Extender pattern; internal function names remain candidate confidence. Reader 0x87D0 returns zero for invalid input. Repeated unloads do not constitute repeated completed sessions.
- `DLL_PreInitMap_Multiplayer` RVA 0x86270 (confirmed export/PInvoke) receives byte skirmish flag, signed Int32 restart byte length and byte pointer, signed Int32 coop trail/mission, and byte test/custom/extreme flags. It resets via 0x87D10/0x8ADC0 and stores coop trail at RVA 0x366A090 and mission at 0x366A094 unchanged. Frontend selection 21..24 maps to native trail 1..4; the UI's one-based mission is decremented in `CoopMissionChanged`. StartGame and the local StartSkirmishGame pass the resulting zero-based mission unchanged. Capture the managed preinitializer arguments; the shared skirmish entry alone cannot distinguish standard local Coop from custom games.
- `LoadMapReturnData.siege_or_invasion` is serialized 0=Siege, 1=Invasion, 2=Economy, 3=FreeBuild. `GameData.Init` explicitly converts this to `Enums.GameModes`; these enum numeric values are not interchangeable. `coopMissionID`, `skirmishTrailLevel` and campaign `mission_level` retain native zero-based indices. Game player IDs are one-based.

## Managed completion and retirement [mod integration]

Interactive roots: EditorDirector creation/editor load/campaign/trail/custom trail/save, FRONT_StandaloneMission.StartMap, FRONT_Multiplayer.StartSkirmishGame/RestartSkirmishGame, HUD_Tutorial.StartTutorial, Platform_Multiplayer.StartGame/StartSave. Nested custom-trail/skirmish calls belong to one attempt. Editor creation observes newMapEditor output, editor loading requires both native success and the outer bool success. Lower LoadMapFile exports without an interactive root create no mission.

`postLoading` returns after GameData/GameMap/UI initialization but the enclosing root still performs player assignment, colour mapping and other setup. OnStart waits for the outer normal return. Clients waiting for the random seed complete in the main-thread `processMessage` packet-2 path after postLoading and its subsequent setup. Repeated messages have no waiting operation to complete. An operation ID retired by replacement cannot become current again. Simulation start is later (packet 4) and is not guaranteed by OnStart.

`MainViewModel.GoToScreen` and direct `FatControler.NewScene` are observed after their actual screen state changes. Options bypass scene replacement. HUD win/lose presentation is not departure. The Extender's HUD exit hook publishes a synthetic Unload Pre with a null pointer; this is logical retirement even without a native Unload Post. An editor flag can survive departure and is not session evidence.

## Public and Shared contract [mod integration]

`IMissionLifecycleCapability` supersedes the editor-specific API completely. Context and notifications are immutable; process-local attempt IDs are monotonic. Initialization phases never replay. Only a current, fully managed-ready session replays. End includes last captured context, last reached phase, reason and whether Start occurred. Observer and diagnostic exceptions are isolated; Vanilla delegates execute once. Unpublished failed hook candidates are rolled back; published services remain process-rooted.

Mode classification and the existing regular-mod/feature permission tables are defined once in APIShared. Shared's per-assembly adapter updates the gate before feature subscribers. Lobby network authority remains available outside a mission without permitting gameplay. Startup resources exclude save/editor/replay. Save persistence, player switching and actual building/HUD/render readiness remain separate contracts.

Legacy Customize-origin fields retain their provider schema: Custom Trail IDs 81..92 and one-based mission IDs; Coop provider trail IDs 0..3 and mission IDs 1..10; built-in Vanilla/Sands mission IDs are zero-based. These fields describe provenance, whereas `MissionContext.MissionIndex` consistently uses a known zero-based position. Absent evidence does not invent an index.

## Evidence and limits

The user's prior ElevatedMoat editor test and the last inspected log establish one Created session, one End and one Loaded session in the preceding editor implementation (19:26:24.494, 19:26:40.977, 19:26:44.671). They do not validate this later unified implementation. Two preceding Ally-Goods/ExtendedData errors are outside this lifecycle change.

Automated validation and final build results are recorded in `_inspect/MissionLifecycleValidation/RESULTS.md`. Game validation of the new implementation, particularly real multiplayer host/client and mission-specific features, remains a separate required observation. No live coverage is inferred from state-machine or boundary-double tests.

## Current PlayState readiness (2026-10-21)

For native hash FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2
and rechecked installed managed hash BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789,
`EngineInterface.CopyPlayStateStruct` constructs a new `PlayState` object;
`GameMap.processTestMap` passes the copied state to `GameData.setGameState`, which
replaces `lastGameState`. A managed mission Start notification is not proof that this
render-buffer publication has happened for that mission. Castle preview captures
the previous reference at BeforeNativeStart and waits for a nonnull replacement
before interpreting spectator flags or authorizing a personal selection. This avoids
classifying a new human game from an earlier spectator save's state. The evidence is
the hash-bound managed export for those three methods and the current installed
assembly's public member metadata. The consumer readiness/deadline regression is an
isolated test; current-game rendering and network timing still require game acceptance.

# Moat terrain restoration [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Observation: 2026-10-25. Canonical native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
The function names in the database remain candidate symbols; the following particular
machine writes, branches and register contracts are confirmed statically against the
installed image. This is not in-game or multiplayer acceptance.

## Soil and terminal states

The native tile manager is at module `+0x405EDB0`. Its `Logic2Grid` is a byte per
packed tile at manager `+0x9D2500`, separate from logic flags `+0x898400`, height
`+0xD7E5A0`, default height `+0xDCCAC0` and structure IDs `+0xB0BCA0`. The physical
capacity is 320800. `TileType.OasisGrass` is bit `0x10`; the complete original byte
must be retained, rather than inferring grass from neighboring cells or recording
only that bit. Native readers also distinguish foliage, sand, height-edge and stone bits.

`0x639C0(manager, taskIndex)` increments the byte progress of a 16-byte moat record.
Only its completed branch (progress >=4) reaches `0x63A4E`: task state becomes 0x0204,
height becomes zero, planned/pitch flags are cleared, completed moat is set, and
`0x63A9F` explicitly writes soil zero. Task-index callers from all ten audited unit
handlers share this branch. `0x69470(manager, taskIndex)` decrements progress; positive
progress returns without removal. At <=0 it restores height 8, clears completed moat,
invalidates/rebuilds path data and removes the task through `0x61E70`. It never restores
the original soil. A resource-visual update can follow if a building occupies the tile.

`0x6FE90` iterates accepted brush cells. Its moat operation numbers are 0 plan,
1 cancel plan, 2 immediate completed placement, 3 direct removal. Modes 2/3 pass the
soil-zero writer `0x705BF`; mode 2 allocates through `0x59210` afterwards, so a hook
only on task creation would already observe the erased byte. `0x70940` is reached
after the accepted mutation and before the unchanged 3x3 update call. It is also used
by non-moat terrain operations; these represent explicit replacement, not restoration.
Some texture-only paints skip that update block, and require the accepted texture
commit at `0x7082E`. The editor's `0x7AE50` clear operation deliberately replaces soil
with zero/height-edge bits and must invalidate history, including when invoked as
preparation for another paint by `0x6FE90`.

## Bridges and replacement

`0x6D580` validates a building request before iterating its footprint. At `0x6D8DF`,
`RBX=tileManager`, `ESI=packed tile`, `R12D=native building struct type` (drawbridge 0x31).
It deletes prior moat tasks and clears the moat/planned bits before dispatching to
drawbridge creation `0x739C0`. That function writes the bridge occupancy and recreates
tasks with `0x59210`. Therefore capture/preservation has to precede the cleanup, and
the later allocation must not replace the retained origin with the current dirt.
The native bridge mapper selects its underlying moat cells; other footprint cells
also need origins because bridge removal ORs soil bit 2 on non-moat footprint cells.

`0x622D0` may remove a bridge while keeping a completed moat underneath. Its later
soil OR-2 path follows the existing height-restoration block. `0x6240E` is after the
last soil write but before structure occupancy is cleared. Remaining completed moat
retains its origin. `0x6CA30` purges the bridge footprint and its `0x6CADD` block is
after task/flag cleanup. `0xED2E0` area removal reaches `0xEDA8C` after the moat flag
and height writers and before later region/3x3 publication.

Filling a moat under a surviving bridge can finish before the bridge disappears.
Restoring soil at filling completion must retain the bridge's origin until a later
bridge demolition, otherwise the OR-2 writer can again change the restored soil.
An old untracked moat or lowered bridge is not a source of historical information.

Ordinary building preparation invalidates history. `0x5D740` is another accepted
replacement path, and vegetation creation/update `0x108320/0x109930` can clear moat
state after allocating or updating vegetation. Their committed replacement branches
invalidate history rather than repainting the new object.

## Ownership, persistence and evidence [mod integration]

BugfixesAndQoL's private native stubs own only the disjoint soil/capture spans listed
in its `MoatTerrain/NativeDefinition.cs`. ExtraFeatures retains its height hooks;
command-runtime task entry detours remain authoritative. The native-site registry
records the new exclusive spans. No new APIShared interception API is introduced.

The map-scoped ushort buffer is mod memory: planned, dug, bridge and transient direct
placement states are distinct. It never occupies spare Vanilla record fields. Only
persistent, still-relevant entries reach schema-1 `BugfixesAndQoL.MoatTerrain` via
APIShared VersionedSaveData, with map/save scope and simulation-relevant comparison.
Disabled loading discards known history. Unknown future records retain APIShared's
opaque preservation rules and cannot activate this mission's restoration.

The real `EngineInterface.SaveSaveGame` holds its private static `threadLock` around
`DLL_SaveSaveGame` (also for map saves). The mod resolves this existing object once by
validated reflection for lifecycle/save coordination; it adds no lock in native tile
paths. Missions arm after managed initialization and retire/reset through APIShared.

Retained evidence: `.work/a/moat-terrain/001` (18 complete instruction streams,
canonical byte comparisons and feature bodies); compiled-site audit and executable
production tests in `BugfixesAndQoL/tests/MoatTerrain.Tests`. The audit resolves
CURRENT.json and the current database manifest, checks whole function bytes,
instruction-aligned spans, incoming interior xrefs and own overlap. Fixtures execute
the production operations/emitter and use the installed RedBird backend on private
memory; external refresh/call destinations are explicit fixture boundaries.
Game visuals, actual farm placement and real multiplayer remain untested.

Release ownership review, 2026-10-27 [mod integration]: the installed RedBird
transaction activates patches during its default Commit and disposes owned hooks
on Dispose. The terrain owner now explicitly prepares without activation, retains
its buffer after save registration or the first attempted Enable, and publishes
readiness only after all installed-span checks. Initialization failures after either
publication boundary keep the feature logically disabled and retain all resources.
This changes no Vanilla bytes, native spans or terrain/persistence semantics above.

# Modsettings activation: peace time and No Dogs [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Observation: 2026-10-22. Native SHA-256:
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Read together with [VANILLA_PEACE_TIME](VANILLA_PEACE_TIME.md).
This records verified native behavior and isolated feasibility checks, not an installed fix.

## No Dogs: complete relevant state and decision chain

The confirmed export `DLL_IsMapperAvailable` at RVA `84A20` passes the mapper ID
from ECX to EDX, sets RCX to the mapper manager at image RVA `32C7730`, and
tail-jumps to `FFC70`. The latter has a fully decoded 889-byte body; its generic
`FUN_1800ffc70` name is still a candidate semantic label, not a public API identity.
It is a leaf function with a manager pointer and unsigned mapper ID. It also
implements scenario/content restrictions, signed short availability entries at
manager + `22C` + mapper * 2, special mapper entries and table branches.
The installed Extender enum confirms `MAPPER_DOG_CAGE = 0x138`.

For that mapper only, the relevant path is:

| RVA | Original action |
| --- | --- |
| `FFD87` | Compare mapper with `0x138`; other mappers branch to their own restrictions |
| `FFD8F` / `FFD92` | Test game mode in R10D; mode 0 bypasses the NoDogs restriction |
| `FFD94` | Compare R10D with 99 |
| `FFD98` | `74 31`: mode 99 bypasses to `FFDCB` |
| `FFD9A` | Compare active NoDogs int at image RVA `37EF964` with zero |
| `FFDA1` | Zero continues ordinary availability |
| `FFDA3` | Nonzero returns zero (unavailable) |

The current BugfixesAndQoL replacement is exactly two NOPs at `FFD98`, so it
removes only the mode-99 bypass. It does not remove the earlier mode-0 bypass,
change the setting, spawn/remove dogs, or change other mapper paths.

Managed setup provenance, checked against the hash-matched managed baseline:
`FRONT_Multiplayer` toggles `MultiplayerSetupData.no_dogs`; `setMPSetup` copies it
to the transfer struct. `setMultiplayerStartingData` serializes the struct and
calls confirmed export `DLL_ApplyMultiplayerSetupData` (`81050`). It tail-jumps to
`26370`, whose writes at `263D4/263D7` copy int at transfer offset `24` to
manager + `279FB8`. The manager is image RVA `8574320`, making the setup global
`87EE2D8`. The reverse export `DLL_GetMultiplayerSetupData` (`84280`) reaches
`20420`, which reads that field and writes transfer offset `24`.
This agrees with Extender `ChoreManagerOptionsInternal.NoDogs` offset 2596792.

Preinitialization (`DLL_PreInitMap_Multiplayer`, `86270`) sets native mode 99 for
the skirmish boolean and mode 1 otherwise. Mode 99 also occurs in local Coop
starts using that managed initialization path; it is not a cosmetic UI flag.
Initialization routine `94350` copies setup `87EE2D8` to active `37EF964` at
`96D79/96D7F`. Save/setup serialization at `14C00` transfers the four-byte setup
field in both directions. State production in `19D960` reads the active flag and
sets bit 8 in its option byte at offset `7DF`. No proposed activation gate should
erase either representation. The indexed reference in `D6B40` is a table access;
its symbolic decompiler alias must not be mistaken for an unconditional NoDogs read.

All native callers of `FFC70` were inspected: the export, `C2030` (mapper IDs
`60`/`61`, so it does not take the dog branch), and state producer `19D960`.
Preserve native restrictions and state production outside the narrow extension.

## Permanent logical dispatch feasibility [mod integration]

A six-byte indirect jump at `FFD94` can replace exactly the complete CMP/JE pair.
Dormant execution replays both instructions, preserving the branch to `FFDCB`;
active execution replays CMP plus the current NOP replacement and resumes at
`FFD9A`. A flag-neutral byte dispatch can preserve incoming flags, RCX, stack
and SIMD state. The complete original mapper function was executed in a private
mapped image for 322,560 inputs in four variants: canonical original, production
patch, dormant prototype, active prototype. Dormant matched original and active
matched production for every input. The 40 changed cases were exclusively dog-cage,
mode-99, nonzero-NoDogs states with otherwise nonzero availability.

For peace time and No Dogs together, the 31 existing intervention sites admit
25 nonoverlapping grouped dispatch candidates. Complete function ranges and all
known code/table incoming targets were checked; function size is the sum of its
possibly discontiguous ranges and must not be treated as a contiguous extent.
The installed `X64AssemblyPatch` backend prepared all 25 six-byte bodies with
exact complete-instruction spans of six through nine bytes. For the two existing
entry hooks, retain the independently audited 16-/18-byte production spans.
The other 23 dormant/active copied blocks relocated 104 instructions successfully,
preserving operands, flags, RIP-relative data targets and internal/external branch
destinations. Existing peace tests passed 499,401 assertions, including 1,520,832
inactive and 1,520,832 active wildlife cases.

This does not establish an already integrated installer or game/MP acceptance.
Keep hooks permanent, prepare near pointer slots and all dependent resources,
validate the expanded physical spans against live bytes, and fail closed on
ownership/byte mismatch. Do not use a minimum-14-byte hook on a two-byte branch
or restore published native bytes when a setting changes.

Reproducible scripts, decoded functions, span candidates, source identities and
test logs: [modsettings audit](../../../../../.work/a/modsettings/001/AuditReport.md).
The local audit artifact is intentionally retained; native raw data and SQLite
were opened read-only and remain unchanged.

title: Move-command release contract [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

# Move-command release contract [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

## Scope and provenance

This contract describes how one managed mouse release becomes one native troop
command. Addresses are RVAs for native SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
The managed side was checked against the canonical publicized
`Assembly-CSharp` baseline and Script Extender 2.8.0.

## Managed input handoff

`EditorDirector.getMouseStateForEngine` is the single consumer of the managed
release state used by `EditorDirector.preDLLCallActions`:

- The left-command scheme reports release as `leftMouseStateForEngine == 3`.
- The right-command scheme reports release as `rightUpForEngine == true`.
- Reading clears `rightUpForEngine`. Left state 3 normally advances to 0.
- If `upPending` is set, the read clears `upPending` and publishes left state 3
  for the following call instead. `stateRead` is part of this state machine.
- `clearMouseStateForEngine()` sets left state to 0, `stateRead` to true, and
  `upPending` to false; right-up must be cleared separately.

Temporarily hiding a release across `EngineInterface.run` therefore requires a
snapshot and exact restoration of left state, right-up, `stateRead`, and
`upPending`. Once a replacement command has been accepted, restoring any of
those release states can enqueue a second command and is invalid.

## Native flow

`DLL_TroopSelection` at RVA `0x879A0` stores `mouseState`, `rightDown`, and
`rightUp` in the native input globals. `DLL_RunTick` at RVA `0x86680` passes
them to RVA `0x8B7E0` and the command-decision path at RVA `0x8C5F0`, then
clears all three native globals before returning.

RVA `0x8C5F0` uses left state 3 or right-up according to the selected control
scheme. Its ground-move branch stages the selected group and target through
RVA `0x195E30`. The synchronized move then follows Chore 17 at RVA `0x10AE0`,
move staging at `0x196100`, group movement at `0x11B520`, a formation selector
or common-group path, and terminal unit movement at `0x196280`.

The release is an edge-triggered transaction. A mod that sends an equivalent
authoritative move before the original run must still call the original run
once with neutral release state, and must not restore that consumed edge.

## Preview target eligibility

The held-button preview precedes the terminal command decision, so it must not
infer a ground Move from the mouse button alone. `DLL_RunTick` supplies the
current map coordinates and object-depth inputs to RVA `0x8B7E0`; the cursor
target resolver at RVA `0x79B90` rejects out-of-map and unavailable movement
targets and publishes building, unit, wall, and ground identities. The command
dispatcher at RVA `0x8C5F0` handles object attacks and interactions before its
remaining ground branch reaches RVA `0x195E30`.

A managed preview may therefore start only from a coherent cursor snapshot for
the captured native tile with no hovered or tile-resident unit, building, or
wall, nonzero movement-target availability, and a nonzero path component. The
immediate managed `grabTroopsOnScreen` result is part of the same object-target
decision and must also be empty. If the managed tile, native cursor tile, or
native grids disagree, the classification is ambiguous and must fail closed to
Vanilla without consuming the release. While the cursor later supplies drag
direction, only the fixed command tile is revalidated; the live hover identity
must not be mistaken for a replacement command target.

### Native troop-command mode

Object-free ground is not sufficient to identify a movement command. The
managed `Troops_AttackHere` action (`1012`) enters `DLL_GameAction` at RVA
`0x81870`, whose case calls RVA `0x90510` with value `5`. For an ordinary
eligible troop selection, RVA `0x90510` writes `5` to the 32-bit current and
saved troop-command modes at RVAs `0x67E8410` and `0x67E8414`. Special
selections can instead enter modes `0x14` or `0x16`.

The dispatcher at RVA `0x8C5F0` treats current mode `1` as the ordinary
movement/object-command path and mode `5` as Attack Here. The mode-5 ground
branch may call move stager `0x195E30` as part of preparing the special order
before issuing the actual attack-tile command, so observing that stager is not
proof of a Move command. Patrol/attack-move variations remain in mode `1` and
carry their semantics through the separate move parameters.

A held-ground preview must therefore additionally require current native mode
`1` at gesture start, while held, and immediately before release handoff. Any
other or unreadable value fails closed to Vanilla without consuming the release
or publishing a move context. `MainControls.CurrentAction` is a distinct
managed placement/editor state and is not a substitute for this native mode.

## Managed event ordering

Script Extender 2.8.0 raises `OnKeyDown`, `OnKey`, and `OnKeyUp` from the
separate `KeyManager.keys` state machine after the original managed
`KeyManager.Update` has run. Those events and the `EditorDirector` release
state consumed by `preDLLCallActions` are therefore observations of different
state machines; their relative delivery order must not be assumed.

The native-facing `EditorDirector` release is authoritative. A drag controller
may use `OnKeyUp` to capture its final main-thread cursor state and remove its
preview immediately, but it must also accept the native release when no
`OnKeyUp` was observed and use the last held main-thread snapshot. Requiring
both signals can indefinitely defer the native release, leave preview markers
active, and misinterpret later mouse presses as controls for the stale drag.
After an observed input release, a new mouse-down must first discard any stale
unclaimed drag before it may start or modify another gesture.

An input event rejected in a Script Extender 2.8.0 Pre handler is not merely
hidden from the current subscriber: the extender clears the corresponding
`KeyManager.keys` entry. Code must therefore never reject an auxiliary mouse
down and then wait for its later held or release event. In particular, doing
so for the opposite primary button can suppress Vanilla deselection and leave
a permanent capture state. Auxiliary primary and middle clicks must remain
with Vanilla unless their complete down/held/up lifecycle is handled without
depending on the cleared `KeyManager` state.

## Confidence

- Managed state transitions: confirmed-static.
- `DLL_TroopSelection` and `DLL_RunTick` parameter/global flow:
  confirmed-static.
- `0x8C5F0` release branches and ground-move staging: confirmed-static.
- `0x79B90` cursor target rejection and unit/building/wall/ground publication:
  confirmed-static.
- Object-command dispatch preceding the `0x195E30` ground branch at `0x8C5F0`:
  confirmed-static.
- `Troops_AttackHere` mode setup at `0x90510`, 32-bit command-mode global RVA
  `0x67E8410`, and mode-1/mode-5 dispatch split at `0x8C5F0`:
  confirmed-static.
- Duplicate-order consequence from restoring the release: confirmed-runtime
  by a formation command completing all terminal assignments before a later
  Vanilla order replaced its targets.
- Independent Script Extender input-event and `EditorDirector` release state
  machines: confirmed-static against Script Extender 2.8.0 and the publicized
  managed game assembly.
- Missing `OnKeyUp` leaving a FormationTest drag active while the native
  release was repeatedly deferred: confirmed-runtime in the 2026-09-19 log.
- Rejected Pre events clearing the corresponding Script Extender 2.8.0
  `KeyManager.keys` entry: confirmed-static and confirmed-runtime by the lost
  auxiliary release and subsequent blocked Vanilla deselection.


## 2026-10-02: final native ground feedback and formation preview

Revalidated installed native SHA-256 FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2
and real managed SHA-256 BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Feature audit covers RunTick 86680 Ã¢â€ â€™ 8B7E0 Ã¢â€ â€™ 8C5F0; representative selection
18D460 / route mode 18DC40; E7C40, E2610, DB650 and the E2CA0/E9D90/E9FF0
fallbacks; terminal cursor dispatch; renderer 41D60/436DE/41D10; command staging
195E30 Ã¢â€ â€™ chore17/10AE0 Ã¢â€ â€™ 196100 Ã¢â€ â€™ 11B520 Ã¢â€ â€™ 196280/F4930.

Ground reject 8F3DA writes detail -10 at 60AD560, image 41 at 60AD548,
file AC at 60AD54C and command 11 at 60AD55C. Final cursor dispatch table
90088 entry 3 goes to 90028: 9002D/90033 publishes kind 3 at 34A9E4C.
Approved ordinary ground starts file 6B/image 0, command 1/detail 0; applicable
special ground output uses file 6B/image 20, command 9/detail 0. Type-specific
positive fallback results remain authoritative. Object/wall contexts are excluded.
Terminal kind 3, mode 1 and coherent player/group/count/anchor are required;
unknown or rejected output never authorizes extra green formation markers.

Read-only RVAs: player 88E3D70, active tribe 7CC6720, selection count 67E8420,
mode 67E8410, cursor X/Y 3A11E2C/3A11E30, hovered unit 3A11DF0,
hovered building 3A11DE4, wall 3A11E34, cursor kind 34A9E4C,
file/image/command/detail 60AD54C/548/55C/560. Cursor offsets corroborated by
installed-layout GameCursorManager (unit +30, building +24, wall +74).
The new reader validates unchanged rejection, terminal-dispatch and mode bytes
before use; no executable memory is changed.

IMPORTANT: 41D60 calls 41D10 at the END, after visible tiles and cursor drawing.
It clears 34A9E4C immediately before that reset. Therefore authorization runs in
the first existing 436DE callback of each render pass, not in the reset callback;
reset only invalidates per-pass memoization. A confirmed gesture keeps its fixed
anchor when hover moves during spacing adjustment. EngineInterface.run and
existing input/map paths invalidate changed selection/gesture context. No native
search is added to marker rendering. 195E30 queues before checking feedback;

## 2026-10-08: formation Move classification over units

Native SHA-256 remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2. Rechecked the complete command-decision export at 8C5F0, target resolver 79B90 and Move staging 195E30, with the input and terminal flow above. The earlier requirement for empty unit hover/tile occupancy describes our conservative ground-only preview policy, not a general Vanilla prohibition on Move over units.

Ordinary mode 1 initializes file 6B/image 0/command 1/detail 0. Object interactions and attacks set distinct detail values (1..6, 10..12, etc.); rejected routes use detail -10, file AC/image 41. Final kind 3 plus the accepted file/image/command pair and detail 0 classifies ordinary Move; hovered-unit identity alone does not invalidate it. Attack Here remains a separate mode even when staging a preliminary Move. Confidence: confirmed-static; visible game and multiplayer acceptance remain separate.

Formation uses separate authorization from the unchanged strict queue ground policy. A candidate waits for a newer EngineInterface.run and coherent terminal-render cursor feedback at its captured anchor. The render callback can execute inside DLL_RunTick, before run returns; it uses the active run generation so immediate dragging does not miss the first confirmed anchor. A no-buffer run never reaches the terminal render callback and returns zero without advancing the completed generation. The real managed run calls preDLLCallActions then DLL_RunTick when a free buffer exists; its no-buffer path returns zero. Proof is read in the existing first tile-render callback before the render tail clears cursor kind. Later hover affects facing only. Selection/player/group/mode and map identity changes invalidate proof; unconfirmed releases remain untouched for Vanilla. Existing accepted-release consumption and per-slot placement checks remain authoritative.

## 2026-10-17: infinite patrol versus extended Shift queue

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Rechecked the complete Chore-17 pack/unpack function 0x10AE0 against its current
hash-bound dataset. Stager 0x195E30 writes parameter 5 to 0x86C1338; the handler
serializes one byte and sign-extends it before 0x196100 -> 0x11B520. The native
patrol field is therefore distinct from the move-type field at 0x86C133C.
Chore 71 reaches 0x11C3A0 through 0x176C0 and writes the indexed point, point
count and patrol mode; collapsing it to a plain queued Move loses that mode.
The Extender source and referenced assembly agree: PatrolInfinite=1, PatrolOnce=-1.
These data-flow findings are confirmed-static; internal function names remain
candidate-level. Consumer regression tests execute production capture and marker
entrypoints with boundary doubles; native gameplay and real multiplayer looping
remain untested by those fixtures. No new native hooks were installed.


## 2026-10-17: local formation command speech

Native SHA-256 remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Confirmed-static complete command feedback chain: 195E30 enqueues Chore17 before
selecting voice at 11A1B0, representative at 18D460, exclusions/route checks and
busy test E0E0; its terminal 1960DC call invokes 3BC0 with dialogue manager
64C4490. Voice selection returns EAX (the decompiled void signature is incomplete).
Near response6 uses inclusive +/-72 on EACH axis relative to the tribe leader and
passes the packed target tile; distant response10 and reject9 pass zero.
Default move type excludes types22,23,39 (not type38); types40,41,61 are silent.
Representative type30 with native unit field at public GameUnit+388 !=0 is silent.
18D460 temporarily changes current-unit global9302C4; callers using it as a pure
query must save/restore that scratch value. 3BC0 owns voice variants, special-type
branches, duplicate suppression and downstream 3770/38A0 -> EDF0 -> native audio.

RunTick86680 updates sound-channel inputs before render41D60; draw reset41D10 is
at its end, before dialogue41C0, native sound handling and return-data export.
This existing reset hook can emit local accepted-gesture feedback without staging
another move. Formation consumes its own local release and calls group movement
directly, bypassing 195E30 feedback; incoming synchronized commands must not emit
that local acknowledgement on every peer. The speech callback does not certify
that each selected unit moved. Data layouts remain canonical-hash bound.

Implementation/update contract: BugfixesAndQoL/UpdateToNewDLL.md, Formation command
speech. Offline behavior and native-contract checks are separate from pending
audible/Mono/real multiplayer acceptance. No additional native hook is installed.

Capture acquires the real private static object EngineInterface.threadLock by
validated reflection and nonblocking Monitor.TryEnter. A busy engine omits only
that optional response. Both the temporary 18D460 scratch write and its restore
are inside this lock. The render-end emitter also requires Monitor.IsEntered
on the same object. EngineInterface.run holds it around preDLLCallActions,
DLL_RunTick and play-state copying; no new native call races the simulation.
The offline test checks this field against the real Assembly-CSharp metadata,
not a publicized assembly, and exercises busy/unprotected/protected cases.

## Formation drag start under a busy engine lock (2026-10-26)

Managed SHA-256 `BC8B6A39...`: `Director.runSimTickTest` runs `EngineInterface.run`
on the separate `Stronghold1Engine` thread; a `System.Threading.Timer` queues ticks at
game speed, and `run` holds `threadLock` for the complete tick. Vanilla blocks the
main thread on that lock only for discrete inputs (`KeyManager` hotkeys and HUD
buttons through `GameAction`); `TroopSelection` and building placement run inside
`preDLLCallActions` on the engine thread. The Formation press therefore captures
its Unity target on the main thread and its native selection only under the lock:
when `TryEnter(0)` fails, the next `EngineInterface.run` hook completes the start
before Vanilla's preparation. A blocking wait was rejected (one frame stall per
command click, up to a long AI tick); dropping to Vanilla was rejected (the
formation is lost under load). A click released before completion remains Vanilla.

## Confirmed render-time cursor lifetime (2026-10-26)

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
`DLL_RunTick` (`86680`) calls `8C5F0` at `86920`, then the visible renderer
`41D60` at `86A68`. Renderer range `41D60..4580E`, exclusive end; native body
SHA-256 3EF71AC141815F4AAD74E1A20B6991425175728DA09EC4F07E2C813DF8533FFF.
Its first three instructions save RBX/RBP/RSI at `[rsp+10/18/20]`, 5 bytes each.
Cursor kind is cleared to -1 at `45702`, before the `41D10` draw-list reset call
at `4570C`. Consequently reset-completion feedback is too late for a fresh Move
proof. Six integer/pointer ABI arguments are preserved by an entry observer.

The prologue span has no direct interior targets across executable sections and
no interior exception-function entry. Inline/context minimum 14 therefore rounds
to 15 bytes, continuation `41D6F`. The function includes embedded switch data;
a linear disassembler byte total is not a valid whole-function coverage check.
Evidence: `.work/a/island-targets/001/audit.py` and `native-audit.json`;
production entry/demand machine execution in `GroundFrameMachineTests.cs`.
These are static/machine contracts, not an in-game frame-time measurement.

## Confirmed simulation-thread speech contract (2026-10-26)

Same native SHA-256 as above; real Assembly-CSharp SHA-256
BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Director.Awake starts `Stronghold1Engine`; runSimTickTest calls EngineInterface.run
on this simulation thread. Its private threadLock covers native RunTick and
PlayState copying. The main thread later plays exported speech through GameMap
case18 / SFXManager. Requiring the initialization/main thread at native reset
therefore suppresses valid local acknowledgement.

Correction to the older shorthand "default move type": the conditional exclusion
in 195E30 is parameter6 == 0, matching installed TribeMoveType.NoChange. Actual
DefaultInSync is 1, Fast is -255. Types22/23/39 are excluded only for zero;
types40/41/61 are always excluded, type38 is the explicit debug exception.
The audited 3BC0 special-type branch 0x4F can query DF120 with radius4. This is
a bounded local tile/nearby-unit query using shared scratch, not a full route.
Preserve native Busy/duplicate/special handling under the engine lock; do not
call 195E30 again for audio because it stages another Chore and can reach DB650.
11C650 owns additional rate-limited group Foley; this correction does not add it.

The existing render entry41D60 stamps the owning thread-local run scope, reset
41D10 consumes local pending speech before dialogue41C0 / export19D960. No-buffer
runs and unrelated reset calls cannot provide that render proof. Production-code
two-thread fixtures and native adapter tests verify sequencing and scratch restore;
audible gameplay, actual Mono behavior and host/client remain separate acceptance.


## Anchored rejected gestures and death snapshots (2026-10-26)

Same canonical native SHA-256 as above. The ordinary-ground failed-route producer
8F3DA..8F45E writes command17/detail-10, fileAC/image41, local cursor kind4 which
the terminal renderer dispatch publishes as kind5. Object/structure branches
share rejection imagery, so ownership additionally requires native mode1 and no
hovered unit/building/wall. Details1/3 of command9 are interactions, not a general
ground-denied proof. A fresh result at the captured press tile can own cancellation;
it is never positive movement authorization. Do not consume unclassified input.

The native mode1 release branch at 8F64D handles detail-10 separately (optional
reject sound through 109EF0), while ordinary accepted movement calls 195E30 with
current 3A11E2C/3A11E30. Passing a rejected drag back to Vanilla after moving the
mouse therefore allows a different release target. Consuming the managed release
before the original run prevents that retarget without a new native hook.

LocalSelectionAPI reads a completed PlayState, whereas UnitAccess reads live
native metadata. A selected ID can still be present in that snapshot after its
native death marker is set. UnitAccess.IsReallyAlive (AliveState plus WORD29C)
is the existing audited predicate, including melee writer199110; do not infer
life from health, animation or AliveState alone. Filtering those original stable
identities under the engine lock requires no new death-event hooks or path probes.
The neutral-run/exact-restore input contract above applies only before acceptance;
restoration after cancellation, acceptance or gesture replacement is invalid.

# Move-stager data anchors [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

## Scope and provenance

This note records code anchors from which native data addresses and layout values can be derived without a fixed RVA. Addresses are RVAs for native SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.

Evidence:
- complete Iced disassembly of the mapped installed DLL (2026-10-22, `Shared/Tests/Native.Tests/DisassemblyProbe.cs`);
- the semantic baseline function export of `0x195E30`;
- a whole-image count of `lea rcx,[rip+X]` arguments before direct calls (`call_args` scan).

Confidence is confirmed-static. Runtime acceptance of a derivation does not exist yet.

Purpose: the update fallback in [AGENTS/native-analysis.md](../../../../../AGENTS/native-analysis.md) (section „Prüfkosten“) needs a validated anchor plus a second independent evidence per value. The table lists both for every value.

## Cursor move stager `0x195E30`

The function also appears in [MOVE_COMMAND_RELEASE.md](MOVE_COMMAND_RELEASE.md). APIShared validates its entry as „cursor move-stager entry“, and BugfixesAndQoL owns a detour at it. Derivations must therefore read the unmodified load image (`CrusaderLibraryLoadContext.Memory`), not the live code.

Arguments: `rcx` = unit manager context, `edx` = tribe ID, `r8d` = tile X / command, `r9d` = tile Y, stack `[rsp+80h]` (arg 5) = patrol mode, `[rsp+88h]` (arg 6) = move type.

| Value | Anchor in 0x195E30 (offset, instruction) | Second evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Chore tribe ID `0x86C132C` | +0x44 `mov [rip],r14d` (r14 = movsxd edx) | `0x10AE0`+0x2C `lea rdx,[rip]` (first packed field) |
| Chore tile X / command `0x86C1330` | +0x52 `mov [rip],r8d` | `0x10AE0`+0x4B `lea rdx,[rip]` (second) |
| Chore tile Y `0x86C1334` | +0x4B `mov [rip],r15d` (r15 = movsxd r9d) | `0x10AE0`+0x6A `lea rdx,[rip]` (third) |
| Chore patrol mode `0x86C1338` | +0x59 `mov [rip],eax` (eax = arg 5) | `0x10AE0`+0x8A `lea rdx,[rip]` (fourth) |
| Chore move type `0x86C133C` | +0x5F `mov [rip],ebp` (ebp = arg 6) | `0x10AE0`+0xAA `lea rdx,[rip]` (fifth) |
| Tribe manager `0x7CC6720` | +0x6D `lea rcx,[rip]` before `call 0x11A1B0` | +0x1C5 and +0x236, same `lea` |
| Tribe record stride `0x688` | +0x1CC `imul rbp,r14,688h` | followed by `cmp [rcx+rbp+2Ch],eax` with rcx = tribe manager |
| Tribe player-ID offset `0x2C` | +0x1D3 `cmp [rcx+rbp+2Ch],eax`, eax = active player | the stride and tribe manager of the same compare |
| Unit manager `0x67E8400` | +0xC1 `lea rdx,[rip]` | +0x11D, +0x15D, +0x1A1, same `lea` |
| Unit record stride `0x490` | +0xBA `imul rsi,rcx,490h` | `0x18D460`+0xA7 and +0xBA `imul …,490h` |
| Path manager `0x60AD660` | +0x102 `lea rcx,[rip]` before `call 0xE2610` | +0x173 `lea rcx,[rip]` before `call 0xDB650` |
| Active player ID `0x88E3D70` | +0x109 `mov edx,[rip]` | +0x1BF `mov eax,[rip]`; also `0x18D460`+0x6C, `0xE0E6` |
| Sound manager `0x88E72D0` | +0x202 `lea rcx,[rip]` before `call 0xE0E0` (speech busy) | whole image: 10 of 11 direct calls of `0xE0E0` pass this `lea rcx` argument |
| Dialogue manager `0x64C4490` | +0x2A5 `lea rcx,[rip]` before `call 0x3BC0` (speech) | whole image: all 13 direct calls of `0x3BC0` pass this argument |

Direct call targets inside the stager:
- `0x11A1B0` selected voice, `0x18D460` representative, `0xE0E0` speech busy and `0x3BC0` speech;
- also `0xE2610` PCL reachability and `0xDB650` direct tile search.

These are a second evidence for the separately pattern-resolved FormationSpeech and gate-routing entries.

## Other anchors

- **Chore mode `0x85F8FEC`:** read by `mov eax,[rip]` at the start of all three Chore handlers: `0x10AE0`+0x06, `0x12BF0`+0x06 and `0x176C0`+0x04.
- **Current-unit scratch `0x9302C4`:** written by `mov [rip],edx` at `0x18D460`+0x75 and +0xFE.
- **Chore handler table `0x2C7A30`** (populated at runtime): entries 17, 36 and 71 hold the move, target-order and waypoint-append handlers. Three entries matching three pattern-resolved handlers would locate the table without its RVA.

## Without an anchor yet

- **`TribeUnitCountOffset 0x5C`** (Formation core): no anchor was confirmed. The stager reads `[tribe+0x5A]`, a different field.
- **`MovementTargetAvailability 0x3A11EA4`** (Formation core): no anchor was confirmed.

## Limits

- **Dependent runtime:** ExtendedShiftCommandQueue and Formation (including FormationSpeech) depend on BugfixesAndQoL's shared command runtime `UnitCommandPathRuntime`. That runtime requires the reference hash (about 40 fixed detour prefixes and about 100 native constants). Until it gets the same fallback, deriving these values cannot keep the features working after a game update.
- **Fixed instruction offsets:** these anchors locate values at fixed offsets inside the validated function. An update that changes the function body fails closed instead of guessing.

# Minimap last-frame speech ownership [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The installed DLL matched CURRENT.json during this investigation. Native function
labels below are candidate names in the semantic database; the stated field and
output-record flows are visible in the exported pseudocode.

## Audited flow

- Notification presentation at RVA 0xFEE50 calls 0xEF20 for nonempty audio before
  0x14F0 for nonempty video. 0xEF20 emits command 18 through 0x1A4270 with channel 1;
  0x14F0 emits command 21 through 0x1A4100 with loop and speech-wait arguments.
  GameMap.processTestMap consumes those records in order and calls SFXManager.
- SFXManager.playSpeech resolves the resource and MyAudioManager.PlaySpeech accepts
  or rejects the request. Only an accepted request calls the five-argument private
  LoadClip overload, after setting speechMode1 to loading (1). Successful loading
  changes it to playing (2); MonitorLoadedSounds clears it when playback stops,
  except while deliberately paused. isSpeechPlaying(1) means mode != 0, including
  loading and intentional pauses; it does not identify a particular voice line.
- SFXManager.playBink constructs a fresh request URI, records whether existing
  channel-1 speech is to be awaited, and requests state 1 (once) or 2 (loop).
  Replacements negate that state until FatControler installs the new source.
- The installed NoesisMediaPlayer interprets ** as nonlooping playback with a
  MediaEnded event. MainHUD.RadarME_Ended(object, RoutedEventArgs) changes state 1
  to state 3 and opacity 0 when speech is still pending; otherwise it closes the
  media and clears playing/state. The parameterless overload always closes it.
- Director.Update invokes GUI checks for rendered buffers and also at a 100 ms
  fallback interval while simulation is running. FatControler closes state 3 only
  when the entire speech channel is idle. Briefings pause/resume the media.
- DLL_RunTick (RVA 0x86680) copies binkPlaying into the native flag checked by
  notification update 0xFE570. Even beyond its 10000 ms age gate, that update waits
  for the video flag to clear. Finalizer 0x102A70 clears the current presentation
  and promotes the next queued entry when present. The native age gate therefore
  does not limit an incorrectly retained managed video.

## Consumer defect and correction [mod integration]

NotificationLastFrameFeature formerly forced binkWaitForSpeech=true based on any
channel-1 occupant and retained no voice identity. An unrelated replacement could
keep an old portrait visible. A source-compiled isolated fixture confirmed retention
across 100 unrelated replacements. This establishes the code defect, not the exact
unrecorded sequence in the supplied user log.

The corrected consumer gives every accepted channel-1 load a generation, binds
eligible video requests to that generation, and closes only its own held video
when the generation changes. It never forces waiting on a video without the
original wait request. Its completion callback uses APIShared GuiChecks on the
HUD caller thread; no simulation-tick callback touches Noesis. Speech hooks and
GUI registrations remain installed for process lifetime. Mission end invalidates
pending identities through the existing central lifecycle subscription.

The shared internal speech owner also invalidates pending skip loads when an
unrelated request supersedes them. It retains the Script Extender's _SE_ path
semantics and calls the existing single-path loader through reflection, preserving
that loader's override hook. No native hook spans or public APIs change.

## Verification and limits

BugfixesAndQoL/Test-NotificationLastFramePreflight.ps1 validates installed Noesis
identity, real game member signatures and reflection fields, then runs the actual
feature sources in tests/NotificationPlayback.Tests. Tests substitute Unity/Noesis
objects and hook dispatch, retaining audited Vanilla state predicates. They cover
speech replacements, repeated filenames, rejected requests, pauses, source/HUD
replacement, disabled behavior, stale asynchronous loads and mission reset.
A real-game reproduction and live acceptance remain unavailable; these tests do
not validate decoder timing or prove the historical user's precise trigger.
## Current text-owned presentation, 2026-10-18 [mod integration]

This supersedes the consumer's speech-generation completion policy above; the
historical audit and its verification limits remain unchanged. Native SHA-256 is
FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2; installed
Assembly-CSharp.dll SHA-256 is
BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Both installed files were rechecked against the referenced evidence.

- Presentation 0xFEE50 emits text through 0x1A2850 (command 20) before optional
  audio and video. GameMap.processTestMap processes these records on Director's
  rendered-buffer caller, then GameData.setGameState/updateOST applies text state
  before the subsequent GuiChecks callback. Function labels remain candidate-level;
  the record order is supported by the exported pseudocode and managed consumers.
- OnScreenText.addOSTEntry(OST_MESSAGE_BAR, ...) refreshes Vanilla's text expiry.
  updateOST applies expiry only when allowExpire is true, refreshes the expiry
  while a briefing is visible, and drives MainViewModel.OST_Message_Bar_Vis.
  Its setter emits the public System.ComponentModel.PropertyChanged event.
  No consumer expiry calculation is required. The Extender's updateOST IL hook
  replaces custom-Lord text resolution, not this visibility signal.
- A nonlooping ** media source can be paused in the MediaEnded callback while
  leaving requestBinkPlayState=1 and binkIsPlaying=true. FatControler neither
  restarts that state nor executes its speech-dependent state-3 completion branch.
  Its briefing-resume path can call Play again; the GUI consumer must pause a held
  frame afterwards without restoring opacity after a left-click hide.
- BugfixesAndQoL now associates each message-bar write with the next accepted
  video in the rendered batch. Identical text/file names do not identify ownership.
  A visible-to-hidden text notification closes only its matching current video via
  the public parameterless RadarME_Ended; GuiChecks handles missing initial text,
  logical disable, source/HUD replacement and deferred mission invalidation.
  This may end a portrait while speech is still playing, as explicitly requested.
- Queue update 0xFE570 waits for the video flag after its age gate. Closing the
  picture when Vanilla hides text releases that dependency; waiting for the native
  finalizer first would create a circular lifetime dependency. No native patch is
  introduced. The separate skip feature retains its audio-load cancellation.

The new production-source fixture covers text-driven completion, silent messages,
independent audio replacement/end/pause, pending text/source, repeated filenames,
left-click preservation, explicit close, briefing resume, replacement HUD/ViewModel
and mission invalidation. The fixture does not prove real decoder timing or a live
in-game acceptance result; no installation is authorized for this change.

## HD-bounded speech presentation, 2026-10-23

This supersedes the 2026-10-18 text-owned consumer policy. The preceding audits
remain historical evidence. Current DE native SHA-256 was rechecked as
FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
The installed managed assembly still matches BC8B6A39 above (preflight validates
actual member signatures and the Noesis player identity independently).

### HD evidence and closed feature flow

Source: the local `HD sources/Stronghold Crusader HD reversed/Stronghold Crusader.exe.gzf`
archive, SHA-256 9069E32DD2B6FEFFEE39E0B12EA9CF17CE68B7CF93AA8B4C7291969298D4E2A0.
Its program metadata identifies original executable SHA-256
3BB0A8C1E72331B3A30A5AA93ED94BECA0081B476B04C1960E26D5B45387AC5A.
This identifies the archived HD program, not an independently checked installed HD
executable or a verified game version. Function names are archive annotations;
the following control/data-flow statements are confirmed-static against its code.

- `playVideoOverMap` VA 004B7AF0 opens nonlooping Bink slot 1, starts speech
  stream 3, and binds that stream to the video only if it is reported playing.
  `setBinkSndStreamAndStartTime` VA 00408E70 writes the stream index at
  BinkControlClass+40+slot*4 and the current timeGetTime DWORD at +48+slot*4;
  binding is skipped if the sound system is unavailable. Only this caller binds
  a speech stream through that setter in the archived program.
- `playSpeechOnStream` VA 0047B830 delegates to `playSoundStreamOnSlot`
  VA 0047B060. An unavailable sound system, focus restrictions or failure to
  open the WAV leaves no playing stream. `isSampleOrStreamPlaying` VA 00479A60
  requires an active sound slot, a nonnull stream and Miles status 4.
- Both `processBinkFrames` VA 00409200 and `copyBinkToVideoBuffer` VA 00408FC0
  permanently clear a nonzero video speech binding when that stream is no
  longer playing OR more than 20000 ms have elapsed since binding. At 0040922E
  the assembler compares elapsed DWORD against 0x4E20 and uses unsigned JBE
  at 00409233 to retain the binding at equality. Clearing does not restart the
  clock, stop speech, or bind a subsequent stream anew.
- For a nonlooping minimap video, reaching the last Bink frame advances no
  further while the binding remains active. Once cleared, the same video-end
  branch calls `stopBinkPlayback` VA 00408E30, closes the Bink object and clears
  isBinkVideoPlaying. The 20-second rule limits speech waiting, not video length.
  A voice replaced on the same occupied stream can extend the still frame only
  within the original deadline; HD does not identify individual voice requests.
- `playAiLordMessage` VA 004B7C90 draws message text separately and waits for
  the video pointer to clear after its 10000-ms age gate. Modal completion reaches
  `playNextStoredAIMessage` VA 004BE960, which clears current presentation and
  promotes a queued entry. This is distinct from the speech-wait bound.

Reproducible local exports and the small reader are retained under
`.work/a/lastframe-hd/001/hd-verified.stdout.log` and `HdRead.java` (workspace
relative). The reader imports the archive into a fresh temporary Ghidra project
and opens a read-only program; Ghidra rejects `.work` as a project path element.
The export includes both video paths, the binding writes and the exact timeout
assembler. The original archive and DE raw baseline were not modified.

### DE implementation contract [mod integration]

- `NotificationLastFrameFeature` uses nonlooping `**` sources for accepted
  nonlooping minimap videos and captures Vanilla's wait request plus the current
  audio manager. No message text subscription/hook or speech-generation identity
  controls this feature. `NotificationSpeechPlayback` remains unchanged for skip
  load cancellation, including the Extender single-path loader override.
- A Stopwatch timestamp is captured once after each accepted video request.
  The original wait predicate is permanently cleared after channel-1 idle,
  audio-manager replacement or elapsed >20 seconds, including while the video
  is still playing. Loading/paused states count as channel occupancy, as in DE
  Vanilla, but cannot renew or bypass the fixed bound. Time is monotonic and is
  not suspended for game pause/briefing. The precision improvement over HD's
  DWORD clock does not change its strict greater-than threshold.
- On MediaEnded, an active binding holds the frame paused in state 1; otherwise
  the existing public close method releases it. GuiChecks checks completion and
  re-pauses held media if Vanilla resumed it after a briefing. The end marker is
  recorded before Pause, so a decoder-Pause failure falling back to Vanilla's
  state 3 still has bounded completion. No UI work is done from simulation ticks.
- Existing logical disable, deferred mission invalidation and stale HUD/request/
  source checks remain. A foreign current media source is never closed by old
  owner cleanup. Text visibility cannot close or extend the video; audio is never
  stopped by picture completion. The native queue observes the released video
  flag through DLL_RunTick and can finalize normally, without a new native hook.

Production-source fixtures cover strict 19999/20000/20001-ms boundaries, hung,
failed and null speech loads, long videos/voices, replacement voices and files,
observed-idle latching, pause/briefing, left/right clicks, stale HUD/media/manager,
mission end, logical disable, and decoder Pause failure. These isolated adapters
validate the consumer, not live Noesis decoder timing. Actual game acceptance is
still required; this task requests no game installation.

## Diagnostic refinement (2026-10-23) [mod integration]

The fixed 20-second bound above does not by itself establish behavioral parity
with HD. The retained HD export confirms that VA 00479A60 queries the actual
Miles stream status (4 = playing), while DE's `isSpeechPlaying(1)` reads
`speechMode1 != 0`, including loading and intentional pause. DE's private
`MonitorLoadedSounds` only clears a playing-but-silent channel while
`speechPaused` is false. A silent busy channel is an observation to distinguish
from a stuck decoder; a single transient sample is not proof of a defect.

HD checks Bink's final frame directly in both audited processing paths.
The current DE feature instead requires a HUD `MediaEnded` event accepted by
its managed request/HUD/media/sender guards before setting `Held`. Therefore
an absent or rejected event can leave the video outside its later held-frame
completion path even after the speech deadline. This is a static possibility,
not an established explanation of the reported game run.

Installed Noesis (SHA-256
98476D3CA84AE0F2DCFBADDCC64B01A1F65474BD44402673FD6856D1B5347648)
exposes this callback chain: Unity `loopPointReached` -> private
`NoesisMediaPlayer.OnMediaEnded(VideoPlayer)` -> `RaiseMediaEnded` -> private
`NoesisApp.MediaElement.OnMediaEnded()` -> routed HUD callback. `MediaElement`
owns private `_player`, and the Unity adapter owns private `_videoPlayer`.
`Noesis.BaseComponent.getCPtr(BaseComponent)` is public static and returns a
HandleRef. Diagnostic managed and native identities can consequently expose
different wrappers for the same Noesis object without altering production
identity checks. Each private read is reflection-only and preflight-validated
against the installed assemblies.

The diagnostic build records both callback chains, independent render/GUI/audio
monitor counts, raw audio and decoder state, and observed close results. Missing
callbacks or failed reads are explicit evidence gaps. Playback decisions remain
unchanged pending a reproduced game run. Managed IL evidence and build/test
records are retained in `.work/a/lastframe-diag/001`; the native DLL still matches
CURRENT.json. These observations supplement, rather than replace, the archived
HD/DE audit above.

## Confirmed URI rejection and consumer correction (2026-10-23) [mod integration]

The complete diagnostic run from 21:15:31 through 21:17:05 confirms the cause
for `wf_taunt2.webm`, video request 1 / speech request 5. At 21:16:04.800 the
Unity, MediaElement and HUD end callbacks all arrived. Every identity guard was
true except URI equality: Noesis returned
`Assets/GUI/Video/Characters/wf_taunt2.webm**`, while the SFX request retained
backslashes. Relative System.Uri equality treats these spellings as different.
The feature rejected the event, so Held remained false. At 21:16:06.721 the
audio monitor correctly cleared speechMode1 from 2 to 0. After 25 seconds there
were 996 successful GUI calls, no skipped/replaced calls, no diagnostic errors
or missing callbacks, and zero close attempts. This is a consumer source-guard
defect, not a stuck audio channel in this run. Original log:
`.work/a/lastframe-uri/001/reproduced.log`, especially lines 2947 and 2954-2965.

The correction preserves URI equality and additionally compares only slash-
normalized OriginalString values, ordinally and with equal absolute/relative
kind. Expected normalized text is cached per accepted request. The same guard
serves end acceptance, briefing re-pause and both close paths; request reference,
HUD/media/sender checks, text independence, audio state and deadline are retained.

The installed Script Extender's NoesisMediaElement_Setter_Hook can also redirect
a registered relative/provider-qualified video to an absolute file, possibly
swapping .webm to .mp4. Its TryResolveVideoPath uses Path.ChangeExtension during
lookup and returns the physical path without the input ** suffix. Thus applying
** before an override is resolved loses both source identity and nonlooping end
semantics. The consumer now calls that existing, signature-validated internal
resolver via reflection once per eligible request before adding **. No Extender
or APIShared files, global hooks or public contracts change. Unregistered paths
retain their original URI, including Vanilla absolute custom-lord sources.

Source-linked fixtures reproduce both observed boundaries: Noesis separator
round-trip and SE physical override/extension selection. They cover the Wolf
timeline, provider-qualified/ordinary mod assets with/without speech and waiting,
absolute custom-lord paths, text-only messages, foreign sources and unchanged HD
wait/lifecycle/click safeguards. A soundless video runs to its own end; visible
text may continue independently. These tests do not substitute for an actual
post-fix game run or prove every decoder/media format.

# Outposts: curated static observations [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Managed SHA-256: `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
Installed Script Extender: 2.6.0. Local source commit `2cee24e33b5a5d81d1c275efabc714ac59917b7b`, tree `9cfb59b7b531553b23709b90b3cc3f10b0615cc1`.
Date: 2026-09-16. Static analysis only; no runtime verification or approved hook spans.

Detailed audit, all profiles, field map, limitations, workspace references and diagnostic cases: [Findings/Outposts.md](../../../../../Findings/Outposts.md).
Reproducible hash-checked evidence extraction: [audit.py](../../../../OutpostAudit/audit.py).

## Confirmed static relationships

- Building dispatch table RVA `0x2DEAE0` entries 2, 106 and 107 all point to RVA `0xABB90`. Caller is the indirect dispatch at `0xC64AD`, within `0xC60F0`. An empty direct-call graph for ABB90 is not evidence of no callers.
- ABB90 lacks usable baseline pseudocode. Its actual contiguous code ends with RET at `0xACDE7`; jump tables begin at `0xACDE8` and `0xACDFC`. Baseline function size 4501 is summed body size, not the contiguous extent. See [full disassembly evidence](../../../../OutpostAudit/FBCB9319/ABB90.json).
- Profile table RVA `0x2DD880` has 24 records of 13 signed int32 values (52 bytes): interval, minimum, base group size, random span, eight type slots, role. Records 0–7 European, 8–15 Arabian, 16–23 Bedouin. See [extracted data](../../../../OutpostAudit/FBCB9319/profiles.json). Mask chooses enabled profiles, not percentages of units.
- Building slot formula is manager RVA `0x64CCBB0` + `0x5C` + one-based buildingId * `0x32C`; managed array starts at manager + `0x388`. GameBuilding offsets `0x300/302/304/308/30A/30C/30E/310/312/314/316/318` are respectively profile mask, active tribe ID/global ID, counter, target size, profile, size setting, delay, catapult flag, vicinity-init flag, two acceleration counters. Offsets are structure-relative, not manager-relative.
- Initializer `0xB47E0` sets mask 255, size 1, delay 0, guard target 6 or 7, guard counter 1200. Dispatch `0xC60F0` first promotes NeedsInit, later executes ordinary updates; deletion state enters `0xB8310`.
