## Confidence and remaining work

### Macemen-only production replacement audit (2026-09-17)

The narrower test contract is documented in [OutpostTest native contract](../../../../../Testmods/OutpostTest/UpdateToNewDLL.md). Installed Native hash and Extender commit/tree remain unchanged; installed RedBird.X64 1.1.0.0 was inspected. Gate `0xABC78..0xABC88` contains CMP(7), JE(6), TEST(3); incoming jump `0xABC6E` targets its start, no baseline xref or direct function branch targets its interior. `0xACDDB` is the early epilogue before the later RBP/RDI/R14 spills. Skipping this section also skips vicinity initialization and production counters, while keeping the registration/animation prefix.

Maceman type 26 dispatches to `0x146A70`. Its normal state 101 uses the native movement continuation and returns to idle/special states as other native Macemen do. Unit field manager-relative `+0xA82` / GameUnit `+0x426` is exposed by the current Extender as `r_AITribeRole`; the outpost writes value 50. The unit recruitment-rally field `+0x708` / GameUnit `+0xAC` is cleared. The dedicated allocator at `0x119D60` initializes tribe Alive=2, not NeedsInit=1; units created by `0x17FEF0` start NeedsInit=1. The exact completion ABI at `0x2E2B0` is `(AI manager, tribe ID, tribe global ID) -> void`; the third argument is required for queue identity.

Additional production blockers are RVA `0x37EF974` (int) and `0x38722DC` (byte), bypassed for native modes 0/99. The player cap compares sum of `0x379B30C + owner*0x583C` and `0x379E6D4 + owner*0x583C` against `0x37EF950` if player category `0x8574BCC+owner*4` is -1, else `0x37EF954`. Native Create separately enforces its pool limit. These exact predicates are test-contract findings, not guesses about the display names of the modes/counters.

These are specific static relationships, not blanket promotion of the baseline's candidate function signatures. Decompiled signatures may omit live register/stack arguments. Function evidence retains the original confidence and binary hash. Raw exports, database, function-claims and Ghidra projects were not relabeled or regenerated.

Do not infer runtime-safe hooks, all-type AI-role compatibility, complete native save-field persistence or multiplayer archive roundtrip from these findings. Full normal-UI run/stance command tracing, remaining mode/limit semantics, special-type role readers and runtime cases are listed in the detailed audit. Any implementation still requires that narrower contract closure and installed-hook-backend validation.

## Runtime comparison, 2026-09-17 (scoped observation)

The passive OutpostTest comparison under the same verified native hash is documented in [Findings/Outposts.md](../../../../../Findings/Outposts.md), section Vanilla-Vergleichslauf. All three building variants were observed for owners 1 and 2. The previously static incremental-group relationship has a concrete runtime example: tribe 4426/392 grows from 1 to 12 members while its first unit remains at the exit; movement follows. Unlike this incremental path, the earlier custom test completed each five-unit group immediately.

Hold occurs later for eight identity-confirmed guards, but all 39 guards initially have no tribe in the observed samples. The logger measures tribe stance, not an independent unit/UI stance. Therefore neither universal initial Hold nor its writer is established. Six guards also later occur in Aggressive tribes. These observations must not be promoted to a claim that guard membership/stance is immutable. State 114 is absent in this run; its semantics remain unresolved. These are modded-session observations with bounded sampling, not new function-signature or writer claims.

## Maceman state 114 clarification (2026-09-17)

The previously unresolved semantics of 114 are now established for Macemen: death animation, not an unknown live AI command. Under the same reverified native hash, damage handler 0x199110 subtracts target health (+0xA20 manager/slot, GameUnit +0x3C4), returns early for positive health, and writes 0x71 or default 0x72 to state (+0x918 manager/slot, GameUnit +0x2BC) after lethal damage. Additional lethal writers include 0xC1B40 and 0xC70B0. Maceman update 0x146A70 shares animation processing for 0x72/73/74, transitions to 0x6E (110), then marks AliveState=3 after its terminal byte counter exceeds 32. AliveState can remain 2 during the death animation. Generic baseline function confidence remains candidate; these are scoped static field/control-flow findings.

See the State 114 addendum in Findings/Outposts.md for parameter bases and qualifications. The first custom-spawn log shows nine dying Macemen; it does not identify their damage source or the writer of tribe=0. Previous statements that state 114 semantics are unresolved are superseded, without claiming a proven group-detachment path or a spawn defect.

## Macemen timing audit closure (2026-09-17)

ABB90 disassembly confirms group-wait threshold max(2000 - signed acceleration at GameBuilding+316, context minimum): native modes other than 0/99 enforce at least 400; the world predicate int RVA3668E34>3000 && int RVA3669048<11 then enforces 100, otherwise 600. Same world predicate selects group acceleration increment 100 versus 33 at completion. Spawn acceleration +318 increments by 4. Profile 2 uses max(100,250-acceleration) * (100-15*size)/100 with signed integer truncation and resets the shared +308 counter to RNG%40 after each due attempt. Group creation sets that counter to 2000, allowing the first unit in the same update.

Target is (10+RNG%10)*(size+1). Positive +310 delay decrements before production; after the interval test it blocks spawning when members>=target-1. For a delayed empty group, int RVA379D0D0+owner*583C !=0 selects initial target/2 batch; normal Macemen production uses batch 1. Completion requires members>=target and delay<=0. These scoped control-flow claims are extracted from AC4C5..AC52F, AC7D0..AC857, AC871..AC962, ACA8A..ACAD7 and ACD51..ACDC3, under the unchanged verified hash. No new symbolic names for unknown globals are asserted.

The incremental OutpostTest implementation is intentionally Macemen-only and uses independent bounded random draws plus saturation against acceleration short overflow; it does not claim an identical vanilla RNG stream. Save/load and owner/deletion behavior of that new implementation require their own live acceptance tests.

## Rally implementation contracts (2026-09-17) [mod integration]

Reverified canonical hash remains FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2. The installed Extender Create-tribe pattern has a single relative call at 0x11E17C resolving to 0x119C00. Unlike the dedicated outpost allocator's owner-strided scan, it scans 1..4499 and initializes Alive=2; the false third argument leaves selected tribe unchanged. Human per-unit groups can therefore use the public Create(owner,false) wrapper without a new raw allocator adapter.

The full 0x196100 disassembly confirms six Win64 inputs: ignored incoming manager, tribe ID, tile X, tile Y, patrol, flags. It writes manager/slot +0x56C based on low-byte bit7, clears that bit and calls 0x11B520 with newOrder=1. Flags 0x81 propagate moveType=1 and enable the run/formation marker. Calling its entry preserves existing MoatMove detours; installing a competing detour is unnecessary. The function returns void, so observing a forwarded call is not an arrival guarantee. Baseline signatures remain candidate; do not infer the six-argument ABI from the incomplete pseudocode declaration alone.

Implementation and live-test boundaries are recorded in Findings/Outposts.md under human rallypoints. Human Hold is deliberately per newly created singleton tribe, independent of AI production groups; pending destinations are immutable spawn snapshots. This does not retroactively alter the vanilla guard-stance findings above.

Selection follow-up (2026-09-17, same verified binary hash): own outposts reach editor check RVA 0x8A1F9 after the separate owner/restriction switch. Its CMP/JNE/MOV block spans 18 bytes, next instruction 0x8A20B. The earlier foreign-owner editor exception 0x8A051 must not be bypassed. Normal continuation sets panel 45 and pending building ID, 0x8470 commits the selected ID, and 0x19D960 panel-45 export copies GameBuilding+0x300/+0x30E/+0x310 to managed offsets 1264/1266/1268 (marry_m_name1/marry_m_name2/marry_f_name1). The managed GameData mode/submode/building-ID change branch calls InBuildingGameAction -> setUpInbuilding; Show_HUD_Main becomes false, Show_HUD_Building true. Its inSetup guard prevents initialization of the sliders from issuing writes; manual controls are not editor-gated. These are static dataflow findings, not a completed gameplay validation.

# Opt-in pathfinding table replacement audit, 2026-10-14 [Scope: Mod work, not Vanilla]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Recomputed from installed CrusaderDE.dll before implementation; it matches
CURRENT.json and the feature evidence. Installed SE: 2.14.1.0; canonical source
commit 5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3, tree
c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295.

## Confirmed native and SE contracts

Full direct profile-reader bodies and disassembly remain in
`_inspect/EnemyGateBuildingContextAudit/pathfinding-globals-evidence.txt`:
0x18E1E0, 0x196280 and 0x198ED0 read Int32 profiles from 0x322540 using the
unit's signed 16-bit type. Movement readers branch on profile zero for surface
eligibility/search; their failure paths retain normal failure/state clearing.
The third reader branches on profile zero during an active unit transition.
Profile storage capacity is 90 Int32s.

Permission reader 0x181E00 has no callees or branches. It reads signed type at
manager + gameId*0x490 + 0x6E6, then returns the Int32 at class-zero base
0x32BC48 indexed by class*0x5A + type. Classes 1..6 begin at 0x32BDB0 and
occupy 540 Int32s, with 0x168-byte rows. Symbol names in the semantic database
remain candidate-level; these machine address calculations are confirmed.

Independent installed-file PE reads confirm class 2 / archer (type 22): native
RVA 0x32BF70 contains 1; SE's stride 89 selects 0x32BF6C, containing 0.
Installed SE decompilation and canonical source agree on 89/534 span lengths
and erroneous (class-1)*89 row addressing, inherited by Can/Set. Enum values
0..88 remain valid; storage slot 89 is not a newly valid unit type.

## Additive correction and validation

APIShared/src/ScriptExtenderReplacements contains the opt-in replacement and
its standalone documentation. It validates hash, complete in-module ranges,
loaded enum metadata and public SE-resolved addresses before publishing immutable
process-lifetime state. Initialization neither compares mutable canonical values
nor writes tables. It installs no hooks and changes no existing SE callers.
BugfixesAndQoL's startup comparison consumes these complete spans and retains
the canonical-value comparison plus explicit unavailable-service diagnosis.

The canonical Fixes source's shield option uses class 1, whose row origin was
already correct. Fixes and SE sources remain unchanged; foreign live values
are preserved. No competing hook or private game member is used.

The first canonical APIShared build passed 305 tests: 164 Core, 120 runtime
and 21 preset tests. Seven new tests cover the real replacement against owned
unmanaged buffers, all 534 valid class/type pairs, neighboring writes, all storage
slots, foreign live values, invalid arguments, unavailable states and public
SE signature parity. The migration example compiled. Test-only constant
assertions were subsequently improved to inspect loaded metadata. Final build
and consumer evidence is retained under `.inspect/PathfindingReplacement/`.

The final APIShared driver again passed all 305 tests, compiled the public
example and installed successfully. BugfixesAndQoL's driver also completed
successfully, including 157367 integrated gate-routing assertions. Installed
DLL hashes match the prepared packages. A fresh Steam launch at 14:48 verified
the real SE_PATHFINDING_REPLACEMENT availability marker with profiles=90,
permissions=540, rowStride=90 and validUnitTypes=0..88; captured evidence is in
`.inspect/PathfindingReplacement/startup-evidence.txt`.

The existing Workshop updater then staged APIShared and SerpsMods and restarted
the game. It replaced the installed development APIShared DLL with published
SHA-256 8AC07D530411F93DDB443FD15C45708060C0CE31F855FAD0CA899E5A028E59DB;
the tested local development package remains SHA-256
23289CE8531A88B3F735D4D49C71E82D911EEAE9CA507B8FA33C662044110238.
Do not attribute the subsequent session to the replacement. Reinstallation and
the existing Workshop update flow must be accounted for before map acceptance.

This does not prove in-game path-search outcomes. The user explicitly deferred
map acceptance. A consumer comparison with profileLength=90/90 and
permissionLength=540/540 after startup cleanup remains pending.

## Follow-up code review, 2026-10-14

Native hash/provenance and the complete feature audit remain unchanged. Added
initialization-only validation of loaded enum underlying widths and all six
connection-class values. A new metadata regression rejects changed widths,
changed intermediate class IDs, profile values and unit count without native
access. All eight replacement tests passed; the full run passed 167 Core,
121 runtime and 21 preset tests (309 total). No further current-layout address
or bounds defect was found. The active consumer remains migrated; legacy gate
testmod code is inactive and must not be loaded with the integrated feature.
The bridge diagnostic's correct 90/540 copied snapshots are not live-view
consumers and retain their independent snapshot contract.

The final input-consistency check then rejected packaging because parallel
Workshop sources changed during the build. The user confirmed that work is
still active; further builds/installation are deferred. This review therefore
does not attest a newly installed or game-tested build. Results are retained
in `.inspect/PathfindingReplacement/review-results.txt`. The manual acceptance
guide now specifies declining the SE staged-update/restart dialog, enabling
DetailedDiagnostics and checking both initialization and complete comparison.

## Build continuation after parallel work completed

On 2026-10-14 the current APIShared source/package proof passed and the installed
DLL matched the local package (SHA-256
13699714D6F426E312622DF3DB4493BDC6F15C6B085C2466050383D3C7138A47).
The existing APIShared build was therefore reused. BugfixesAndQoL's canonical
build driver then completed tests, build and installation successfully, including
157367 integrated gate-routing assertions. Local and installed DLL hashes were
verified equal for both mods; the legacy standalone gate test remains inactive.
Evidence is in `.inspect/PathfindingReplacement/review-results.txt` and
`review-consumer-build.log` beside it. No game was started; manual map acceptance
is still pending. Versions remain unchanged during testing.

## Live map acceptance, 2026-10-14

The user confirmed a running map. The latest BepInEx startup section contains
the replacement availability marker at 15:33:13.200 and the integrated consumer
comparison at 15:33:42.868, after chainloader startup cleanup. Gate routing
reported hostFix=True and DetailedDiagnostics=True. Coverage is 90/90 profiles

Actual and expected fingerprints are both 0xC63EAAE3BB01A032; profiles Large/Default
are 13/77 and class allowed totals are 4/16/89/89/89/83. The old coverage warning,
unavailable warning, access/type/method exceptions and APIShared/QoL Error/Fatal

read path are accepted. This does not add a new claim about gameplay outcomes
or live setter exercise; exact writes remain covered by isolated tests. Evidence:
`.inspect/PathfindingReplacement/map-acceptance.txt`. No code/build/version change
was made during the running game.

# Incoming gold and periodic ExtraFeatures amounts [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2` (installed canonical DLL rechecked on 2026-10-25). This is a static machine-code finding; in-game and multiplayer acceptance remain separate.

## Producer, storage and consumer

The installed Extender exposes `GamePlayerManagerAPI.AddIncomingGood(int playerId, eGoods good, int amount)`. It validates the one-based player ID and performs a signed Int32 addition into the incoming table, through an `int*` view of `r_incomingNull`. `eGoods.STORED_GOLD` indexes `GamePlayerResources.r_incomingGold` at record offset `0x4A8`; its source declaration is UInt32, but the consumer comparison is signed. The player record stride is `0x583C`, with the first record at player manager + `0x1343FC`. Thus the player-indexed native incoming-gold address is image + `0x379B278 + playerId*0x583C`; the signed current-gold balance is image + `0x379B2DC + playerId*0x583C` (record offset `0x50C`). These addresses are evidence only, not new runtime accesses.

Three incoming-gold consumer code paths begin at RVAs `0xA4FE0`, `0xA50E0`, `0xA5200`; their dispatch-table references are `0x2DEC20`, `0x2DEC28`, `0x2DEC30`. They derive the one-based owner from the current building and skip gold processing under the existing global update/mode guards (including native mode 1 and 6). At `0xA506B`, `0xA5183`, `0xA52A3` they read incoming gold, execute TEST/JLE, and skip any zero or negative pending amount. Positive values transfer 100 when >1000, 10 when >100, otherwise 1. The same amount is subtracted from pending and added to current gold. The following writes update the two displayed gold words and the presentation-dirty flag. This is gradual delivery tied to eligible building updates, not an immediate credit or a fixed additional 400-tick settlement.

The installed Extender's `SubtractIncomingGood` clamps the pending value at zero; it cannot debit already credited gold. `SetPlayerGold` writes only the current signed gold balance; pending incoming gold remains untouched. For a real periodic debit, ExtraFeatures therefore computes max(0, balance + signed amount) with Int64 intermediate arithmetic and uses that public setter. Positive periodic amounts use the public incoming-good API, bounded by Int32.MaxValue minus nonnegative balance and pending credit. This prevents this feature from creating signed overflow without changing foreign accounting.

## Evidence and limits

All three complete leaf-code bodies were decoded directly from the hash-checked installed binary, including entry/owner setup, all guards, transfer thresholds, pending/balance writes, display writes and returns. Audit instructions and byte hashes are retained in workspace `.work/a/periodic-gold/001/native-audit.json`. The generic semantic function inventory lacks these three leaf entries; their DATA references and machine instructions establish their identity. Do not infer zero/negative support from the UInt32 field name or from successful AddIncomingGood invocation. Gold input must never be negated in Int32 (Int32.MinValue is accepted by the mod setting).

The mod installs no new native hook or direct address adapter. Its 400-tick schedule uses the existing Extender OnTick event and the public real-assembly `Director.instance.getSimTickCount()` at mission completion to avoid replaying an already saved boundary. Only started, allowed sessions subscribe; initialization, replacement, end and disabled configuration stop the ticker.

# Plague cloud height and damage eligibility [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Feature audit 2026-10-14; semantic baseline selected by CURRENT.json, crosschecked
against installed-image disassembly. Static native contracts below are confirmed;
the 20-unit testmod tolerance has no gameplay/multiplayer acceptance yet.

## Damage path

Natural D17D0 and catapult-impact 9C730 creation flow through 9B2B0. 9F960 moves
Disease and resets source elevation at 9FDB8..9FDD8 to raw tile height+20. Its
registration 9C730 visits center, eight neighbors and sixteen outer-ring tiles.
Neighbor gates 9CB6F..9CB89 and 9CC3D..9CC57 compare surface heights via 6B910
with strict absolute difference <120, followed by projectile AliveState==2.
This comparison is not the unit's actual standing height.

192750 takes manager, one-based unit ID, sentinel-based projectile slot and radius
classification 0/1/2. Its Disease branch rejects the dead marker, surface mask
10000100 (wall/elevated), and building types 40..47/74..78. It does not compare
the projectile elevation against unit base+height addition. Type immunity table
32BC40, damage 400/200/150, player resistance, HP/death and bar updates follow.
Disease skips the ordinary projectile-height check later in the same function.
The only static caller is registration 9C730; Extender wraps 192750 with its
existing projectile-damage event. The candidate linked list 4C559B0 / unit +8FA
also supplies tower/keep occupancy at 198C40: roof units need no global scan.

## Height data

Normal standing-unit calculation 184FD0 uses native base +712 plus signed +714
(GameUnit +B6/+B8, manager header 65C and stride 490). It prioritizes stairs +12,
building-backed walls +40, IsBuilding +2, then Elevated building base+C07C0.
Movement/base normalization 19B260 and unit-specific tunnel/siege/transition
branches mean raw tile height is not the actual target unit height.

C07C0 reads building type at manager+id*32C+12E, returns height by switch, and
clobbers only RAX/RCX/RDX/flags. All return branches and C0830/C0858 jump tables
were checked in installed code. It has no SIMD or mutable-memory effects.
Elevated building base is manager+id*32C+148 (GameBuilding +EC, header 5C).
6B910 adds roof height to its tile/default grid; it differs from normal-unit
wall handling and is insufficient as a universal standing-plane query.

Renderer 41D60 uses Disease material 134's surface rendering branch, independent
of the damage eligibility filter. Visual appearance on roofs does not imply
native damage eligibility there. Treatment A0470 sets fade 1016; 9A080 advances
animation/lifetime and terminal state; A0540/9F2D0 retain death/removal paths.

## Testmod evidence and limits [mod integration]

Testmods/PlagueHeightTest uses four permanent X64InlineHooks at 9FDB8 (32 bytes),
192809 (26), 9CB6F (26), 9CC3D (26). Full containing functions and hash-matching
SQLite Xrefs show no external entries into these interiors. Production generator
fixtures execute heights, both directions of the inclusive +/-20 boundary,
all native roof height switch entries, disabled originals, alive/invalid paths,
and register/stack preservation. Installed RedBird and Iced are checked by hash.

LoadContext.Memory is explicitly a snapshot; live competing patches and committed
jump/pointer forms must be read from actual module memory. Existing Extender
192750 entry ownership is preserved. Current ExtraFeatures and BugfixesAndQoL
plague features do not own these four sites. Canonical Fixes HEAD f91968217e5ece7901df45a7d90e01fb48be2b96 has no matching plague/target hook source.
This is static compatibility evidence, not combined-installation game acceptance.

Current implementation/publication contracts and pending game cases:
APIShared/UpdateToNewDLL.md, section Plague standing heights. Raw baseline exports remain unchanged.

Review fixtures additionally execute the complete installed 192750 routine plus
its jump tables. Ground hits match Vanilla's whole unit record across radius
0/1/2, resistance 0/1/2/3 and lethal/nonlethal health. The thirteen building
exclusions are removed only when enabled; height rejection, wall damage, source
self/dead/type immunity and unrelated-projectile early exclusion remain tested.
These are isolated native execution results, not a game or multiplayer run.

## Integration observation, 2026-10-23 [mod integration]

Installed native/backend hashes and the full original four spans were revalidated.
APIShared now owns these sites; ExtraFeatures is an owner-bound policy consumer.
Tests/audits formerly under Testmods/PlagueHeightTest moved to
APIShared/tests/PlagueHeight.NativeTests and workspace _inspect/PlagueHeightAudit.py.
Full native damage fixtures now also cover all 16 category combinations and
building-before-wall classification. Existing historical findings above are retained.
User reports successful in-game cloud-edge movement, wall demolition and tower
collapse on the prior testmod. This does not establish multiplayer acceptance of
the new integration or the separate category controls.

# Plague popularity: scheduling and identity contract [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Audited installed Native SHA256:
FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Audit 2026-10-08, semantic database selected by CURRENT.json; local/installed
Script Extender 2.14.0, source commit 5049b5d051d0face848cc2eb098db1fedf5451a7.
Role names below are descriptive; generic database symbols remain candidates.

## Relevant control/data flow

- Disease scheduling via 0xD1600 (callers include random-event 0xF82B0 and Chore
  dispatcher 0x1045F0) selects an eligible player's building. 0xD17D0 receives its
  building game ID and creates a herd near the building. Native placement attempts,
  bounds, map eligibility, RNG, cloud count and sounds remain Vanilla-owned.
- Projectile creation 0x9B2B0 allocates/reuses a native E8-byte slot, writes Global-ID
  at +44, state at +3C and type at +3E; type helper 0xA1DB0, movement initialization
  0xA13E0 and map registration 0x9C730 precede return. Failure may return zero.
  Projectile API IDs are native slots including a sentinel at zero; they do not use
  the unit-array index conversion. Herd-created Disease type 22 can have source
  player zero, so the source building supplies the herd owner. Catapult-generated
  Disease follows another route; this optimization does not broaden the fix.
- 0x9F960 advances projectiles: NeedsInit=1 becomes IsAlive=2; state=3 deletes through
  0x9F2D0. Movement/map checks in 0x9C730 and helper 0xA0540 can write state=3 directly.
  Type 22 dispatch at native pointer table 0x2DA9C0 + 22*8 resolves to 0x9A080; its
  expiration/fade path also writes state=3 without calling Delete in that operation.
  Therefore a Delete-only cache can still count an expired cloud before the next
  deletion. 0x9F2D0 unlinks through 0x9F490 and clears its native record through
  0x7490/memory fill. Slot reuse must additionally match Global-ID and Disease type.
- Resource scheduler 0xD1AD0 calls popularity updater 0xCB090. Its normal per-player
  path computes Vanilla's timed plague modifier and writes the accumulator before
  the common report write at 0xCB57C. Some special player/mode branches bypass this
  block. At the existing correction boundary, R14 identifies the player, signed AX
  is the Vanilla plague contribution, EDX the accumulated popularity, and
  R12+RBP+12EC20 the authoritative accumulator. Both EDX and that memory value must
  replace the old plague contribution; AX supplies the corresponding report.
  Subsequent components and Vanilla's final 0..10000 clamp remain authoritative.
- A previously managed player must remain eligible for zero-herd correction after
  the last cloud expires; otherwise Vanilla's remaining timed penalty can reappear.
  The save payload preserves ManagedPlayerIds independently from surviving herds.

## Managed publisher boundary

Installed Extender source BulkProjectileDetours confirms Spawn/Delete Pre/Post are
synchronous around the original operation. Delete Pre may change ProjectileId or
skip Original; skip produces no Post. Original receives the changed ID, whereas
Post is built with the original argument. Consequently Post's reported slot may
still contain its old living identity. Revalidate that identity before deleting
the index entry, and reconcile the actual player's living clouds at popularity.

The existing popularity hook is the sufficient authoritative reconciliation point;
an additional global OnTick scan is unnecessary. Full reconciliation is still
required before serialization. Original creation remains exactly once, with nested
capture restored in finally; native creation and random state are untouched.

Confidence: selected branch/offset/dispatch/identity and accumulator flows are
confirmed by semantic decompilation, installed-image disassembly/table inspection
and current managed APIs. Generic native role names are not confirmed symbols.
No gameplay timing, FPS gain or multiplayer acceptance is inferred from this audit.
The optimization leaves hook addresses, displacement and backend unchanged.

## Watchdog opportunity audit (2026-10-23) [mod integration]

Rechecked against the same installed native SHA256 above. The Extender's existing
OnPlayerCalculatePopularity Pre publisher replaces the calculation span at
0xCB16E..0xCB4B5. The native continuation from 0xCB4B5 through the plague branches
converges at the existing correction boundary 0xCB57C, including the no-plague
branch. The earlier special-player/mode bypasses do not emit that calculation
event. This was checked against the complete intervening instruction flow and
the managed PlayerCalculatePopularityEventArgs/PlayerR3EventHooks contract.

Therefore an observed Pre for the watched player and revision proves a calculation
opportunity; elapsed simulation time alone does not. A three-second diagnostic
window with no such event is not evidence of a missing correction. Successful
correction, replacement revisions, deactivation and session end invalidate the
watch, including already queued timer callbacks. This diagnostic change adds no
native hook and does not narrow zero-herd correction eligibility. The isolated
runtime tests exercise player/revision separation and stale callbacks; actual
gameplay acceptance remains a separate test.

# Player defeat observation audit [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Audited native build: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.

Reproduce the primary evidence packages from the workspace root:

```powershell
& '_inspect\CrusaderDE-Native-Baseline\tools\semantic\query.ps1' function 0xCDE60
& '_inspect\CrusaderDE-Native-Baseline\tools\semantic\query.ps1' function 0x1D160
& '_inspect\CrusaderDE-Native-Baseline\tools\semantic\query.ps1' function 0x57330
& '_inspect\CrusaderDE-Native-Baseline\tools\semantic\query.ps1' callers 0x1D160
& '_inspect\CrusaderDE-Native-Baseline\tools\semantic\query.ps1' callees 0xCDE60
```

`FUN_1800cde60` (RVA `0xCDE60`, structurally verified) is the simulation-loop path that calls
`FUN_18001d160` (RVA `0x1D160`) before downstream player/lord processing in
`FUN_180057330` (RVA `0x57330`). `FUN_18001d160` is the normal runtime writer of the
player `r_WinLossState` and checks lord validity periodically; save loading is a separate writer
and therefore must be treated as baseline state rather than a new transition.

The relevant `GamePlayerResources` fields are relative offsets `r_LordUnitId = 0x21F8`,
`r_IsPaused = 0x2210`, and `r_WinLossState = 0x2244`. Player and unit game IDs are one-based.
The installed Script Extender exposes these records and unit identity/alive fields directly.

APIShared consequently observes all eight player records from `GameTimeManagerAPI.OnTick`
only after the first subscriber registers. The first tick after that registration is
baseline-only, including registration during an existing mission; earlier deaths/losses
are not replayed. Without subscribers, the callback performs no state/resource/unit reads.
This consumer-demand contract was approved and covered by service regression tests on
2026-10-11; the native simulation and ID contracts below remain unchanged.
The hook is pre-tick, so mutations made by the current native simulation step become visible on
the next tick. A living lord identity arms the early edge; disappearance, invalidation, or death
then emits once unless another living identity has already replaced it. Independently, entry into
`WinLossState.Loss` emits the official defeat edge, including lordless scenarios. The first
observation of every session is baseline-only, which prevents loaded saves from replaying events.

No additional native detour is installed: melee/projectile hooks omit other causes, unit deletion
is late, the game-over presentation callback is local and late, and the AI-state hook is not an
elimination contract. Tick observation covers Vanilla `KillUnit`, fire, scripts, and direct state
changes without adding another version-sensitive hook surface.

Local SE source commit `5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3`, tree
`c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295`, matches database provenance.
Installed SHCDESE assembly version: 2.14.1.0. Its GameGlobalsManager declarations
were independently decompiled and the consumer type-checked against that DLL.

## Audited path and scope

Current-hash semantic records: resource scheduler 0xD1AD0 calls popularity updater
0xCB090 outside the excluded app modes. The updater rebuilds church/cathedral
counts through 0xCCD20, iterates player IDs 1..8, and checks player eligibility.
Special app-mode branches assign fixed popularity; small-population protection
can assign 7500 instead of executing the component block. These bypasses remain
authoritative; configuring a contribution does not force those branches to run.

The ordinary component block selects ration, food-variety, crowding and tax
contributions, followed by fair, blessing/building, ale and fear contributions.
The SE's existing inline replacement reads 41 ManagedValue<int> parameters for
these contributions, 13 separate coverage/ratio thresholds, and publishes
OnPlayerCalculatePopularity(Pre). This event is before subsequent native event
penalties and the final clamp, not a final-popularity notification.

The names above are semantic role descriptions. Generic database function names
retain their candidate classification. The component branches, constants and
managed replacement are supported by the current-hash decompiler records and
the matching SE implementation; no new hook span or instruction claim is made.

## Display scale and defaults

Total popularity uses 100 internal units per displayed point (0..10000 internally).
Component reports instead divide their signed contribution by 25; this is directly
visible in the current managed FatControler consumer. Configuring component points
therefore multiplies by 25, not 100.

| Components | Defaults in report points |
|---|---|
| Rations None/Half/Full/Extra/Double | -8/-4/0/+4/+8 |
| No preferred/available food; no population | -8; +8 |
| Food variety exactly 2/3/4 types | +1/+2/+3 |
| Crowding 101..120/121..140/141..160/161..180/>180% | -2/-4/-6/-8/-10 |
| Taxes modes HugeDonation through Cruellest | +7/+5/+3/+1/-2/-4/-6/-8/-12/-16/-20/-24 |
| Donation without positive gold; unknown mode | +1; -24 |
| Fair event flag active | +16 |
| Blessing 25..49/50..74/75..94/>=95% | +2/+4/+6/+8 |
| At least one church; at least one cathedral | +1; +2 (additive, not per building) |
| Ale coverage 25..49/50..74/75..99/100% | +2/+4/+6/+8 |
| Fear coefficient, multiplied by signed fear boost | +1 per level |

Ration-mode contribution requires positive population and preferred-food state;
otherwise the separate fallback applies. Food variety is added independently.
Donation selection requires positive gold for modes below None. Thresholds use
strict > for religion (24/49/74/94), >= for ale (25/50/75/100), and strict > for
overpopulation (100/120/140/160/180). Ale coverage helper 0xCEA90 computes the
coverage from inn state and population and clamps to 0..100. Configuring the
coefficient does not change those producers or thresholds.

## Downstream effects and acceptance limits

The replacement updates the normal contribution report fields, the current
popularity accumulator and its worst-source selection, then resumes the remaining
native path. Plague and other timed events continue afterwards; the existing
BugfixesAndQoL plague correction at 0xCB57C remains outside this mod's ownership.
Vanilla clamps the final total to 0..10000 and retains its popularity-change
speech/history decisions. Report producer 0x19D960 independently recomputes component values using hardcoded
Vanilla constants; it does NOT consume the SE replacement contribution fields.
The original 2026-10-16 claim that these report fields followed SE values was incorrect.

Religion also adds `(uint)combinedReligionContribution / 25` to
`r_UnknownPopularityAccumulationByCurrentDividedBy25`. The SE preserves this
unsigned native bookkeeping expression. A negative configured religion sum
therefore has a large unsigned quotient in that auxiliary counter. Its gameplay
meaning is unconfirmed; do not claim that negative religion values preserve all
unrelated statistics. PopularityTest intentionally exposes the existing direct SE
parameters and adds no correction hook. Negative modifiers' complete in-game
effects and report presentation still require runtime acceptance.

No game UI or real multiplayer acceptance is inferred from source/type checks.
PopularityTest's independent catalog/UI checks compare all 41 SE defaults and
exercise signed settings, persistence and anonymous-stack ownership separately.

## Display-path correction audit (2026-10-17)

Native hash above unchanged; managed SHA-256
`BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
Installed SE 2.14.2 still replaces the simulation block only. Latest game log:
15:37:34 applied 17 overrides; 15:37:40 callback accumulator=10025 with 17 active
(overall final delta is not logged). The earlier loaded save had zero overrides.

Confirmed static flow: native 0x19D960 -> PlayStateReturnData ->
EngineInterface.CopyPlayStateStruct -> GameMap -> GameData.setGameState ->
FatControler.NoesisGUIUpdateChecksInGame -> public MainViewModel properties.
The native report contains hardcoded contributions for all eight groups and builds
upcoming_total_popularity from these plus the existing event amounts. Ration and
tax modes incorporate the selected panel preview. food_types_available carries
the same native preferred-food field used by the simulation. Fear uses the signed
fear_factor. Crowding report amounts identify its selected tier (-50..-250).
Religion coverage thresholds: 25/50/75/95, ale: 25/50/75/100.

Vanilla church_adjustment (25/50/75) is copied from byte to sbyte and serves both
as a numeric bonus and building identity for localized labels. Do not replace it
with configurable values: signed/large settings overflow and break label dispatch.
PopularityTest corrects only public HUD text properties after the existing
APIShared GuiChecks publisher, preserving PlayState and native simulation.
The report's zero-population ration value is zero whereas simulation uses +200;
when that explicit fallback is enabled its absolute effective value is displayed.
Thus that known Vanilla discrepancy is not a valid default-equality assertion.

The GUI callback also owns the increase/decrease booleans and event-details-button
visibility (the latter depends on the displayed event sum). Public text setters
update their associated face icons. Panel wire values 16:{2,3,4,69,72,73,79} are
Vanilla protocol constants; SE exposes no corresponding panel enum. Normal GUI
checks also run paused. No new native hook ownership is introduced.

Runtime acceptance of the correction, including multiplayer, remains pending.

## Transfer to APIShared (2026-10-17) [mod integration]

The user confirmed the original PopularityTest correction working in-game. The
reusable calculator and presentation adapter now live in APIShared ScriptExtenderFixes.
This transfer reads effective SE values independently of consumer toggles and only
corrects values differing from Vanilla. Consequently the zero-population discrepancy
above remains Vanilla when its SE modifier is unchanged. The 13 separate threshold
parameters are outside this correction's scope. Simulation and override ownership
remain unchanged. The transferred implementation still requires separate game,
editor/save/load and real host/client acceptance; no installation is part of this task.

## Fractional fear coefficients (2026-10-18)

Same native fingerprint; the installed SE fingerprint audited for the managed adapter is
`577F9AAB5DE504BE0BFA2193C7DEB734B26076ECBBAF0A408FC9ABC4CC5E7175`.
The SE callback has two signed-boost multiplication paths (getter/GetValue, signed local,
`mul`), then stores `r_GoodBadThingsPopularityModifier`, adds to the accumulator and
compares with the previous worst component before publishing the Pre event. A correction
only at that event is too late to preserve the worst-source decision. APIShared therefore
changes just those managed multiplication instructions through one permanent adapter;
no new native span is installed. It rounds signed level times exact decimal coefficient
away from zero at midpoint ties, then multiplies whole report points by 25. No registration
leaves the original unchecked SE product intact. Existing eligibility bypasses and later
native events/clamp remain unchanged. Display correction uses that same calculator.
Static installed-body generation and pure fixtures passed; actual Mono/game, editor,
save/load and host/client acceptance remain outstanding for the new adapter.

## Semantic SE compatibility (2026-10-18)

The original SE hash above remains historical audit evidence. It no longer gates the
rounded fear adapter. Startup discovers the owner from coefficient access plus native
contribution storage, checks loaded/disk module identity, and analyzes CFG/stack/locals
and ref/out resource-pointer provenance. All coefficient reads/products must reach the
signed-fear multiplication and 32-bit contribution of the same player resources. Site
count, generated carrier/method names, local encoding and operand order are not fixed.
Unknown or ambiguous meaning fails closed; native game/report fingerprints remain their
separate ABI boundaries. The game and native calculation audited earlier are unchanged.


## 2026-10-18: managed IL operand representation

The installed Extender fear method has two audited coefficient sites. Inside MonoMod ILContext.Invoke its branches use ILLabel/ILLabel[] operands; direct Cecil-only CFG traversal falsely reported unreachable coefficient access. APIShared now resolves and validates label targets without mutating operands. This is a managed-analysis correction; the hash-bound native formula, resource identity, signed input and hook sites remain unchanged. Offline regression invokes the real installed method through ILContext.Invoke; runtime gameplay acceptance is still required.

## Fear-level production and fixed contributions (2026-10-25)

Native SHA-256 remains `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
The current raw function/instruction packets were compared with the canonical installed
DLL: 3,734 instructions across 0xBCEB0, 0xCD850, 0xCB090, 0x19D960, 0xD1AD0 and
0x180560 matched byte-for-byte. Generic function names retain their candidate labels;
the following local machine/data-flow observations are confirmed-static.

The resource scheduler 0xD1AD0 calls building recount 0xBCEB0 before productivity
0xCD850 and the popularity component path 0xCB090. Recount clears counts and level
for all eight player slots, excludes building statuses 0 and 3, and classifies owned
building types using the native ranges/bitmask. Bad types are 62..64 and 91..98;
good types in this exact build are 65, 66, 100, 101 and 103. This records the observed
classification, not an assumption that every decorative building counts.

Resource identity is anchored by manager VA 0x18366C210 (scheduler caller 0xCDE60),
record stride 0x583C and native slot prefix 0x12EBC0. Slot 1 begins at manager+0x1343FC,
matching the Extender array. Signed fear boost at struct+0x2134 is native slot+0x130CF4;
its neighboring bad/good counts are struct+0x212C/+0x2130 and total population +0x2180.
The independent report producer copies those same count/level fields. For nonnegative
population, recount computes denominator = trunc(population/16)+1, then
level = clamp(trunc((goodCount-badCount)/denominator), -5, +5). Division truncates toward
zero (signed IDIV); equal counts retain the zero from the initial clear. The next-stage
field records the remaining net buildings needed. Thus population 100 requires seven
net buildings for each level. Building count, population and ownership are inputs;
a popularity-contribution override does not change this producer.

Productivity is separately 100-10*level percent for native levels -5..5, clamped at
150/50 percent at the extremes by 0xCD850. The popularity path multiplies the signed
level by 25 internal report units; its result reaches component storage, accumulator
and worst-source selection before events and the final popularity clamp. Report
0x19D960 independently computes level*25, so the API display correction uses the same
selected contribution as simulation. 0x180560 independently consumes the level in its
own arithmetic; changing the popularity contribution leaves that input untouched.

APIShared's fixed-level tables use the existing managed multiplication adapter, with
no new hook or change to native branches. Tables select on the signed input level,
not the sign of the configured output. Unspecified levels reveal earlier applicable
registrations or the complete original SE multiplication. Level zero stays neutral.
The Extender's configurable multiplier directly exposes Vanilla's constant 25; that
is a technical explanation, not evidence of the author's personal design motivation.
Actual game, report/preview and real host/client acceptance remain separate.

## Human/AI targeting feasibility (2026-10-25) [mod integration]

Canonical native SHA-256 was rechecked and remains
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
The earlier complete scheduler/component/report audit above therefore remains the
native contract; no new native address or hook span is proposed here. The installed
SHCDESE 2.14.3.0 assembly SHA-256 is
`5CB1C33BE5463086505A17F5C48AAA357D733CFFF7240E101C821F0E3C668498`.
Its actual BulkPlayerDetours and GamePlayerManagerAPI bodies were decompiled for
this feasibility check; generic native function labels retain their earlier trust
classification. The managed observations below are confirmed-static.

The popularity replacement already obtains the current native player ID from R15
and resolves that same player's resource pointer before reading the component
parameters. GamePlayerManagerAPI publicly exposes IsAIPlayer(playerId), backed by
the AI-lord lineup. Classification must use a valid participating slot; a false AI
result alone does not prove that an empty or invalid slot is an active human.

All ordinary popularity coefficients currently come from global ManagedValue<int>
objects. ExtraFeatures publishes its owned overrides for the session, and the
existing FearPopularity selection accepts a level without player identity. These
interfaces do not currently support Human/AI targeting. Existing calculation
context makes such a capability feasible, but both the ordinary coefficient reads
and the fear selection would need player-aware selection before their consumers.
Unmatched players must retain existing SE/foreign values and the original branches.

The installed callback raises OnPlayerCalculatePopularity(Pre) only after component
stores, the auxiliary unsigned religion accumulation and worst-source comparisons.
Changing only its final Popularity value cannot reproduce player-specific component
semantics. The native event/clamp path and eligibility/small-population bypasses
remain independently authoritative. Temporarily changing global stacks per player
would also expose transient global values to other readers; it is not a verified
targeting mechanism.

The independent report path follows the selected native viewpoint. APIShared's
current presentation snapshot captures component inputs but does not select ordinary
or fear policies by that player's identity. A future targeting implementation must
apply the same player-specific selection to simulation, report and previews; the
existing public PlayerPerspectiveAPI.GetViewedPlayerId is the relevant identity
boundary, including uncertainty handling. No targeting behavior, lifecycle roster
timing or real multiplayer execution was implemented or runtime-tested in this check.

## Targeted policy implementation audit (2026-10-25) [mod integration]

This is an additional dated implementation observation, retaining the preceding
feasibility snapshot. Native SHA-256 remains
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`;
installed SE 2.14.3 SHA-256 is
`5CB1C33BE5463086505A17F5C48AAA357D733CFFF7240E101C821F0E3C668498`.
Managed game report identity remains BC8B6A39 as documented above.
Evidence: workspace `.work/a/pop-targets/001` (installed method/player API
extraction) and `.work/a/pop-human-ai/001` (tests, review and delivery).

Native scheduler 0xD1AD0 calls 0xCB090 only for eligible resource slots. Its
signed checks at manager offsets 0x12EC54 and 0x12ED94 require values >0.
Subtracting resource base 0x12EBC0 yields public `r_KeepId` +0x94 and
`r_KeepDoorId` +0x1D4, with slot stride 0x583C. The targeting classifier uses
these typed public fields to exclude empty/unresolved slots, then the public
SE `IsAIPlayer` query. `ActivePlayerListVA` must not be interpreted as a human
roster: its values distinguish native slot activity, not controller type.

The installed SE callback reads its player ID from the native callback argument's
`NativePointer<X64SmartCPUContext>.Pointer->R15`, narrows to Int32 and passes that
same value to `TryGetPlayerResourcesById`. The new startup data-flow validator
requires the resource pointer for every resource access and source read to be
that resolver's output, and the ID local to retain that same origin. It covers
all declared ordinary source getter/GetValue reads and the existing fear products.
The rewritten real method is generated and JIT-prepared by installed-assembly
tests; a counterexample replacing R15 by R14 is rejected before player edits
and retains the independent legacy fear manipulation.

Selection occurs immediately after successful resource resolution. Each ordinary
GetValue result is replaced only for the captured role/source; missing entries
retain its effective foreign/global value. Fear consumes the same captured policy.
Original arithmetic/branches, strongest-component comparisons, religion auxiliary
bookkeeping, event paths and final clamp remain downstream. No native hooks,
global stack swaps, per-read locks, allocations or roster scans were added.
The independent report adapter captures the viewed player's policy and applies it
to its detached component/preview data. Explicit targeted values equal to a SE
default remain present, covering the known zero-population report discrepancy.

Automated tests prove installed managed data flow and isolated policy/report
behavior. They do not execute native gameplay or establish Mono rendering,
save/load gameplay or Host/Client acceptance; those remain separate game checks.

# Prebuilt AI workshop production [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Installed `CrusaderDE.dll` SHA-256:
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Addresses below are RVAs for this hash. Evidence is the semantic decompiler export, the installed Script Extender interop, and the Frederick runtime trace below.

## Vanilla path

- Skirmish setup `0x94350` prepares the selected AIV and, with the complete AI castle option, sets that player's bit in the prebuilt-player field before calling `0x55F50`.
- Completed castle execution `0x55F50` enters frame executor `0x51790`. After a successful workshop placement through `0x6D580`, the frame executor calls production initializer `0x31000`. Ordinary AI construction also calls the same initializer.
- `0x31000` reads the player's AI Lord slot. A zero slot returns without writing production. For nonzero slots, AIC offsets `0xCC`, `0xD0`, and `0xD4` respectively configure blacksmiths, fletchers, and poleturners. The editor represents Both with `-999`.
- For Both, `0x31000` calls `0xBEC10` and writes the chosen good to both building offsets `0x28E` and `0x290`. The Script Extender names these `r_NextProducedGoodId` and `r_ProducedGoodId`.
- `0xBEC10` counts alive (`2`) workshops of the same owner and building type, reading the next good at `0x28E`. It counts every good other than the tested good as the opposite side. Fletcher ties select bows (`0x11`), poleturner ties spears (`0x13`), and blacksmith ties swords (`0x16`). The scan includes a just placed workshop if its alive state is already `2`.
- Both audited `0x51790` workshop placement branches set the new building's alive state to `NeedsInit` (`1`) immediately before calling `0x31000`. The current workshop therefore does not contribute to `0xBEC10` in these paths. In ordinary staged AIV construction, previously placed workshops contribute only once they have become alive (`2`); the complete-castle path processes its frames together before those earlier workshops advance. The correction models the consecutive choices that the same balancer makes when each previous workshop is already active, using the same two production fields as `0x31000`.

The installed editor's `PnlEditLordViewModel` maps Both to `-999`. Extracted Vanilla AIC data contains `fletchers_make = -999` for Baldwin, and his bundled AIVs contain several fletcher frames. This gives a reproduction scenario without modifying `testlord_serp`.

## Diagnostic boundary [mod integration]

`BuildingR3EventHooks.OnBuildingSpawn` Post fires after the native spawn call and before the caller's `0x31000` initializer. The testmod captures the Lord slot and AIC value there. Its correction is limited to a new complete-castle start with a confirmed Both AIC value and prebuilt workshops that retain `NeedsInit` and both default goods at managed start. Save loads and later workshop construction are outside the correction scope. The earlier zero-slot theory was refuted by the Frederick trace and was removed from the correction condition.

## Frederick runtime observation, 2026-09-27

The first local game session used a new custom game with seven Frederick AI players and complete starting castles. The testmod observed 41 prebuilt fletcher/blacksmith spawn events. Every event reported native Lord slot `10` and roster Lord `SK_FREDERICK`; the completed-start bitfield was `0xFE`. The zero-slot early return at `0x31000` is therefore not the cause for these observed spawns. The mod correctly made no production changes. Two subsequent new-game sessions without completed castles reported no prebuilt workshops and no production changes. The static Extender event and first-tick marker ran after startup cleanup.

This first diagnostic build logged no production goods for the 41 captured IDs because its startup scan filtered for `AliveState.IsAlive`. A newly spawned workshop may still be `AliveState.NeedsInit`; the absence of lines does not establish an absent or invalid building. A follow-up diagnostic must read those IDs directly and log alive state, AIC setting and both production fields at spawn, native-start completion, managed start and first tick before assigning a different cause.

## Frederick production trace, 2026-09-27

A second new game with a complete castle for player 2 yielded five captured workshops: fletchers `35`, `322`, `325` and blacksmiths `37`, `327`. At spawn, native-start completion, managed start, and simulation tick 1, every fletcher was `AliveState.NeedsInit`, with both production fields set to `STORED_BOWS`. The live Frederick AIC reported `fletchers_make = -999` at every observation and the native Lord slot was `10` at spawn. The blacksmiths used their fixed AIC value `22` and had both fields set to `STORED_SWORDS`.

This ties the observed default-only Fletcher result to the `0xBEC10` filter: it counts only alive-state `2` workshops, so the other prebuilt fletchers still in state `1` do not influence each subsequent Both choice. The call path through `0x51790` invokes `0x31000` after successful placement; the runtime trace by itself does not instrument entry to `0x31000`, so the exact execution count is supported by static control flow rather than a direct call trace. The original zero-Lord hypothesis is refuted for these sessions. No production values were changed by the diagnostic mod.

The bounded correction now plans choices in ascending captured building-ID order. It begins with existing alive workshops of the same player and type, then adds each planned prebuilt choice to the balancing counts before choosing the next. For fletcher IDs `35`, `322`, `325` with no alive fletcher baseline, this produces bows, crossbows, bows. It writes both production fields only after every captured group member still matches the confirmed `NeedsInit`/default-goods state. The next trace confirms this behavior in a new Frederick game.

## Frederick correction trace, 2026-09-27 [mod integration]

A subsequent new complete-castle game for Frederick as player 2 captured three fletchers, IDs `34`, `246`, `247`, and two blacksmiths, IDs `36`, `248`. The prebuilt bitfield was `0x00000002`; the Lord slot was `10`, and Fletcher AIC value `-999` was stable from spawn through the first tick. Before correction all three fletchers were `NeedsInit` with both fields set to bows. At managed start the correction planned bows, crossbows, bows in ascending ID order, then wrote both fields for the group. First-tick snapshots confirmed that the crossbow choice persisted in both fields for ID `246`, with bows retained for IDs `34` and `247`. The blacksmith AIC value was the fixed swords value `22`; both blacksmiths retained swords in both fields. The post-startup-cleanup first-tick marker fired and this game section contains no testmod error or exception.

This confirms the correction through simulation tick 1 for the Frederick Fletcher case. Later production cycles, Both-configured blacksmiths and poleturners, save loading, and multiplayer remain separate runtime checks.

# Minimap (radar) pass 0xF5A40 (FBCB9319) [Scope: Vanilla]

Native DLL SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2` (verified against the installed DLL on 2026-10-23). The addresses below are RVAs/VAs for this binary only.

Evidence:
- semantic pseudocode `exports/semantic-decompiled-functions.c`;
- Rizin disassembly of the call site and of the whole function (`pdr`, 0x1800F5A40–0x1800F6DDD);
- managed decompilation of `Assembly-CSharp` `BC8B6A39…`;
- PerfProbe thread sampler (2026-10-23, 63 633 sim-thread samples, `0xF5A40` self share 42.1 %).

## Call

- `DLL_RunTick` (`0x86680`, confirmed) calls `0xF5A40` at `0x86B9B` unconditionally on every tick, including paused ticks (the call is after the `paused` block).
- Arguments:
  - `rcx` = `&0x183496220` (radar object);
  - `rdx` = `retData`;
  - `r8` = `radarMap` (managed `MemoryBuffers.MemBuffer.radarMap`, pinned in `EngineInterface.run`);
  - `r9d` = `screenCentrePosX`;
  - stack: `screenCentrePosY`, `screenTilesWide`, `screenTilesHigh`, `radarMapWidth`, `radarMapHeight`, `radarZoom`, `0`.
  - Ghidra shows 9 parameters; Rizin reads stack arguments up to `arg_48h`.
- Trust level: confirmed (call site and argument names from the `DLL_RunTick` export signature).

## Work

- An 800-row tile walk with rotation variants selected by `0x1860AD40C` (0/2/4/6).
- Per minimap pixel inside the radar window it reads:
  - the tile index (`0x183B4ACE4`);
  - the unit on the tile (`0x184C559B0` → unit record `0x1867E8xxx`, stride `0x490`/`0x248`);
  - the diplomacy table `0x1837EDF3C` (colour against the local player `0x1888E3D70`);
  - tile flag layers (`0x1848F71B0`, `0x184A312B0`, `0x18485A770`, `0x184DDD350`, `0x184EC82B0`, `0x184F64CF0`);
  - the colour tables `0x1803126xx`/`0x1803127xx`/`0x180312880`.
- Afterwards it draws the camera frame (`0xFFFFFFFF`) with a thickness depending on the radar width (`+0x44` < 0x100, < 0x1F0, else).
- No callees.

## Writes (complete: 27 non-stack stores)

- 26 stores through `r12` = `radarMap`: ARGB pixels (two horizontal pixels per tile) and the frame.
- 1 store at `0x1800F64B7` into `*(radar+0x70)[row*width+col]`: the tile index per minimap pixel (click lookup).
- No store through `retData` and none to absolute globals.

## Readers

- `radarMap`: managed only. `Director.Update` → `GameMap.processTestMap(…, radarMap)` → `ApplyRadarMap` (texture upload). The save radar uses a separate buffer (`0x183496298` via `0xF6FB0`).
- `radar+0x70` table: allocated by `0xF6F80` (`DLL_GameAction` 0x406 = `ResizeRadarMapBuffer`, 1030; `c_game_malloc(0x271000)`).
  - Read only by `0xF6F20` (`DLL_GameAction` 0x404 = `RadarClicked`, 1028, from `FatControler`).
  - On a non-zero entry `0xF6F20` calls `0x50220` on the view object `0x183A11DC0` (camera jump to that tile) and sets `0x183A11E48 = 1`.
- Other methods of the radar object (`0xF4C50`, `0xF4D40`, `0xF4DF0`, `0xF6FB0`, `0xF7210`) do not access `+0x70`.

## Call contract and managed buffer ring (audit 2026-10-23, capstone over the installed DLL)

- `0x86B9B` is the only direct caller (`E8` scan over `.text`); no absolute pointer, RIP-relative `lea`/`mov` or `jmp` references `0xF5A40`.
- The call passes 11 arguments: `rcx`, `rdx`, `r8`, `r9d` and seven stack dwords at `[rsp+0x20..0x50]` (`0x86B4C..0x86B82`); the last one is `r12d`. The return value is not used (`0x86BA0` reloads `r8d` from a global).
- Entry prologue: `mov [rsp+0x10],rbx` (5 bytes) + `push rbp` (1) end at `0xF5A46`, so a 6-byte Indirect detour ends on an instruction boundary; the remaining prologue continues at `0xF5A46`.
- Managed side (`Assembly-CSharp` `BC8B6A39…`): `EngineInterface.run` takes a free `MemoryBuffers.MemBuffer` from a pool of `NUM_BUFFERS = 6` and passes its `radarMap` array; `Director.Update` processes up to three filled buffers per frame in `frameID` order, `GameMap.processTestMap` stores each buffer's `radarMap` in `lastRadarMap`, and `GameMap.ApplyRadarMap` uploads only the last one once per frame (`SetPixelData`, `Apply`, `MainViewModel.TestRadarMap`).
- Consequence: if `0xF5A40` is skipped for one tick, that buffer still holds the image from its previous fill (up to six ticks old). Uploading it would make the minimap jump back; a throttle must keep the previous `lastRadarMap` for such buffers.

## Classification

- Presentation and local camera input only. Nothing the simulation reads, so skipping or delaying it does not change simulation state or MP synchronisation.
- Output depends on every tick (unit positions, ownership colours, camera), so exact reuse is impossible.
- Paused ticks still cost 5.1–6.5 ms against 6.6–6.9 ms running (managed `EngineInterface.run` timing, 40 ticks/s, `test_dustyFPS2.sav`). This is consistent with presentation passes (`0xF5A40`, `0x41D60`) dominating the tick.
- Uncertain:
  - the exact meaning of `radar+0x48` (mode value read at entry) and of the frame-thickness thresholds;
  - per-map cost scaling (measured only on the maps above).

# Raid target selection and attack access (FBCB9319) [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native DLL SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`. The addresses below are RVAs for this binary only.

- `0x29190` appends a living building to its owner's bounded candidate list without checking raid-unit reachability or distance. `0x2C620` selects a building from that list using one of three 47-type priority tables. The Extender's `eStructs` enum identifies type `0x13` as `STRUCT_GRANARY` and `0x14` as `STRUCT_QUARRY`; both are intentional Vanilla candidates, regardless of whether this is desirable raid policy.
- `0x2C620` selects table RVA `0x2C7F80` when global `0x856A6D2 & 7` is 0-1, `0x2C7EC0` for 2-3, and `0x2C7E00` for 4-7. Their first priorities are respectively granary/armoury/churches, apple/cattle/wheat/hops farms followed by granary, and quarry/iron mine/pitch digger/wheat/hops/apple farm. All three tables also contain non-farm targets, including inns and barracks; wall tiles are not building entries in these lists.
- `0x2AE40` schedules the raid update `0x3E200`. For its ordinary harassment-group branch, `0x3E200` validates the stored target at tribe offsets `0x622` (building ID) and `0x626` (global ID), selects a replacement through `0x2C620` when needed, and calls `0x199C70` with command 9, building ID and global ID. The latter forwards to `0x11E960`.
- Command 9 in `0x11E960` writes building ID/global ID at manager-relative offsets `0x64C`/`0x650` plus `tribeId * 0x688`. The tribe array begins at manager offset `0x2A`, so these are the same stored-target fields at tribe-relative `0x622`/`0x626`; there is no second command-target pair at tribe-relative `0x64C`/`0x650`. The function filters eligible units, calls `0xDA020` to enumerate building attack positions, then `0x123090` to rank reachable candidates. Selected units receive movement through `0x196280`. The building can remain the stored raid target even when no suitable approach is assigned.
- `0xDA020` checks candidate positions around the building with height, occupancy and player-specific path-component conditions. It also has an alternate route check. A building's worker delivery access point is a separate contract and does not demonstrate a valid melee attack position.
- `0xDA020` writes 12-byte candidate records in the pathfinding context beginning at offset `0x1B344`; the first two 32-bit fields hold a position and its building-attack tile. `0x123090` filters/sorts this list, and command 9 tests the second field of the first record at offset `0x1B348` before issuing per-unit movement. The list is shared scratch state and must not be treated as a current command's result unless the command reached its candidate-generation path.
- List-end contract, checked against the installed machine code on 2026-10-01: `0x123090` iterates while the approach field is nonzero (`0x123228` and `0x1232B1`) and writes only a zero approach field at the filtered end (`0x1232C2`). The building field and score at that sentinel, and records beyond it, may retain old values. `0xDA020` normally clears both approach and building fields at its generated end (`0xDA56B`/`0xDA577`), but the filtered list must use the approach-only sentinel. A reader requiring both fields to be zero can consume stale tail records. The runtime bounds the read to 500 records; a missing sentinel within that limit remains uncertain.
- The command-9 consumer calls the builder at `0x11FF9A`, the filter at `0x11FFA7`, and checks the first building field at `0x11FFAC`; zero branches past the complete per-unit movement pass. Later paired records cannot rescue a failed first building-field gate. An empty list or a zero first building field therefore means no usable melee point only when the result is associated with the current command. Identical pre/post contents alone do not prove whether the search ran again or was bypassed; even two freshly generated empty lists can be identical. Ignored sentinel/tail fields must not manufacture a content-change freshness signal.
- `0x2C620` scans up to 100 16-bit building IDs in the victim player's resource record at offsets `0x3560..0x3627`; the 32-bit count is at `0x3628`. It compares each building type with the 47 entries in the priority table selected by global `0x856A6D2 & 7`. An equal-ranked later list entry replaces the earlier selection. `0x3E200` writes the selected building ID/global ID and a 100-tick raid pause after issuing command 9, so a post-command correction of its stored target must run after that outer call has returned.
- For the observed harassment group 0 (storage role 180), `0x3E200` reaches `0x2C620` when it needs a new building target. Neither `0x29190` nor this selection branch compares candidate coordinates with the group or previous target; same-rank ties follow candidate-list order, not proximity. Vanilla also has a distance-scoring selector at `0x2C710`, called by `0x30E90`, but the observed group-0 branch in `0x3E200` does not call it. This establishes behavior for this native path, not a claim about every game AI target selector.
- The `0x3560` and `0x3628` offsets above use the native record origin `module+0x379AE2C+playerId*0x583C`. `GamePlayerManagerAPI.TryGetPlayerResourcesById(playerId)` returns a pointer 0x5C bytes before that origin, so the same list/count are at API-pointer offsets `0x35BC` and `0x3684`. In the 2026-09-30 runtime log, module base `0x7FFEDE870000`, the Extender's player-1 resource pointer `0x7FFEE201060C`, and native player-1 list address `0x7FFEE2013BC8` independently establish that 0x5C displacement. Reading the unadjusted offsets yielded a false count of zero after Vanilla selected live granary `119/6450`.
- `0x2DC30` gates raid updates using tribe counters at offsets `0x5EA`, `0x5EC` and `0x5F0`; their exact gameplay meanings are not established here. Other writers of the stored target include `0x30620` and `0x30E90`, so a stored target change alone does not prove command 9 ran.
- The installed `0x3E200` loop ends at six entries (`0x3E61E`) and reads storage roles 180 through 185 from table RVA `0x2CF0D8`. The Extender labels these `HarassmentCombat0..5`; role 186 is `SiegeCover0`, not an extra raid group. The storage role resolves the current tribe ID and global ID for each player, so tribe ID alone is not a stable raid-group identity. Roles 1 and 2 also enter an alternate branch at `0x3E50B`: it tries `0x2D370`, then falls back to `0x2C620`. The ordinary building-attack branch for the other roles calls `0x2C620` at `0x3E46B`. The mod's replacement logic must therefore react to the observed command-9 event, not infer one from a role or stored-target change.
- In that regular role-1/2 branch, `0x2DC30` and the player's update counter gate action. `0x2D370` scans the victim's building-candidate list from a rotating start, accepting only the first eight types in table RVA `0x2C7E00`: quarry, iron mine, pitch digger, wheat/hops/apple/cattle farm, woodcutter's hut. If it returns no building, `0x2C620` supplies a candidate from the ordinary priority selector. Code at `0x3E55F..0x3E5DD` converts the chosen building to a tile, tests path-component connectivity via `0x3E650`/`0xE2610`, and issues a tribe move order through `0x11DD10` if connected. Otherwise it calls `0x3E9A0`, which may issue a move order to stored player fallback coordinates. This branch does not call the target-based command-9 building attack and does not test melee attack positions. The separate state-2 branch at `0x3E309..0x3E35D` precedes the role split and can affect any of the six roles; depending on its predicate it tries `0x2D370` or `0x2C8B0` before the same movement path. `0x2C8B0` uses the fixed `0x2C7E00` table across the candidate list. These are code-path findings, not observed orders for roles 1/2 in `Log_197.log`.
- The command-9 unit pass in `0x11E960` uses the type dispatch table at RVA `0x121FB0` with indices at `0x121FD0`. Melee-type cases (including ordinary European/Arab/Bedouin melee units, tunneler and Lord) increase the count used before the `0xDA020` approach search at `0x11FF9A`. Archer, crossbowman, Arab bow, slinger and Bedouin ambusher use a separate case that does not increase that count. Catapult, trebuchet, mangonel, ballista and Arab ballista use another case that can still receive command 9 without increasing the melee count; battering ram has a separate case. A missing melee pair is therefore insufficient to reject a target for a group containing building-capable siege units. Other special unit cases require individual validation before inclusion in the fix.

Runtime observation from `test_Raid_Retarget_Delay.sav`: player 2 harassment group 0 destroyed apple farm building `155/6649` at tick 704. Its stored target became granary `119/6450` by pre-tick 830; it retained that live target through tick 4209 without logged damage to it. That earlier diagnostic lacked group-command and unit-path events, so it alone could not establish why the attack stalled.

The later diagnostic session confirmed command 9 for granary `119/6450` after pre-tick 828. Through tick 2773 there was no damage to it and no per-unit destination adjacent to its footprint. The granary's `4x4` footprint begins at `407/515`; its `20` valid bounding-ring tiles include only three walkable, connected diagonal corners. The user also issued a manual building-attack order against that granary and observed no movement. A previous diagnostic field labelled `nativeCommandTarget=0/0` used the wrong pointer-relative offsets and is not evidence of a failed native command.

In the 2026-09-30 session saved as `Log_195.log`, the raid group's granary command at tick 821 produced 50 approach-only records, all with building-attack tile zero; the manual granary command also produced no paired records. Commands to apple farms produced paired first records and the group destroyed those farms. The first fix prototype queued 12 retries but made zero direct alternative attempts because it read the candidate count at the unadjusted API-pointer offset. Its apparent success came from clearing the stored target and letting Vanilla select a farm about 50 ticks later; this does not validate the direct retry path.

In `Log_197.log`, the corrected candidate pointer validates the direct retry path. Session 1 rejects granary `119/6450` at tick 836; the next update reads 50 candidates with table RVA `0x2C7F80`. Attempts on armoury `122/6479`, church `220/64373`, tradepost `116/6420`, brewers' workshop `223/64648`, and three inns return `NoAttackPoint`; wood barracks `176/62732` returns `AttackPoint` at tick 838 and takes damage from player 2 by tick 1192. Session 2 similarly reaches stone barracks `128/6515` with `AttackPoint` at tick 2110 and logged player-2 damage at tick 2651. These results show both successful direct fallback and non-farm targets in the active Vanilla priority order.

Later in session 1, Vanilla's selected quarry `193/9136` and fallback quarry `195/9698` have no usable melee attack point; apple farm `204/19080` returns `AttackPoint` at tick 1387 and takes player-2 damage at tick 1623. After that farm is destroyed, the same quarry attempts fail again, and apple farm `203/17536` returns `AttackPoint` at tick 1737 and takes player-2 damage later in the session. The logged footprint origins are `449/510` and `346/525`, about 104 map tiles apart in a straight line. At the second choice the group's logged units were still around `445-455/505-513`, confirming a long new trip rather than local clustering.

User observation from a separate Vanilla run with the walls around their own buildings removed: the knights still crossed large distances between targets, although they sometimes destroyed two or three nearby farms in succession. No matching raid diagnostic log is available for that run. The short local sequences are therefore not evidence of proximity scoring; candidate-list order (which `0x29190` appends to and `0x2C620` uses for ties) is a possible but unverified explanation for that particular run. The user also observed a wall around an enclosed inn being attacked in a modded run. `Log_197.log` records no `AttackWallTileId` group command for the observed raid group and does record `Unknown37` commands during movement; the log does not establish which native path caused the wall attack.

The compact 2026-10-01 session at 14:19:08-14:21:27 in `LogOutput.log` records player 6 role 0, tribe `4390/1375870`, deleting apple farm `924/1374290` at tick 21604. Granary `800/1373345` returns a fresh empty list and `NoAttackPoint` at tick 21643. At tick 21644 the replacement command for armoury `808/1373353` is issued and stored, but its result is `U`/uncertain and the retry ends. That armoury remains the stored target without logged damage through session end at tick 26914. The compact retry format then omitted the specific uncertainty reason, so this observation cannot distinguish unchanged scratch from a validation failure. The user's observation of knights returning to their position after fighting nearby units is compatible with this sequence but is not an independently identified unit trace.

The corrected diagnostic session started on 2026-10-01 at 16:03:08.466 on Back to Back.map (not the original save). Its log snapshot is retained at `.inspect/RaidRetargetEvaluation/LogSnapshot_2026-10-01_1603-session.log`. By tick 44000 it records 14 retries: eight selected replacements, five uncertain replacement attacks, and one candidate-list ownership mismatch. All five uncertain replacement attacks have matched pre/post events, an available context, return 1, and an identical empty prefix before and after (`unchangedPossiblyStale`, `notEvaluatedWithoutFreshness`, terminator/count 0). They involve armouries `67/1371696`, `246/1371886`, and `11/1371637`; the log cannot yet distinguish an executed empty search from a bypassed search. documentedContracts.statement: - `0x2C620` scans up to 100 16-bit building IDs in the victim player's resource record at offsets `0x3560..0x3627`; the 32-bit count is at `0x3628`. It compares each building type with the 47 entries in the priority table selected by global `0x856A6D2 & 7`. An equal-ranked later list entry replaces the earlier selection. `0x3E200` writes the selected building ID/global ID and a 100-tick raid pause after issuing command 9, so a post-command correction of its stored target must run after that outer call has returned.

Vanilla also has a distance-scoring selector at `0x2C710`, called by `0x30E90`, but the observed group-0 branch in `0x3E200` does not call it. This establishes behavior for this native path, not a claim about every game AI target selector.
