# Rally-point terrain slowdown audit (2026-10-08) [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Installed managed SHA256: BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Canonical Extender source: commit 5049b5d051d0face848cc2eb098db1fedf5451a7,
tree cc31dd3beea7c50a1bd1b6825b5ae3624f0dee31.

## Vanilla data flow

The full feature chain was audited: recruitment (0x1819D0/0x190CA0), type
initialization (0x19A240), transformation (0x195D10), rally orders
(0xBED20/0xBFD40), path start (0x196280), all 26 dispatched handlers,
the unit-update dispatcher (0x182B00, length 0x23B1), movement (0x1855A0),
arrival (0x188340), and the complete terrain calculation (0x19B260).

AI state 105 handlers copy base movement delay to effective delay before
the dispatcher uses it. Terrain calculated after a step is consequently
discarded on the next update. This affects types 5, 22..30, 37, 70..76,
and 78..85, without an owner restriction. Handler reset RVAs, in that order:
12E5E8, 13FB77, 141FEF, 143951, 1454B7, 146EFB, 148588, 14956A,
14A635, 14B454, 151310, 16807C, 169F80, 16B48F, 16CF4E, 16E6E9,
16F731, 1707E4, 17337A, 17430D, 175400, 176B5B, 178956, 17A7B1,
17B9C3, 17D59C.

At 0x18410C the dispatcher calls [r14+rax*8+0x321CB0] (8 bytes).
At 0x184114 it loads EDX from the current unit ID at RVA 0x9302C4
(6 bytes). Continuation 0x18411A is MOVSXD RAX,EDX. RCX is the
one-based unit ID multiplied by 0x490; RBX is the unit-manager base.
The manager-relative unit origin is RBX+RCX. GameUnit starts 0x65C
bytes later. Raw xrefs and the entire dispatcher have no external
entry into the displaced span's interior; the preceding branch skips
to its continuation. The installed RedBird X64InlineHook decoder
displaces exactly 14 bytes here (minimum 14, rounded by instruction).

The common cadence load at 0x184203 reads the effective delay at
manager-relative +0x9A2, base delay is +0x9A4, running bonus +0x916,
and movement ticks +0x9A8. Alive state +0x6E4 must be 2; the low WORD
at death marker +0x8F8 must be zero. Type +0x6E6, global ID +0x6F0,
and AI state +0x918 establish the capture/restore identity.

Terrain calculation remains Vanilla: elevation comparison against
unit height at +0x712, swamp/moat flags 0x20000000/0x40000000
(delays 3/4/6), ford flag 0x00200000 (delay 2), and later state
adjustments. The old mod hook at 0x19B506 copied the base delay before
terrain checks and erased the already calculated elevation adjustment.
The terrain setting bypasses only that additional reset.

## Hook and lifecycle contract [mod integration]

BugfixesAndQoL captures the effective delay before the original handler,
then restores it at the shared cadence hook before Vanilla loads it.
Capture restores flags, RAX, RCX, RDX and the complete stack before
executing the indirect call once. Other registers and SIMD are untouched.
Restore uses only registers overwritten by the displaced cadence loads;
the common wrapper saves flags. Both before and after must be alive,
non-dying, state 105, with matching type and global ID.

Native snapshots use 16 bytes per one-based unit slot: global ID (0),
type (4), delay (6), enable epoch (8), valid marker (12). Capture first
invalidates the slot. Restore consumes it once, including rejected
snapshots. Atomic enable transitions increment the epoch; bit zero
is the enable flag. A setting roundtrip invalidates old snapshots.
No recruitment events, unit-list scans or managed callbacks per tick
are needed. Save-loaded units enter the same native capture path.

The optional capture transaction validates the pattern, complete span,
continuation and dispatcher incoming branches before commit, and checks
the actual DisplacedByteCount after commit before publication. Failure
rolls back only this unpublished candidate and leaves the terrain flag
off. Shared hooks, allocations and integration publisher are rooted for
process lifetime; setting changes only publish data flags. No published
hook is undone. Fixed layout is admitted only for the validated hash.

Canonical local Fixes 1.25.1 and the installed Script Extender have no
competing hook at this capture span. Existing shared movement ownership
is retained. Native execution tests assemble/decode and execute the
production generators, covering both independent settings, 26 types,
owners, original call/registers/flags, death, identity/state changes,
epoch rejection and single consumption. These are isolated execution
tests; real in-game terrain routes and save loading still require playtest.

## Startup interaction: immutable static analysis (2026-10-08) [mod integration]

The 18:36 start log confirms the process-owned rally capture was installed at
RVA 0x18410C before the cadence resolver ran. Reading the original dispatch
operand from live memory after that installation produced an out-of-module
handler table and disabled the shared commands, Shift queue and formation.
Static cadence analysis must read the dispatch displacement, handler pointers,
handler instructions, compressed state mapping and case jump tables from the
existing CrusaderLibraryLoadContext.Memory load-time snapshot. Keep the context
rooted; validate all reads against its span and calculate decoder virtual
addresses from its real ModuleHandle. Do not decode published live hooks or
dispose the extender-owned region. No new native hook boundaries are needed.

Cadence qualification is optional. Its failure must reject weighted route
publication without disabling the shared command/selector runtime. Executable
production-resolver tests independently mutate live dispatch, handler pointer,
handler code, state map and jump table, including the combined mutation, and
verify identical snapshot-derived profiles plus rejection of invalid addresses.
Fixes' speed-reduction patches remove stores; snapshot analysis retains the
original possibilities conservatively, in addition to the captured current
speed bonus. No Fixes or Script Extender sources are changed.

title: Recruit Transformation and Rally Tracking [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]
document:
# Recruit Transformation and Rally Tracking [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

## Provenance

- Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
- The generic function names remain `candidate`; the field and control-flow claims below are confirmed for this binary by static data-flow analysis and the BugfixesAndQoL runtime trace from 2026-09-17.

## Recruitment entry points

- Mercenary recruitment at RVA `0x1819D0` and European recruitment at RVA `0x190CA0` select an existing type-1 unit slot. They store the requested type at manager-relative unit offset `+0x922`, set AI state `0x6D` at `+0x918`, and return the unchanged one-based unit ID.
- The slot's owner and GlobalId remain its identity throughout the recruitment transformation. `0x117000` performs the associated tribe/notification work; it does not allocate or return a successor slot.

## Transformation completion

- Type-1 dispatch handler RVA `0x12A8F0` advances the `0x6D` transition for 33 updates. On completion it sets the same slot's AliveState at `+0x6E4` from `2` to the transient value `4`, retains the requested type at `+0x922`, and leaves the slot type at `1` for the remainder of that update pass.
- Unit update orchestrator RVA `0x182B00` processes AliveState `4` through RVA `0x195D10`. That function restores AliveState `2`, restores the queued AI state, and calls RVA `0x19A240` with the value from `+0x922`.
- RVA `0x19A240` initializes the requested target type in the same unit slot by writing `+0x6E6` and the target type's dependent fields. There is no successor-ID handoff.

## Consumer contract [mod integration]

- Per-unit consumers that formerly had an outer `AliveState == 2` gate must skip all feature logic while the slot is in State `4` without invalidating identity or feature-owned tracking. Unit deletion remains a separate event/state transition.
- BugfixesAndQoL rally tracking is therefore keyed by the unchanged one-based unit ID plus GlobalId and owner. Its native cadence fastpath must replay Vanilla for every non-alive state and resume validation when the same slot returns to AliveState `2`.
- Observed trace: all affected recruits reached the cadence hook 33 times as type `1`, AI state `109 -> 0`, TransformType unchanged, and AliveState `2 -> 4`. Clearing tracking at that point prevented the final target type from receiving its rally animation and speed bonus.

# Savegame metadata and missing original maps [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Confirmed 2026-10-16 against native SHA-256 FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2 and managed SHA-256 BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.

The confirmed native DLL_LoadSaveGame entry is RVA 0x853F0. It loads the simulation state independently of the later managed restart metadata. EditorDirector.loadSaveGame clears restart state, invokes that native loader, and then reads the save header with loadRestartInfo=true.

MapFileManager.GetFileInfoFromFileName routes restart versions 50..99 to HUD_IngameMenu.RestartSkirmishMapInfo.decode. That decoder retains the AIVs, AICs, lord names, images and setup only if the original map header is available (except customTrailMission callers). The final availability block discards the entire successfully decoded object on two null-return paths. Custom trails first try their Maker map; absent trail dictionaries can additionally raise KeyNotFoundException. These are managed contracts, not native offsets.

The original map source is a byte: 0 user, 1 built-in, 2 Workshop. GetHeaderFromFileNameForSkirmishRestart searches only that source catalog by case-insensitive filename. A map copy in another catalog does not satisfy the lookup. The separate parsing-exception return must remain a rejection.

With no restart object, MainViewModel.getAIFace falls back to GameSprites[738] for custom slots; OnScreenText.getComputerName returns an empty name. The user confirmed that installing only the original Workshop map Tactical Boardgame (2 Player) repairs both displays for test_dusty in Vanilla. The save embeds both Mansur and The Leopard with intact 144x144 PNGs.

Removing only the final rejection is insufficient: encode dereferences selectedHeader three times (workshopMap, builtinMap, fileName). Correct portable metadata must retain that original identity separately, while leaving selectedHeader null. RestartSkirmishGame ultimately loads selectedMPHeader.filePath and requires the original map; its menu and action must reject missing-map restarts. FRONT_Multiplayer.doOpen clears selectedMPHeader before listing installed maps.

Testmods/SavegameMissingMapFixTest implements this as managed IL transforms with no native hook. Desktop tests execute clones of the actual game decoder/encoder, isolate catalog and Unity image creation, adapt one Unity Mono String.Split overload in a cloned setup parser, and verify byte-identical save roundtrips, disabled behavior, installed/local/Workshop/built-in/trail cases, corruption rejection and restart guarding. In-game acceptance of the new mod remains pending; the user confirmation above concerns Vanilla's original map dependency.

## Trail Maker consumer audit (2026-10-21) [mod integration]

The same native and managed hashes were checked again. The integrated BugfixesAndQoL
recovery can expose a non-null restart object with a null selectedHeader to Trail Maker.
FRONT_ManageTrail.DoImport's confirmation copies missions, rescans the Maker catalog,
then calls Init. Init clears its exists array, projects all 50 button markers and calls
SelectMission while doing so. SelectMission dereferences the restart's selectedHeader
display_filename without a null check (managed IL 0x01CB..0x01DB). The tested session's
Unity Player log records 14 null-reference exceptions there, including the import
confirmation -> Init chain; BepInEx's log does not contain those exceptions. An early
selection therefore interrupts the remaining markers, leaving stale occupied icons.

The Maker Load command reads with folderType 3 and may reject missing-map metadata
before FRONT_Multiplayer.Open is reached. Portable editing must decode with the existing
folderType 4 Custom Trail contract and supply a real extracted map, not the serialization
header. GetFileInfoFromFileName selects map versus campaign parsing from the first
argument's .map extension, including for temporary validation files. populateMapList
selects a supplied header only by reference identity among GetMultiplayerMaps results;
an extracted map outside that catalog needs a context-local row containing that same
header. No native address is involved in these selection and presentation contracts.

Regression evidence: BugfixesAndQoL/tests/SavegameMissingMap executes transformed
copies of the installed Init/SelectMission with catalog/Noesis boundaries isolated:
selected slots 1/5, 5 -> 2 -> 5, empty/reopened lists, installed/missing source maps,
inactive fix and changed-IL rejection. These tests do not prove actual Noesis rendering
or a portable lobby/gameplay roundtrip; those remain in-game acceptance items.

title: Savegame settings load boundaries [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

# Savegame settings load boundaries [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Managed SHA-256: BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
Installed Script Extender: 2.14.1; source provenance in the current database manifest.

## Audited flow

- Multiplayer confirmation occurs inside an existing lobby. HostLoadGame publishes
  the selected save basename; FRONT_Multiplayer then calls StartSave on each peer.
- StartSave calls initMultiplayerGame and loadMultiplayerMap with the save flag set.
  DLL_PreInitMap_Multiplayer (RVA 0x86270, confirmed export) initializes the multiplayer
  family; DLL_LoadMapToPlay (0x84AC0, confirmed export) passes the save byte unchanged
  to the skirmish initializer (0x94350, internal name still candidate confidence).
- The initializer reads the file through the existing reader and its save branch
  returns 0xFFFFFFFF after restoring state, bypassing ordinary new-game construction.
  The enclosing loader fills LoadMapReturnData. A zero reader result is failure.
- Local saves, including local Coop, instead use DLL_LoadSaveGame (0x853F0,
  confirmed export), whose successful return and output errorCode are both 1.
- The host posts the random seed and completes managed postLoading. Clients complete
  immediately with an already received seed or later through packet 2. Packet 3 is
  a Vanilla loading acknowledgement, not a modsettings fingerprint. The host's
  monitor later sends packet 4 and starts simulation; the current roster can have
  no remote humans. Original player remapping remains authoritative.
- Coop frontend/provider trail IDs are 0..3; native IDs are 1..4. Frontend mission
  IDs are decremented once by CoopMissionChanged. Save retData is authoritative
  for the actual loaded mission; the selected lobby mission is not a substitute.

## Managed mismatch and ownership [mod integration]

The installed Extender OnLoadMap sets its archive IsSaveFile to false even with
MultiplayerSave set. Its LoadContext therefore cannot by itself distinguish a
multiplayer save from a map. APIShared previously rejected its settings entry at
that flag check. Confirmed managed save entries now read the existing appended
metadata independently; no extra native hook or memory patch is required.

APIShared metadata is written only by the multiplayer host. A client save can
legitimately lack that entry. Vanilla matches save names plus its play checksum/time
evidence; whole-file SHA equality between different peers is not established.

## Managed requester timing (2026-10-19 audit) [mod integration]

The installed native and managed hashes were rechecked against the identities above.
The real public `HUD_LoadSaveRequester.OpenLoadSaveRequester` selects the visible
requester instance and opens it with confirmation/cancellation callbacks. Selection
updates `selectedHeader`; double-click routes through public `ButtonClicked(1, true)`.
`ButtonClicked(1, ...)` hides all three requester surfaces **before** `RunOKAction`
invokes the confirmation callback. Reading `IsVisible` only in that callback therefore
cannot establish whether the user was offered an option. Capture visibility/choice
before the original ButtonClicked executes, retaining the file-specific decision.

Editor overwrite confirmation defers RunOKAction until its popup is confirmed;
declining the overwrite restores the requester without confirming the save.
`CloseRequester` hides the surfaces and invokes CancelAction. RunOKAction returning
only establishes that its delegate returned: asynchronous host-load admission and
mission initialization still have their existing independent completion boundaries.
No native load flag, player remapping or archive identifier changes are required
to move the requester owner. APIShared's save-contract validator checks the public
requester methods and accessed managed fields against the installed assembly.

## Validation limits

Managed follow-up, 20.10.2026: both installed hashes remain unchanged. The private,
instance `HUD_LoadSaveRequester.RunOKAction(): void` invokes `OKAction` and **then**
updates remembered map/save names and `GameData.currentFileName`, reading the
current requester selection/name again. Editor overwrite executes it later from
the popup callback. Serializing only ButtonClicked or the consumer delegate does
not enclose this delayed caller's bookkeeping. APIShared therefore also encloses
the validated private RunOKAction entry with a permanent managed hook; nested
requester opens wait until that enclosing operation and attempt cleanup return.
The contract validator checks its real visibility/signature; no publicized direct
call or additional native offset is used.

Source, installed IL and the matching native export were inspected. This establishes
the routing mismatch, not a reproduced multiplayer desynchronization. Automated
readiness, serialization, mode reconciliation and compiled admission checks are
separate from real Solo-Multiplayer, host/client and Coop game acceptance.

title: Script Extender 2.10.1 unit and projectile hook audit [Scope: External component]

# Script Extender 2.10.1 unit and projectile hook audit [Scope: External component]

Native input: installed `CrusaderDE.dll`, SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`. Extender input: tag `v2.10.1`, commit `a8ba202f6ec7966bd115b59a6088a0077ce727a0`, tree `1cc818b1b844b5e121054f2dc2edd731206b8c7b`. This record describes this exact pair only. Function names below remain candidate interpretations unless explicitly identified as exports or confirmed in another baseline record.

## Local troop selection

`DLL_TroopSelection` at RVA `0x879A0` is an exported native entry. The existing `MOVE_COMMAND_RELEASE.md` audit follows the tick path through `DLL_RunTick` at `0x86680` and the troop command branch at `0x8C5F0`; selection is consumed locally before commands are sent. The 2.10.1 managed `GamePlayerManagerAPI.GetSelectedChimps()` reads the local `EngineInterface.selectedChimps` array and sizes it with `GetSelectedChimpsCount(GetLocalPlayerId())`. The count API retains its explicit player argument, while the selected-unit array no longer accepts one. Our command/editor callers reject an active player different from the local player; unit IDs in `SelectedUnitInfo` remain game IDs and go directly to ID APIs.

## Target selection and distance

The native function beginning at RVA `0x18E9A0` (VA `0x18018E9A0`, candidate) takes a unit manager base and a unit game ID, uses a `0x490` unit stride, checks attack and target state, maps unit types to projectile range classes, and reads the range table at RVA `0x2DA8F0`. Its target branches validate candidate identity and visibility, compare squared tile distance after world coordinates are shifted by three, and either publish the chosen target/order fields or return without a target. Its existing state-specific fallback resets `+0x9F4` and may hand movement back to RVA `0x196280`. The new Extender loader at `0x18EB20` substitutes a per-type range only when its flag is active. No current Serps mod enables that range override.

The native distance predicate at RVA `0x19B630` (VA `0x18019B630`, candidate) receives manager base, attacker game ID and target game ID in that order. It reads the attacker type from `+0x6E6`, positions from `+0x70E/+0x710`, and, for the two special ranged types, can set attack state `+0x9F4` to `3` and return false when prerequisite state at `+0x9BA` is absent. Otherwise it converts world coordinates to tiles, squares both deltas and compares their sum with the squared type-specific range. The 2.10.0 hook at `0x19B786` replaced that range-table load; the 2.10.1 hotfix adds a capture at `0x19B64E`, preserving the sign-extended attacker type in the unused third Windows x64 shadow-space slot for the later hook. This avoids relying on registers whose values differ at the later site. The source diff does not prove that the external 2.10.0 crash report had this cause.

The projectile initializer at RVA `0xA1DB0` (VA `0x1800A1DB0`, candidate) reads trajectory mode and default speed/angle tables. Its branches write the default to launch speed at projectile offset `+0xAA` or angle at `+0xB0`, then continue initializing projectile state. The Extender inline hook at `0xA1E0E` preserves the original branch sequence and conditionally calculates extended-range launch speed from source unit type, source/target coordinates and elevation difference. The declared minimum hook size is `0x17`; RedBird rounds displacement to complete instructions, so that declaration is not an exact overwritten span.

## Unit updates, interactions and other hooks

The Extender walks thirteen ranged-unit update functions selected from `UnitFunctionsVTable` and hooks compares against unit field `+0x8FE`. It also adds an interaction-range loader near `0x8D769`. The vtable set is separate from the seven wildlife update function entries optionally hooked by the local Fixes clone. Fixes' unit-selection speed patches address field `+0x916`. `ImprovedHunters` has manual-attack sites at `0x18EB36` and `0x18ED96`, after the `0x18EB20` loader; `BugfixesAndQoL` has the attack-pair gate at `0x8D72B` and a peace-time site at `0x8D7C4`, separate from `0x8D769`. The release-wide source fingerprint, classifications and per-site rationale are in `Shared/ScriptExtenderUpdate/2.9.0-2.10.1.release-hooks.json`.

The installed Script Extender has the parameterless selection method and the new projectile interop field. The `GetProjectilesAsSpan()` header-inclusive slot-view bug remains in 2.10.1 source, so the marked local adapter stays. The early crash-handler false-alarm entry has no positive source or runtime fix evidence. `UpdateForScriptExtender` found 365 patterns; the new hotfix AOB matches uniquely at `0x19B64E` for this native hash. It found no changed Ghidra label, prototype, or type input, so the current hash-bound Ghidra exports were retained. Their `0x19B630` record still has candidate confidence, and no new function label was promoted from Extender source comments. No in-game run of these range paths is claimed here.

# Script Extender 2.11.0 speech-path hook [Scope: External component]

Scope: `CrusaderDE.dll` SHA-256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`; Script Extender commit `48fd239dc56300d9e3acacaa26a8cd87de0c6464`, tree `d9a8f9637987151c243818ddda747e91ea3d4a69`.

`BulkAIDetours.cs:92` adds a module-bound `AddInline` AOB. The current DLL has exactly one match at RVA `0xFEF21`, inside the native message function beginning at RVA `0xFEE50`. The historical DLL also has one match, at RVA `0xFE041`; that address is historical evidence only. The source extractor records the new pattern as `resolutionKind=unknown`, so it does not generate a Ghidra label. Its module and current match are independently confirmed by the pattern scan.

The current overwritten block is three complete five-byte instructions: `lea rcx,[rsp+...]`, `call c_game_cruntime_sprintf`, `lea rdx,[rsp+...]`. The continuation is RVA `0xFEF30`. The installed RedBird.X64 1.5.0 copied-byte probe reports `DisplacedByteCount=15`, retains the relocated call target, assembles the replacement with a common 256-byte allocation in `RCX` and `RDX`, and decodes the resulting stub. No direct incoming edge targets the displaced interval. Local release hooks and the canonical Fixes clone do not patch this span.

The relocation does not protect the earlier native copy at RVA `0xFEEA0` into the immediate message record at `manager+0x70`. `MessageManager.h` places `ImmediatePlayerId` at `+0xD4`; the caller at RVA `0x103290` writes that ID before calling the copy, and RVA `0xFEE50` reads it after the copy. In the 2026-09-27 12:05:39 local BepInEx session, `c_game_ai_enqueue_message_hook_impl` logged a 134-byte ASCII `NotSendingGoods` audio reference. The user reports successful playback. An immediate copy of its 135 bytes including NUL reaches `manager+0xF6`, 35 bytes beyond the 100-byte audio interval; its bytes 100–103 are `NG_G`, or `0x475F474E` as the overwritten little-endian player ID. When the manager is busy, RVA `0x103290` instead copies into contiguous `QueueAudioPaths[slot][100]` without a bound, crossing into the next slot for this length. The log does not reveal which branch handled the test message or the post-copy field contents. These writes remain inside the larger manager allocation for early slots, so a sound can play without a crash while adjacent state is changed. This is a preexisting long-path defect, not a proven 2.11.0 regression. The sound-manager copy at RVA `0xEF20` and the new 256-byte allocation also need upstream length review.

Evidence: `sources/patterns.jsonl`, `sources/pattern-matches.jsonl`, the hash-bound copied-byte probe in `Shared/ScriptExtenderUpdate/2.10.4-2.11.0.HookProbe`, and `Shared/ScriptExtenderUpdate/2.10.4-2.11.0.release-hooks.json`.

# Script Extender 2.14.1 engage-range audit [Scope: External component]

Review date: 2026-10-08. Previous baseline commit: 5049b5d051d0face848cc2eb098db1fedf5451a7 (2.14.0). Reviewed target: 5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3, tree c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295 (v2.14.1). Installed/local build/package SHCDESE.dll: SHA-256 E5D78FDF2EA9701336C398F7D29410F206D141FC01AA8099F30C824E6AB8A0B3, assembly 2.14.1.0. Native SHA-256 FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2; managed Assembly-CSharp SHA-256 BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789. These are provenance-bound facts, not permanent version expectations.

The complete release diff changes only BulkUnitDetours.cs and CHANGELOG.md. No public API or interop layout changes in this release. Unit-vtable role names are candidate associations; native bytes, offsets, decoded branch targets and memory relationships below were verified. Evidence is retained in ../../../../ScriptExtender2141Audit (native-audit.json, native-sites.json, emitter-provenance.json, installed-layout.json, stubs.json, stub-verification.json and their reproduction scripts).

## Complete feature path and identity contract

Dispatcher 0x182B00 selects unit updates through vtable 0x321CB0. The active unit context is a 1-based game ID; iteration begins at 1 and advances by record stride 0x490 relative to the manager sentinel. Installed GameUnitManager.GameUnitArray starts at +0x65C (sentinel origin); API views account for that sentinel, yielding 0-based first-real-unit spans. Do not pass a span index as CurrentContextUnitId or add/subtract one inside this generator. Installed public fields: GameUnit.r_AliveState +0x88 AliveState, r_UnitChimp +0x8A eChimps, r_ControllableForPlayerId +0x92 UInt16, r_GlobalId +0x94 UInt32, r_IsKilledByProjectile +0x29C UInt16, r_WorldDistanceToNearestEnemy +0x2A2 UInt16. Reflection verification is retained in installed-layout.json.

Distance producer 0x18C040 handles wild/owner-zero selection with Chebyshev distance, initializes the distance to 10000 and validates global identity. Producer 0x18C160 traverses enemy candidates, calculates the integer approximation max + (((min * 2) / 5) * min) / max, clamps to 32000 and performs attack/path side effects. Refresh 0x19A1F0 is also included in the producer audit. The native WORD manager+0x8FE is GameUnit+0x2A2 after the sentinel/stride mapping. Native comparisons use signed 16-bit arithmetic despite the public UInt16 storage view. Keep arithmetic signedness and native identity separate from managed field naming.

Downstream 0x18E9A0 retains native identity, visibility, unit type, attack and height checks, followed by native unit-state transitions. ## Generator, registers, flags and publication

The audit extracts the exact upstream emitter lambda, records its SHA-256 and substitutes only two global-address constants for isolated scratch storage. It uses installed Iced and RedBird 1.5 to generate an unpublished X64InlineHook on a copied native byte buffer. Hook Enable is never called. DisplacedByteCount and ReturnAddress must match the native audit, reassembly must match the actual allocated stub, every executable byte must decode, and the trailing indirect-jump pointer must equal target + actual displacement. The last eight pointer bytes are data, not executable instructions. Native full-span bytes are preserved in native-sites.json.

The original compare runs first. A spare GPR excludes the compare operand, memory base and index. Its old value is pushed; the original operand is captured before r13/r14/r15 are repurposed. The scratch registers and flags are saved. CurrentContextUnitId is loaded through r13d before computing the unit record/type; native flag lookup preserves its own temporary. Default-cache initialization records the original operand, including when it occupied r13w/r14w/r15w. Cached defaults are not overwritten.

Vanilla branch restores saved flags and every scratch register. Override branch sign-extends the chosen Int16 threshold into the spare register, drops the saved flag slot with LEA, restores r15/r14/r13 before the replacement compare, compares against the spare WORD, then pops the spare register without changing flags. Thus the following original conditional branch consumes flags from the intended comparison. Stack restoration is identical on both paths. No ContextAssemblyGenerator callback wrapper is used here; its SUB/ADD flag caveat remains applicable to other context hooks. This emitter contains no SIMD operations or managed callback; GPR checks do not assert unrelated wrapper SIMD behavior.

The bounded actual-byte interpreter exercises 35,280 cases: all 35 sites, signed distance/override boundaries, three original thresholds, active/inactive overrides, cold/warm default caches and two incoming flag states. It verifies all sixteen GPRs, balanced stack, six arithmetic compare flags, original-value caching and allowed memory writes at the first restored native conditional branch. It fails closed on unsupported instructions. Full stub decode and continuation-pointer checks supplement this bounded prefix execution. This is an offline machine-contract test, not gameplay execution. Hooks are process-lifetime owned by the Extender; no release mod changes or new hook publication occur in this update.

## Consumers and compatibility

Release native ownership is recorded in Shared/ScriptExtenderUpdate/2.14.0-2.14.1.release-hooks.json (dynamically fingerprinted inventory). No release mod uses engage-range overrides or owns these overwritten spans. Across release sources, relevant test sources and Fixes, partial AOB fragments near two heavy-camel sites belong to ImprovedHunters queries; their complete concatenated signatures resolve inside hunter 0x12FC70..0x131422 and establish no overlap.

Clean canonical Fixes v1.26.3 commit cbabdecac15a6e81cb45404f1a3501a4856dae39, tree 185f84b1fa6fc2faad793f2980a18d38599290e0 is reviewed separately in FIXES_COMPATIBILITY.md. Its ladder hooks 0x111C00 and 0x6A5D0 do not overlap engage sites. EnemyBridgePathTest has an existing competing 0x111C00 owner and remains excluded; this update makes no compatibility claim for that test.

Existing capture-event and PCL route integrations are retained. The additive 2.13/2.14 APIs provide no demonstrated benefit requiring a migration here. AffectedMods and BuildMods are empty; all mod versions, minimum versions, metadata and changelogs remain unchanged.

## Acceptance limits

Gameplay acceptance remains with the user: start beyond startup cleanup, ranged target search, attack and retreat. Review only the new BepInEx start section and newly timestamped crash artifacts afterward. The known early crash-handler null-read/minidump false-alarm note remains: no source change in this release establishes its correction, and no controlled startup evidence has yet been supplied. Offline checks do not substitute for that acceptance.

# Long simulation ticks from AI group movement (FBCB9319) [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native DLL SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`. The addresses below are RVAs for this binary only.

Evidence: PerfProbe DEVDIAG stack sampler (`Testmods/PerfProbe/src/PerfProbeSimSampler.DevDiag.cs`). It suspends the simulation thread about once per millisecond during an `EngineInterface.run` that has run for 80 ms or longer, then unwinds the thread with the x64 unwind tables. Frames are reduced to `RUNTIME_FUNCTION.BeginAddress`, so a value can be the start of a chained fragment rather than a whole function. Observed runs on 2026-10-20 with `test_dustyFPS2.sav` (runs R2 06:33:07 and F1 06:50:27): 390 and 388 samples in single ticks of 483 and 480 ms. No hook was involved.

- 373 of 390 samples share the outer chain `0x86680` (`DLL_RunTick`) > `0xCE099` > `0x5743D` > `0x2AE40` > `0x3C36B` > `0x3D70B` > `0x11B520` > `0x196280` > `0xF4930`.
  - `0x2AE40` is the per-AI-player scheduler (see `RAID_RETARGET.md`, `FIXES_WHEAT_STARTUP.md`).
  - `0x11B520` is the tribe coordinate movement order (see `ASSASSIN_DIRECT_GATEHOUSE_CLIMB.md`).
  - `0x196280` → `0xF4930` builds the per-unit route; `0xF4930` uses search budgets up to 400000.
- Leaf distribution: `0xD86F0` (47 %), `0xDB650`, `0xDA5EF`, `0xE4A1A`, `0xD9C40`, `0xDAA50`. These are pathfinding internals called from `0xF4930`; `0xD90D0` is the confirmed `c_game_update_pathfinding_for_tile_and_neighbors3x3`.
- The cost of such a tick is therefore one AI group order: one route search per unit, each potentially up to the search budget. The renderer frame loop is not involved: it accounts for 3 of 390 samples (`0x86680` > `0x41D60`). Rendering continues during such a tick (`framesDuring` 86–91). The main thread only blocks if it waits for `EngineInterface.threadLock`.
- Timing is driven by AI scheduling, not by zoom or load. Earlier runs on another save showed these ticks every ~25 s. In the automated runs it occurred once, about 4 s after unpausing.
- Uncertain: the exact AI military routine around `0x3C36B`/`0x3D70B` (sampled addresses are fragment starts), the number of units per order, and whether individual searches exhaust their budget.

## Managed measurement boundary clarified, 2026-10-22

Installed `Assembly-CSharp.dll` SHA-256
`BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789` was inspected
using its actual method IL. `EngineInterface.run(bool)` calls
`MemoryBuffers.getFreeBuffer(true)` before entering `threadLock`; a missing buffer
returns zero without calling `DLL_RunTick`. Thus completed managed run calls are
not a native-call count or proof of advanced simulation ticks. The bool argument
must be retained as context rather than interpreted as evidence of advancement.

The single Monitor scope contains `preDLLCallActions`, native argument preparation,
`DLL_RunTick`, deserialization, `CopyPlayStateStruct`, and `returnBuffer`, then releases
the monitor in a finally block. `GetMeritData` and `SetAchData` use the same static
lock. Managed Monitor waiting, pre-native work, the inclusive native call (including
SE/mod callbacks), and post-native publication must be measured separately. This
clarifies managed observation boundaries; it does not add a native address or
attribute every future native-time spike to the AI movement path observed above.

# Situational unit audio: Arabian idle sword draw [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Audit date: 2026-10-11. Native SHA256 `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`; installed DLL matches CURRENT.json. Managed Assembly-CSharp SHA256 `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`. Script Extender local v2.14.1, commit `5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3`, tree `c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295`. Installed NativeX64 SHA256 `0843DD4C381A3E77DD6D8B51D5CCF95465B3FB49BFDF2980F39A212D774AADB0`.

## Complete feature path

Native dispatcher 0x182B00 uses the 1-based current unit Game-ID global at 0x9302C4. Actual type table at 0x321CB0, entry75 at 0x321F08, points to 0x16F590 (Arabian swordsman); European swordsman is type27. The full Arabian handler and its state jump table were inspected. State0 enters rest state1 when unassigned; ordered/other branches enter state3 or 0x69. State1 advances the rest animation, eventually resetting state0 and the action timer; occupancy relocation can lead to state101. Combat/build states106/107 and other sounds are separate paths.

Native unit record = manager(0x67E8400)+0x65C+gameId*0x490. Public GameUnit span begins at slot1, manager+0xAEC. Struct-relative type is +0x8A, AIState +0x2BC, animation timer +0x2AC, animation-advance flag +0x4C, tile sound coordinates +0xC0/+0xC2. Public TryGetUnitById accepts the unchanged Game-ID and indexes gameId-1. These offsets are crosschecked with the installed public struct and native manager/header formula, not inferred from a displacement alone.

State1 targets 0x16FFE9. Animation table depends on gameId&3: 0x330580, 0x3305E0, 0x330640 or 0x3306D0. Sound180/0xB4 (`FX_SHEATH_OUT`) requires animation advancement, gameId&3>2, timer11, and the existing RNG outcome. Actual CALL 0x1700CD -> 0x2960, next0x1700D2. The timer80 branch contains sound179 (`FX_SHEATH_IN`) at 0x17012F; current tables end earlier, so reachability of that later branch is not established. Other handler sounds164/163,65,145 at 0x16FB19,0x16FEA1,0x16FEE0 remain separate. Capturing the entire type75 handler scope plus state1/sound180/flag0 selects the audited draw call without extra RNG calls or simulation writes.

Wrapper0x2960 calls 0x1A41E0 with manager0xA98820 and spatial flag0; wrapper0x2990 passes flag1. Wrapper0x2940 calls explicit emitter0x1A4190 with volume100. Both creators write record kind16, sound[3], volume[11], pan[12], increment count exactly once; spatial emitter also writes x[1],y[2],flag[13],volume=-1,pan=-1. Manager prefix is buffer pointer at0, count int at8. Record size is42 bytes/21 signed shorts. Both writers overwrite volume, so reused records do not retain a prior marker.

DLL_RunTick export0x86680 binds the caller buffer via0x1A45D0, copies pending records through0x1A3EE0 (count*42), executes simulation, returns count and resets output pointer/count through0x19CE70 to its internal buffer at manager+0x10C9E8C. Managed Director.simThread calls the native tick on pinned buffers; six MemoryBuffers.MemBuffer instances hold short[14,700,000]. Director.Update consumes up to three queued buffers via GameMap.processTestMap and returns them to the pool. Simulation thread-local context cannot be consulted later on the Unity playback thread.

GameMap.processTestMap case16 reads volume[11],pan[12],flag[13]. Only BOTH volume>=0 AND pan>=0 select explicit volume/100 and (pan-64)/64. Otherwise Vanilla retains tile lookup, viewport culling, screen-derived pan, and spatial volume attenuation (flag0) before calling SFXManager.playSound. Therefore replacing only spatial volume -1 with -32768 preserves the branch and travels with the record through pending copies and all six buffers.

Actual public SFXManager.playSound signature is `(int soundID, float volumeOfset, float pan, bool unstoppable)`; the last optional argument is still present in IL even though the decompiler omits it at these calls. Preserve it. Both call sites in processTestMap carry the computed volume/pan. Downstream selection/throttling, clip base volume, 20-channel policy, and MyAudioManager.playSFX global SFX/master multiplication are unchanged. Multiplying only the marked per-play volume by0.25 avoids changing global sound-ID properties or clip assets.

## Hook and compatibility contract [mod integration]

Installed NativeX64 Absolute detour needs14 bytes rounded to complete instructions. Handler entry span15 bytes (5+5+5), continuation0x16F59F push rdi; emitter entry span14 (4+3+4+3), continuation0x1A41EE coordinate write. Displaced blocks have no branches or RIP-relative operands. Full-function direct calls/jumps and semantic xrefs contain no incoming interior edges. The actual production backend is tested on complete private function copies before/after publication, including scheme, displacement, target, zero PointerSlot, hook/trampoline addresses, Absolute FF25 pointer patch and NOP padding.

Script Extender audio asset substitution is downstream in MyAudioManager.playSFX and preserves the input volume. No existing contextual unit-sound event was found. APIShared public catalog/integration/architecture contain no owner of these two native entries or the selected managed method. Canonical local Fixes1.25.1 has notification suppression and a different GameMap.getPivotOffset hook, not these targets. Never add a competing MyAudioManager function detour for this feature.

The testmod is statically rooted; native callbacks and the permanent GameMap IL hook survive startup destruction of BaseUnityPlugin. No plugin Update/coroutine or teardown is used. Disabling only changes atomically published logical state. Published hooks are retained until process exit, including failed partial installation. Unknown identities/layout/IL fail closed. Runtime native context and first reduced playback have separate bounded timestamped markers.

## Evidence and limits

Reusable implementation/update contract: Testmods/ArabianIdleSoundTest/UpdateToNewDLL.md. Read-only span/dispatch/call regression: tests/native_audit.py. Isolated executable tests compile the actual runtime sources against installed assemblies and test eligibility, negative spatial marker, unmodified neighboring records, copy/pool transport, reuse, disable/fail-open, real public signatures/offsets, actual IL transformation and NativeX64 private copies.

These static/isolated tests establish the transformation and binary contracts. Audible reduction, actual Unity Mono hook execution after startup cleanup, mission/load transitions and large-army listening remain unconfirmed until an in-game test. No runtime sound-ID match by itself establishes idle context.

## 2026-10-11 startup failure and repair [mod integration]

The user's first listening test left the sound unchanged. The local BepInEx startup at 14:55:06.456 records `ArgumentException: Invalid path` in SoundRuntime.Install line37. Enabled=true was present, but initialization failed before native or managed hook publication. The later "waiting" log was emitted after a synchronously replayed LibraryLoaded callback, so it did not establish an active runtime.

The repair resolves all three binary files from BepInEx.Paths.GameRootPath and retains every audited SHA256 guard. Assembly.Location is not a reliable install path for a byte-loaded Unity assembly. The isolated test now loads the real Assembly-CSharp.dll from bytes, confirms empty Location, validates canonical files independently, and rejects missing files, wrong hashes and a missing game root before activation.

Both immediate unit lookups now use APIShared.UnitAccess.TryGetById with consumed boolean results and the existing type/state/context conditions. Vor dem Eingriff wurden native, verwaltete und NativeX64-Dateiidentitäten erneut
gegen den vollständigen 91-Quellen-Audit geprüft: alle unverändert. Wrapper-

gegen die installierte Vorfassung abgeglichen (2020 Einträge, keine Änderung).

maßgeblich; der erneute Ingame-Vergleich dieser Fassung ist noch offen.

# Spectator building and wall placement [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native baseline SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
These findings are static; the spectator testmod still requires in-game confirmation.

- `DLL_MapAction` dispatches wall input through `0x8AAF0` to `0x94120`. Preview/line handling reaches `0x61210`; the delayed wall chore reaches `0x11B50`, `0x6F230`, `0xC8CC0`, and `0xB7D80`. The line limit uses stone at `0xCF640`. A click-time stone adjustment alone cannot make the later construction free.
- The building click path at `0x90CD0` checks `0xCC420` before enqueuing chore `0x1C`. The chore handler at `0x12090` checks `0xCC420` again before entering `0x6D580`. The latter is the normal structure placement/construction path and retains terrain and collision validation.
- RVA `0xCC420` begins with bytes `48 89 5C 24 20 44 89 44 24 18`: two complete five-byte instructions. For the installed RedBird NativeX64 1.5.0.0 backend, the Indirect detour uses a six-byte entry patch and displaces ten bytes here. No incoming edge into this ten-byte range was found in the audited call contexts. A runtime hook must still validate hash, bytes, backend schema, displaced length, patch form, and pointer slot before publishing.
- The Script Extender exposes `OnBuildStructure.IsFree` at the native construction call and `OnBuildingSpawn` for the actual building record. It exposes `OnBuildWall` and player resource subtraction events for wall accounting. The installed Fixes mod already patches a separate wall cost site at `0x6F230`; no overlap with the `0xCC420` entry hook was found.
- `DLL_MapAction` at `0x85BD0` saves native view `DAT_1888e3d70`, writes its `playerID` argument for the action, then restores the saved value. The queue producer at `0x23990` reads sender field `+0x36FA50` relative to queue base `DAT_188574320`, which aliases `DAT_1888e3d70`; delayed building and wall handlers at `0x12090` and `0x11B50` use the decoded sender `DAT_1888e3d6c`. Thus a human single-player session can submit a mapped action for an AI owner without permanently switching the human view, provided the mod passes that owner to `DLL_MapAction` through the managed wrapper.
- Unit mapper `0x93750` reads the temporary native view/player ID. Ordinary troop creation passes it to `0x118CA0`, which creates units through `0x17FEF0` and assigns them to a tribe where Vanilla normally does so. Special cases can call `0x17FEF0` directly and keep their native no-tribe behavior.

Pending runtime checks: zero-stock walls of all three mapper types, delayed order matching, unchanged stone/cost remainder, regular versus spectator well sprite variation and tile layers, and non-spectator behavior.

# Spectator report path [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native baseline: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Managed `Assembly-CSharp.dll` inspected with SHA-256 `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.

## Native data and mode flow

- `DLL_SetEditorPlayer` at RVA `0x872E0` changes the local native view index `DAT_1888e3d70` independently of spectator status.
- `DLL_RunTick` at RVA `0x86680` temporarily changes that index to zero for spectator input processing, restores it, and then calls `FUN_18019d960` at RVA `0x19D960` to fill the managed `PlayState` buffer. Thus the returned report fields follow the selected view index while the spectator input path remains separate.
- `DLL_SetAppMode` at RVA `0x87220` accepts report mode `16` and its report submodes, including menu `71`, Popularity `72`, Fear Factor `73`, Population `74`, Food `75`, Army `76`, Stores `77`, Weapons `78`, and Religion `79`. Its visible branch does not reject spectator mode.
- `FUN_18019d960` copies resources, popularity components, population, troop counts, religion values, and other report fields using the selected view index. Their managed consumers are in `FatControler`.

## Managed entry gate

- `MainViewModel.ButtonReports(object)` reads `FreezeMainControls` once. When true, it forces every request to Army (`num = 9`) and hides the Army back buttons. Its normal branch maps the book and eight menu buttons to report submodes. This is the spectator menu restriction; it is separate from native report-data selection.
- `FatControler` freezes build controls when `EditorDirector.ActivePlayerID <= 0`. That freeze must remain intact for spectators.
- `FatControler` sets the report menu's `PlayerNameText` from `ConfigSettings.Settings_UserName`, so a changed spectator view needs its own displayed name.
- `MainViewModel.PlayerNameText` only raises `NotifyPropertyChanged` when its incoming string differs from the stored value. Writing a selected lord name once per render fights the Vanilla writer and repeatedly triggers this notification; substituting a cached selected name at the setter keeps the normal equality guard effective.
- The Food report XAML includes four buttons bound to `ButtonSetEdibleCommand`. `MainViewModel.ButtonChangeEdibleState` sends `SetFoodEaten`, so the report page is not entirely read-only. The Food back button returns to report menu when `WasInGranary` is false; `ButtonReports` sets it false.
- Those four buttons use `BTN_Building`. Its `IsEnabled=false` trigger switches to `SpriteLocked`, while its style-level enabled trigger starts a fade-out storyboard; disabling them can hide the food sprites entirely. `Noesis.UIElement.IsHitTestVisible=false` blocks mouse hits without activating either disabled-state visual, while the managed command hook remains the action guard.

These contracts were checked statically against the installed files. Behavior of the added testmod's report navigation and data freshness still requires an in-game test after installation.

## Loading a spectator save

- `DLL_GameAction` RVA `0x81870` (confirmed export) handles `SpectatorMode` (`0x431`) by setting the process-local `DAT_183666080` flag to one. `FUN_18019d960` RVA `0x19D960` (candidate name, confirmed report-buffer flow) copies that flag to `PlayState.spectatorMode` at byte offset `0xB12`. The flag also controls `DLL_RunTick` RVA `0x86680` (confirmed) input suppression.
- The reset path `FUN_1800087d0` RVA `0x87D0` (candidate name) clears the flag. `DLL_LoadSaveGame` RVA `0x853F0` (confirmed) enters this reset path before creating the loaded `PlayState`; its visible save-reader path does not restore the flag. The reader at RVA `0x24B70` (candidate name) restores the native view index from save field `0x1D` but has no writer to the spectator flag. This explains a loaded spectator save reporting `spectatorMode=0` until the local action is issued again.
- In the non-editor branch, `DLL_LoadSaveGame` converts native view index zero to one. If the chosen view has no CPU registration, it writes exactly `1` into that slot's human registration. Thus a single apparent human at the restored view can be synthetic. `retData+0x3C` carries the resulting one-based view index to managed loading, which assigns `EditorDirector` a positive local ID. `EditorDirector.SetLocalPlayer(-1)` changes only that managed ID; the native view remains separate.
- Automatic recovery must require independent CPU-only roster evidence and reject genuine human members. The concrete loaded-save roster and later report values still require an in-game test.
- Managed `Platform_Multiplayer.createLoadedSkirmishMembers` creates eight placeholder `MPGameMember` objects for a local save and does not set `skirmishAI` on them. Their count and `skirmishAI` values therefore cannot prove the saved player roster. The native `PlayState` computer and human registration arrays are the usable post-load roster; a lone synthetic human is indistinguishable from a real human in a matching slot without independent save provenance and must remain unrecognized.
- The 2026-09-29 load of `test_canari_nowoodcutters.sav` had no Script Extender archive and reached the ambiguous human-or-synthetic case. That save offers no mod identity marker. The installed `ModSaveDataAPI` writes registered bytes to an on-demand archive at save time; after its second archive load pass and before `OnPostLoad`, the active archive contains the loaded entry. A future spectator save can therefore carry independent provenance without changing Vanilla's native save fields.

## Ally panel and spectator commands

The installed native hash remains `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`; the installed managed Assembly-CSharp hash is `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.

- `HUD_Main.BuildScreenAllies` opens the same `HUD_AlliesPanel` in Skirmish and Multiplayer. Its ally and enemy lists and current order display use managed `GameData.playerID`, which `SetEditorPlayer` does not update. The panel's `GetAllyList`, `GetEnemyList`, and `UpdateAllies` contain respectively three, two, and two calls to that getter in the installed Assembly.
- `HUD_AlliesPanel.ButtonClicked` sends `Ally_Orders` through `Ally_CancelOrders` (`1061..1066`) to `EngineInterface.GameAction`. `DLL_GameAction` at RVA `0x81870` (confirmed export) uses the current native view index `DAT_1888e3d70` as the ally-command sender. Order/cancel/confirm branches enqueue opcode `113`; send/request-goods branches check or use sender resources before enqueuing. The producer for orders at RVA `0xD7520` is candidate by generic function name but its argument flow and caller are statically traced.
- The opcode `113` handler at RVA `0x1A6F0` (candidate function label, confirmed static producer/handler association) decodes a 16-bit operation and four 32-bit values. Its branches at RVAs `0xD7580`, `0xD78C0`, `0xD7AD0`, `0xD7450`, `0xD7360`, and `0xD77D0` update ally orders, resources, requests and notifications. `DLL_RunTick` at RVA `0x86680` (confirmed) restores the chosen index after suppressing spectator map input, so the ally UI's direct `GameAction` path can still enqueue these commands.
- The managed ally menu has no multiplayer-specific command implementation. The native Chore scheduler at RVA `0x23990` takes different local/network timing branches, but the same ally payload handler is used. Static analysis does not establish whether a spectator-origin packet is accepted and remains synchronized on every peer; this requires a host/client runtime test.

# Offline AI test tools: native request and resource contracts [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

Native SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.
Managed SHA-256: `BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789`.
Extender 2.14.1 source commit `5908e1f12437deb7ef5f5b1dc2d64e301178fba3`,
tree `c238441ea12db35ee36c5c5668d3c8fce0897295`.

This is static feature evidence, not an in-game acceptance record. Autogenerated
function names remain candidate-level; the stated branches are supported by the
hash-matched function bodies and installed Extender source/assembly contracts.

`HUD_AlliesPanel.ButtonClicked` passes selected ally, selected goods and amount to
GameAction; UpdateGoods requires positive amounts and the sender's own inventory.
The private ally/enemy lists have six slots. A separate test view is needed to
avoid changing normal diplomacy and BugfixesAndQoL's spectator authorization.

`DLL_GameAction` (0x81870) dispatches the ally-order action to 0xD7520, which stages
Chore 113. At 0x1A6F0 the handler serializes a signed short request kind and four
signed 32-bit values. Kind zero invokes 0xD7580. That complete function is 587
bytes and takes `(attackTarget, orderedAi, requester, order)`, all player IDs
one-based. Order 10 clears the request; 11 requests protection of requester;
other attack values use attackTarget. This function does not check alliance
membership. It distinguishes AI/human slots, invokes the appropriate acceptance
check and writes request state only on acceptance for AI slots.

Defend acceptance 0x2A500 and attack acceptance 0x41500 require an initialized AI,
check help state and compare army strength to the AIC threshold. The installed
Extender owns both hooks and exposes OnPlayerAIEvaluateDefendOrder and
OnPlayerAIEvaluateAttackOrder. In these events TargetPlayerId is the ordered AI;
SourcePlayerId is requester; attack ContextPlayerId is the attack target.
Pre with SkipOriginalFunction and ReturnValue=true returns acceptance without
the original readiness check. The outer 0xD7580 then performs the normal writes
and accepted-attack preparation through 0x2A580 (which calls 0xC4080, 0x2B5F0,
0x304B0, 0x30550, then clears siege state). A context limited to one call can
therefore force acceptance without another native hook or direct order-field writes.

The request mode, attack target and requester map to Extender fields
r_AIAllyOrderMode (+0x384C), r_AIRequestedAttackTargetPlayerId (+0x3850), and
r_AIAllyOrderRequesterPlayerId (+0x38E4). Record stride is 0x583C. At 0x2F670
the target selector clears requests whose requester Lord is invalid; a valid
attack request retains the explicit target while that Lord remains valid.
0x3C2E0 handles protection through 0x3D020. Accepted request state alone does
not prove that troops can move or reach an objective.

Vanilla send-goods execution 0xD7AD0 adds physical recipient goods, removes
sender goods, updates valuation statistics and clears matching requests. Gold
is handled separately and capped by sender funds. The standard send action is
therefore unsuitable for creation from nothing. Existing Extender AddIncomingGood
adds to the delivery-reserve table (+0x46C base); AddPlayerGold changes signed
r_TotalGoodsGold (+0x50C). Both require caller-side overflow checks. Combining
stored goods and pending incoming goods before a new credit protects eventual
storage totals. Existing storage consumers 0xAED70 / 0xAF210 consume incoming
resources as capacity permits, update local/global goods and resource visuals;
editor mode excludes those simulation paths. Gold can be credited immediately.

EngineInterface's shared monitor is a private static System.Object field named
threadLock in the real assembly. An actual-assembly metadata check and a
single encapsulated reflection read are required; publicized direct access is invalid.

Executable fixture checks live under Testmods/SpectatorEditorBuildTest/tests;
the mod's UpdateToNewDLL.md records its supported origins, resolution limits,
existing placement hooks and outstanding in-game acceptance matrix.

# Surrender selection and multiplayer checksum audit [Scope: Vanilla]

Native build SHA-256: `FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`. The installed Script Extender inspected for the managed path was `2.10.1.0` (local fork commit `a8ba202f6ec7966bd115b59a6088a0077ce727a0`). Addresses below are RVAs for this build; none is used as a runtime call target by the Surrender fix.

`DLL_RunTick` (`0x86680`) reaches the simulation path `0xCDE60` and checksum scheduler `0xD1AD0`. Every 200 map ticks, the checksum builder `0x22020` computes fourteen category aggregates. Its first bucket scans unit IDs 1..9999. For each unit, `0x78E0` hashes 0x404 bytes beginning at the unit's `r_AliveState` offset 0x88, plus the separate 1000-byte packed path plan and three scalar values. The builder temporarily masks eight bytes at unit offset 0x418. The unit's `r_UnitSelected` at offset 0xAE is inside the hashed interval and is not masked. The unit record is 0x490 bytes; native manager and per-unit address arithmetic agree with the installed Script Extender layout and one-based game IDs.

`0x27960` compares the fourteen category aggregates and sends mismatch opcode 0x65 (101). On a flagged first bucket, `0x26D30` compares per-unit checksums, stores the first offending unit ID and sends detail opcode 0x38 (56). `0x27C50` can queue resync opcode 0x36 (54) when the aggregate mismatch is established. These functions have candidate symbolic names in the export; the relevant branch and data flow were checked directly in the current decompilation. The observed opcode 101 flags and opcode 56 unit IDs corroborate the assignment, but other categories and all possible resync triggers were not exhaustively attributed.

Two Surrender traces showed exactly four different bytes in the full Lord unit record at the checksum tick: offsets 0x10, 0x12, 0x13 and 0xAE. Only 0xAE lies in the hashed record interval. After player 2 surrendered, Lord unit 13/global 1356740 had `r_UnitSelected=0` on the host and `2` on the client at map tick 600; Vanilla's detail opcode identified unit 13. After player 1 surrendered, Lord unit 11/global 1356738 had `r_UnitSelected=1` on the host and `0` on the client at tick 1000; Vanilla identified unit 11. Packed path-plan and the three extra per-unit scalar inputs were not captured in those traces, so the selection field is a strong sufficient explanation, not a proof that no other checksum input differed.

Native `0x19A5D0` handles individual and all-unit deselection. In its individual branch it clears `r_UnitSelected` and decrements `GameUnitManager.r_SelectedChimpsCount[playerId]` when the unit was selected. The first count element is at manager offset 0x24 in the installed assembly (`Marshal.OffsetOf`), consistent with the native expression `manager[(playerId + 9)]`; the Extender source comment saying 0x28 is one word late. The final unit deletion `0x1869C0` calls this handler and then zeroes the unit record and path plan. The installed Extender's `KillUnit` instead sets health to 1 and calls melee damage with maximum damage; the dead Lord can remain in its slot through the next checksum. `GamePlayerManagerAPI.SetSelectedChimps(empty)` queues a two-phase local input gesture and is not a synchronous replacement for the selection-field correction inside the common Surrender Chore.

Implementation rule: after the existing synchronized Lord kill, revalidate unit slot/global identity, clear an observed selection flag for the surrendering player and decrement a positive selection count once. Treat zero counts and unexpected selectors as anomalies, never underflow or guess another player's count. A local queued HUD deselection may follow, but checksum correctness must already hold before that deferred gesture. Test selected and unselected Lords, both surrendering peers, a normal enemy kill, repeated Surrenders, and the next 200-tick checksum boundary.

title: Tannery building animation transparency [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

# Tannery building animation transparency [Scope: Vanilla + mod integration]

This audit applies to installed `CrusaderDE.dll` SHA-256
`FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2`.

- The building simulation loop at RVA `0xC60F0` uses 1-based building game IDs,
  manager RVA `0x64CCBB0` (VA `0x1864CCBB0`), record stride `0x32C`, and
  the building type at record offset `0x12E`. Native fields are addressed as
  `manager + buildingId * 0x32C + offset`, with no additional `0x5C` in this
  manager-relative formula. The alive field is at `+0x12C`.
  Dispatch table VA `0x1802DEAE0`, type 16, points to the tannery updater
  at RVA `0xB10D0`. This updater has no explicit arguments and reads the
  current building ID from RVA `0x8F9BE4`.
- The updater writes the animation phase at offset `0x174`, frame at `0x7C`,
  image at `0x78`, and transparency at `0x11A`. Phase 0, frame 0 sets
  transparency to 31. Later phase-0 frames decrement a positive value;
  phases 1 through 5 can leave the value at 30. Phase 6 writes the frame
  index as transparency, beginning Vanillas subsequent fade. The updater
  clamps native transparency to the range 0..31 before return.
- The simulation call at RVA `0xCDE60` invokes `0xC60F0` behind its tick and
  pause checks (`0x7E50` and `0x7EA0`). Counting tannery updater calls therefore
  follows unpaused simulation progress, including changes in game speed.
- The native building render path at RVA `0x488B0` reads offset `0x11A` and
  passes it to the animation packet writer at RVA `0x19D110`. For building
  packets (`kind=4`), that writer composes the object ID as
  `animationLayer * 4000 + buildingId` and writes its twelfth argument as
  packet transparency; the managed `GameMap.addUpdateBuildingAnim` path uses
  that value for the sprite. The observed test log showed raw 31 (3.125%)
  for about 803 ms, raw 30 (6.25%) for about 9147 ms, and raw 0 at the next
  native section.
- The first testmod hooked the updater at RVA `0xB10D0`. Its detour installed
  successfully, but the live test produced no fade-start marker. The exact
  failing subcondition of its phase/frame/image/raw start filter was not
  observed, so the filter is not a validated runtime contract.
- The packet writer prologue begins
  `4C 8B DC 53 55 57 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 60`.
  Its first six bytes are complete instructions. The Ghidra reference export
  has 131 incoming calls to the function entry and no incoming edge to an
  interior byte of that six-byte span. The revised testmod accepts only
  RedBird NativeX64's six-byte `Indirect` detour and checks the live pointer
  slot and hook entry; other schemes fail closed.

The first working packet-writer revision changed only the transparency argument passed to
the native packet writer during the initial tannery animation. It retains the
original native building state and all other packet arguments. Fade progress
comes from the Script Extender's `OnTick` event, which the installed publisher
emits only while unpaused; callback count, rather than the event's game-tick
value, avoids an apparent jump when a paused clock advances internally.

For the next testmod revision, the installed DLL hash was rechecked. The
type-16 entry at VA `0x1802DEB60` in the building dispatcher table points to
`0x1800B10D0`; the `0xC60F0` loop calls it once for each active tannery on
each building simulation pass after `0xCDE60`'s pause/tick gates. The updater
entry bytes are `40 53 55 41 54 41 57`, three complete pushes covering
seven bytes. The Ghidra reference export has table references to its entry
and no incoming edge to an interior byte of this span. The installed NativeX64
backend must produce an `Indirect` detour with seven displaced bytes.

The direct-field revision restores the preceding Vanilla transparency before
each updater call, invokes the full updater once, then writes the visible
transparency to record offset `0x11A` only while phase `0..5` and initial
images are active. The updater's phase-0 branch reads/decrements this same
field, so the restoration preserves that input; phase 6 overwrites it with
Vanilla's exit fade value. Renderers `0x45820`, `0x488B0`, and `0x4C1D0` use
the field as packet transparency. Creation/removal paths also initialize the
field, but the type-16 updater is its active simulation writer. The live
packet-writer test reached 100% alpha after 30 `OnTick` callbacks in about
303 ms, so 64 actual updater calls are the new approximate 600-750 ms target.
The first native updater callback and phase/image/raw values still require a
new live test because the earlier updater detour had no unconditional marker.

The 2026-09-24 test with the direct-field revision installed the seven-byte
updater detour and logged its first callback for building ID 181, but reported
`eligible=False` and no fade-start marker. The managed renderer still showed
raw 31 and 30. Source review found a transcription error: the testmod used
manager RVA `0x64CBB0`, whereas the installed native DLL, this baseline's
building loop, and other building audits use `0x64CCBB0`. The wrong pointer
made the type/alive gate reject the real tannery before fade logic ran. The
corrected address was verified in the following live test.

The subsequent 2026-09-24 game run logged `eligible=True`, building type 16,
alive state 2, phase 0, image 12, and Vanilla raw transparency 31 on the first
updater callback for building 181. It reached effective raw 0 after 64 updater
calls; another tannery, building 364, completed the same fade in 710 ms. The
first fade took 1084 ms wall time and included a startup delay, so wall time
is not an invariant of the callback-count contract. No tannery callback error
was logged. The user confirmed that the animation is visible in-game.

The same run exposed a one-frame transition artifact in building 181: the
rendered alpha went from 1.0 (raw 0) to 0.0625 (raw 30) for approximately
10 ms, then back to 1.0 (raw 0) before Vanilla's descending fade. In native
updater `0xB10D0`, the phase-5 completion branch changes the phase to 6 but
does not overwrite transparency. The next invocation's phase-6 branch writes
its frame index to transparency. Restoring Vanilla raw 30 before the final
phase-5 invocation therefore exposes that old value for one render frame.
The targeted bridge retains raw 0 only on the verified phase-5-to-6 update
after a completed 64-update fade; the following phase-6 call resumes Vanilla.
The user confirmed the bridge works in-game after the next build on 2026-09-24.
The final testmod kept the native updater detour, 64-update fade and one-frame
bridge, with only initialization, first native callback and errors logged.
